In zone 28N\n valid eastings fall around 620000 to 800000 (east of the central\n meridian); in zone 29N around 200000 to 500000 (west of it).\n Overlap is impossible in-country, so the easting alone identifies\n the zone.\n \"\"\"\n return 28 if easting > 550000 else 29\n\n\n_LATLON_TOKEN = re.compile(r\"^([+-]?\\d*\\.?\\d+)\\s*([NSEWnsew])?$\")\n\n\ndef parse_latlon(text: str) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n \"\"\"Parse \"lat, lon\" as a field crew writes it, or None if unreadable.\n\n Accepts a signed decimal pair (``8.4657, -13.2317``), hemisphere letters\n trailing (``8.4657 N, 13.2317 W``) or attached (``13.2317W``), letters\n leading (``N 8.4657, W 13.2317``), and comma, semicolon or whitespace\n separators.\n\n Every longitude in Sierra Leone is west, and a handheld GPS writes that\n as a W rather than a minus sign. Discarding the letter and taking the\n number at face value puts the site 26 degrees east of where it is -\n silently, on the wrong side of the continent - so the letter is read as\n a sign. A letter that contradicts an explicit sign (``-13.2317 E``) is\n refused rather than guessed at, and an explicit E/W on the first value\n means the pair was written longitude first.\n \"\"\"\n raw = (text or \"\").strip()\n if not raw:\n return None\n tokens = [t for t in re.split(r\"[,;\\s]+\", raw) if t]\n\n values: list[dict] = []\n pending: str | None = None # a leading N/S/E/W awaiting its number\n for token in tokens:\n if len(token) == 1 and token.upper() in (\"N\", \"S\", \"E\", \"W\"):\n letter = token.upper()\n if values and values[-1][\"letter\"] is None:\n values[-1][\"letter\"] = letter # trailing \"8.4657 N\"\n else:\n pending = letter # leading \"N 8.4657\"\n continue\n match = _LATLON_TOKEN.match(token)\n if match is None:\n return None\n values.append({\n \"value\": float(match.group(1)),\n \"letter\": match.group(2).upper() if match.group(2) else pending,\n })\n pending = None\n\n if len(values) != 2:\n return None\n\n def signed(entry: dict) -> float | None:\n value, letter = entry[\"value\"], entry[\"letter\"]\n if not math.isfinite(value):\n return None\n if letter is None:\n return value\n negative = letter in (\"S\", \"W\")\n if value < 0 and not negative:\n return None # \"-13.2317 E\" contradicts itself\n if value < 0:\n return value\n return -value if negative else value\n\n first, second = values\n if first[\"letter\"] in (\"E\", \"W\") or second[\"letter\"] in (\"N\", \"S\"):\n first, second = second, first\n lat, lon = signed(first), signed(second)\n if lat is None or lon is None:\n return None\n if abs(lat) > 90 or abs(lon) > 180:\n return None\n return lat, lon\n"}, "groundwater/hydraulics/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Pumping test analysis: aquifer parameters, safe yield and diagnostics.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .analysis import (\n CooperJacobResult,\n TheisResult,\n RecoveryResult,\n StepTestResult,\n YieldRecommendation,\n PumpingTestAnalysis,\n analyse_pumping_test,\n cooper_jacob,\n theis_fit,\n theis_recovery,\n hantush_bierschenk,\n)\nfrom .plots import (\n plot_test_overview,\n plot_cooper_jacob,\n plot_theis,\n plot_recovery,\n plot_step_test,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\n \"CooperJacobResult\",\n \"TheisResult\",\n \"RecoveryResult\",\n \"StepTestResult\",\n \"YieldRecommendation\",\n \"PumpingTestAnalysis\",\n \"analyse_pumping_test\",\n \"cooper_jacob\",\n \"theis_fit\",\n \"theis_recovery\",\n \"hantush_bierschenk\",\n \"plot_test_overview\",\n \"plot_cooper_jacob\",\n \"plot_theis\",\n \"plot_recovery\",\n \"plot_step_test\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/hydraulics/analysis.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Pumping test analysis methods.\n\nAll methods work on non-uniform time series (the sheets record 1, 2, 3\nand 5 minute spacings) and true drawdown recomputed from water level\nminus static water level. Internally time is converted to days and\ndischarge to m3/day so transmissivity comes out in m2/day.\n\nMethods\n-------\n* Cooper-Jacob straight line on drawdown against log time, with the\n u < u_max validity check and automatic late time window selection.\n* Theis type curve fitting of W(u) by least squares. In a single\n pumped well storativity is not resolvable (it trades off against the\n effective well radius), so S is reported with a reliability warning\n unless an observation well distance is given.\n* Theis recovery: residual drawdown against log(t/t').\n* Hantush-Bierschenk step test analysis: s_w/Q against Q gives the\n aquifer loss coefficient B and well loss coefficient C, well\n efficiency per step, and the drawdown-yield relationship.\n* Specific capacity, safe yield with an explicit safety factor, and a\n recommended pump installation depth.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.optimize import curve_fit\nfrom scipy.special import exp1\n\nfrom ..config import PumpingConfig\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, PumpingTest\n\nMIN_PER_DAY = 1440.0\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Result containers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass CooperJacobResult:\n transmissivity_m2_per_day: float\n slope_m_per_log_cycle: float\n intercept_t0_min: float # time where the fitted line crosses s = 0\n storativity: Optional[float] # only when an observation distance is given\n fit_window_min: tuple[float, float]\n n_points: int\n r_squared: float\n u_check: str # narrative of the validity check\n discharge_m3_per_h: float\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass TheisResult:\n transmissivity_m2_per_day: float\n storativity: float\n storativity_reliable: bool\n rmse_m: float\n discharge_m3_per_h: float\n radius_m: float\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass RecoveryResult:\n transmissivity_m2_per_day: float\n slope_m_per_log_cycle: float\n n_points: int\n r_squared: float\n discharge_m3_per_h: float\n residual_at_end_m: float\n # theory puts the line through the origin at t/t' = 1; the fitted line\n # generally does not, and the figure has to draw the line that was fitted\n intercept_m: float = 0.0\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StepTestResult:\n aquifer_loss_B: float # s = B Q + C Q^2 with Q in m3/day, s in m\n well_loss_C: float\n steps: list[dict] # per step: Q, s_end, sw/Q, efficiency %\n r_squared: float\n\n def drawdown_at(self, q_m3_per_day: float) -> float:\n return self.aquifer_loss_B * q_m3_per_day + self.well_loss_C * q_m3_per_day**2\n\n def efficiency_at(self, q_m3_per_day: float) -> float:\n s_total = self.drawdown_at(q_m3_per_day)\n if s_total <= 0:\n return 100.0\n return 100.0 * self.aquifer_loss_B * q_m3_per_day / s_total\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass YieldRecommendation:\n specific_capacity_m3hr_per_m: Optional[float]\n available_drawdown_m: Optional[float]\n usable_drawdown_m: Optional[float]\n projected_drawdown_m: Optional[float]\n long_term_yield_m3_per_h: Optional[float]\n safe_yield_m3_per_h: Optional[float]\n safety_factor: float\n design_period_days: float\n pump_installation_depth_m: Optional[float]\n basis: str # narrative of how the recommendation was derived\n pending_reason: str = \"\" # non-empty when discharge or SWL is missing\n # plausible range of the safe yield over the assumptions it rests on\n # (transmissivity, storativity, effective radius, seasonal allowance)\n safe_yield_low_m3_per_h: Optional[float] = None\n safe_yield_high_m3_per_h: Optional[float] = None\n envelope_basis: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def yield_range_text(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"\"2.4 m3/h (1.8 to 3.1)\" - never a bare number for an assumed one.\"\"\"\n if self.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n return \"pending\"\n text = f\"{self.safe_yield_m3_per_h:.2g} m3/h\"\n if (\n self.safe_yield_low_m3_per_h is not None\n and self.safe_yield_high_m3_per_h is not None\n ):\n text += (\n f\" ({self.safe_yield_low_m3_per_h:.2g} to \"\n f\"{self.safe_yield_high_m3_per_h:.2g})\"\n )\n return text\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass PumpingTestAnalysis:\n test: PumpingTest\n cooper_jacob: Optional[CooperJacobResult] = None\n theis: Optional[TheisResult] = None\n recovery: Optional[RecoveryResult] = None\n step_test: Optional[StepTestResult] = None\n yield_recommendation: Optional[YieldRecommendation] = None\n stabilised_level_m: Optional[float] = None\n max_drawdown_m: Optional[float] = None\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def transmissivity_m2_per_day(self) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"Preferred transmissivity: recovery is least affected by well\n losses, then Cooper-Jacob, then Theis.\"\"\"\n for result in (self.recovery, self.cooper_jacob, self.theis):\n if result is not None:\n return result.transmissivity_m2_per_day\n return None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Individual methods\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _line_fit(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n \"\"\"Least squares line with r^2.\"\"\"\n A = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T\n coef, res, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, y, rcond=None)\n slope, intercept = float(coef[0]), float(coef[1])\n ss_tot = float(np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2))\n ss_res = float(np.sum((y - (slope * x + intercept)) ** 2))\n r2 = 1.0 - ss_res / ss_tot if ss_tot > 0 else 1.0\n return slope, intercept, r2\n\n\ndef _require_discharge(discharge_m3_per_h) -> float:\n \"\"\"A rate of zero is not a measurement, and T is proportional to Q.\n\n A blank left as 0 on the sheet used to divide by zero deep inside the\n fit; raising here puts it on the same handled path as a missing value.\n \"\"\"\n if discharge_m3_per_h is None:\n raise ValueError(\"No discharge recorded, so transmissivity cannot be fitted\")\n q = float(discharge_m3_per_h)\n if not math.isfinite(q) or q <= 0:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"Discharge must be greater than zero to fit an aquifer parameter \"\n f\"(got {q:g} m3/h); check the discharge row on the field sheet\"\n )\n return q\n\n\ndef cooper_jacob(\n time_min: np.ndarray,\n drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n discharge_m3_per_h: float,\n config: PumpingConfig | None = None,\n fit_window_min: tuple[float, float] | None = None,\n observation_radius_m: float | None = None,\n assumed_storativity: float = 1e-3,\n) -> CooperJacobResult:\n \"\"\"Cooper-Jacob straight line analysis.\n\n With no explicit window the fit uses the last full log cycle of\n data (at least 6 points), which is where u is smallest and the\n approximation holds. The u criterion is evaluated afterwards with\n the fitted T (and an assumed S for the pumped well) and reported.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or PumpingConfig()\n _require_discharge(discharge_m3_per_h)\n t = np.asarray(time_min, dtype=float)\n s = np.asarray(drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = (t > 0) & np.isfinite(s)\n t, s = t[keep], s[keep]\n if len(t) < 4:\n raise ValueError(\"Not enough readings for a Cooper-Jacob fit\")\n\n if fit_window_min is None:\n t_end = t.max()\n t_start = max(t_end / 10.0, t.min())\n window = (t >= t_start)\n if window.sum() < 6:\n # the six latest readings. argsort gives sorting indices, not\n # ranks, so comparing it against a rank picked an arbitrary six\n # whenever the sheet's times were not already in order\n window = t >= np.sort(t)[-min(6, len(t))]\n fit_window_min = (float(t[window].min()), float(t[window].max()))\n else:\n window = (t >= fit_window_min[0]) & (t <= fit_window_min[1])\n\n slope, intercept, r2 = _line_fit(np.log10(t[window]), s[window])\n if slope <= 0:\n raise ValueError(\n \"Drawdown does not increase with log time; Cooper-Jacob does not apply\"\n )\n q_day = discharge_m3_per_h * 24.0\n T = 2.303 * q_day / (4.0 * math.pi * slope)\n t0_min = 10 ** (-intercept / slope)\n\n storativity = None\n if observation_radius_m is not None:\n t0_day = t0_min / MIN_PER_DAY\n storativity = 2.25 * T * t0_day / observation_radius_m**2\n\n # validity: u = r^2 S / (4 T t) at the start of the fit window\n r_eff = observation_radius_m if observation_radius_m else 0.1\n S_eff = storativity if storativity else assumed_storativity\n u_start = r_eff**2 * S_eff / (4.0 * T * (fit_window_min[0] / MIN_PER_DAY))\n if u_start < config.cooper_jacob_u_max:\n u_check = (\n f\"u = {u_start:.2e} at the start of the fitted window, below the \"\n f\"{config.cooper_jacob_u_max} criterion; the straight line \"\n \"approximation is valid\"\n )\n else:\n u_check = (\n f\"u = {u_start:.2e} at the start of the fitted window exceeds \"\n f\"{config.cooper_jacob_u_max}; early data were excluded or results \"\n \"should be treated with caution\"\n )\n\n return CooperJacobResult(\n transmissivity_m2_per_day=T,\n slope_m_per_log_cycle=slope,\n intercept_t0_min=t0_min,\n storativity=storativity,\n fit_window_min=fit_window_min,\n n_points=int(window.sum()),\n r_squared=r2,\n u_check=u_check,\n discharge_m3_per_h=discharge_m3_per_h,\n )\n\n\ndef theis_fit(\n time_min: np.ndarray,\n drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n discharge_m3_per_h: float,\n radius_m: float = 0.1,\n observation_well: bool = False,\n) -> TheisResult:\n \"\"\"Least squares fit of the Theis well function.\n\n ``s = Q / (4 pi T) W(u)``, ``u = r^2 S / (4 T t)``. Fitting is done\n in log parameter space to keep T and S positive.\n \"\"\"\n _require_discharge(discharge_m3_per_h)\n t = np.asarray(time_min, dtype=float) / MIN_PER_DAY\n s = np.asarray(drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = (t > 0) & (s > 0)\n t, s = t[keep], s[keep]\n if len(t) < 5:\n raise ValueError(\"Not enough readings for a Theis fit\")\n q_day = discharge_m3_per_h * 24.0\n\n def model(tt, logT, logS):\n T = 10.0**logT\n S = 10.0**logS\n u = radius_m**2 * S / (4.0 * T * tt)\n return q_day / (4.0 * math.pi * T) * exp1(u)\n\n # start from a Cooper-Jacob style estimate\n slope0 = max((s[-1] - s[len(s) // 2]) / max(np.log10(t[-1] / t[len(s) // 2]), 0.3), 0.1)\n T0 = 2.303 * q_day / (4.0 * math.pi * slope0)\n p0 = (math.log10(max(T0, 1e-2)), -3.0)\n popt, _ = curve_fit(model, t, s, p0=p0, maxfev=20000)\n T = 10.0 ** popt[0]\n S = 10.0 ** popt[1]\n rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((model(t, *popt) - s) ** 2)))\n return TheisResult(\n transmissivity_m2_per_day=T,\n storativity=S,\n storativity_reliable=bool(observation_well),\n rmse_m=rmse,\n discharge_m3_per_h=discharge_m3_per_h,\n radius_m=radius_m,\n )\n\n\ndef theis_recovery(\n recovery_time_min: np.ndarray,\n residual_drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n pumping_duration_min: float,\n discharge_m3_per_h: float,\n) -> RecoveryResult:\n \"\"\"Theis recovery analysis on residual drawdown against t/t'.\n\n ``s' = 2.303 Q / (4 pi T) log10(t/t')`` with t measured since\n pumping started and t' since it stopped.\n \"\"\"\n _require_discharge(discharge_m3_per_h)\n tp = np.asarray(recovery_time_min, dtype=float) # t'\n sp = np.asarray(residual_drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = (tp > 0) & np.isfinite(sp)\n tp, sp = tp[keep], sp[keep]\n if len(tp) < 4:\n raise ValueError(\"Not enough recovery readings\")\n ratio = (pumping_duration_min + tp) / tp\n slope, intercept, r2 = _line_fit(np.log10(ratio), sp)\n if slope <= 0:\n raise ValueError(\"Residual drawdown does not decrease; check the data\")\n q_day = discharge_m3_per_h * 24.0\n T = 2.303 * q_day / (4.0 * math.pi * slope)\n return RecoveryResult(\n transmissivity_m2_per_day=T,\n slope_m_per_log_cycle=slope,\n n_points=len(tp),\n r_squared=r2,\n discharge_m3_per_h=discharge_m3_per_h,\n residual_at_end_m=float(sp[-1]),\n intercept_m=float(intercept),\n )\n\n\ndef hantush_bierschenk(\n step_discharges_m3_per_h: list[float],\n step_end_drawdowns_m: list[float],\n) -> StepTestResult:\n \"\"\"Hantush-Bierschenk analysis of a step drawdown test.\n\n Fits ``s_w = B Q + C Q^2`` through the end-of-step drawdowns by\n linear regression of s_w/Q on Q. Q is converted to m3/day, so B is\n in day/m2 and C in day2/m5.\n \"\"\"\n q = np.asarray(step_discharges_m3_per_h, dtype=float) * 24.0\n s = np.asarray(step_end_drawdowns_m, dtype=float)\n if len(q) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\"A step test needs at least two steps with discharge\")\n sq = s / q\n C, B, r2 = _line_fit(q, sq)\n if C < 0:\n # negative well loss has no physical meaning; fall back to pure\n # aquifer loss\n C = 0.0\n B = float(np.mean(sq))\n if B < 0:\n # Neither has a negative aquifer loss: it made the reported well\n # efficiency negative (100 B Q / (B Q + C Q^2) with B < 0), which went\n # into the report as the borehole's efficiency. Refit through the\n # origin as pure well loss - least squares of s/Q = C Q with B = 0.\n B = 0.0\n C = float(np.sum(s) / np.sum(q**2))\n fitted = C * q\n ss_tot = float(np.sum((sq - sq.mean()) ** 2))\n r2 = 1.0 - float(np.sum((sq - fitted) ** 2)) / ss_tot if ss_tot > 0 else 1.0\n steps = []\n for i, (qi, si) in enumerate(zip(q, s), start=1):\n eff = 100.0 * B * qi / (B * qi + C * qi**2) if (B * qi + C * qi**2) > 0 else 100.0\n steps.append(\n {\n \"step\": i,\n \"discharge_m3_per_h\": qi / 24.0,\n \"drawdown_end_m\": float(si),\n \"sw_over_q_day_per_m2\": float(si / qi),\n \"efficiency_percent\": float(eff),\n }\n )\n return StepTestResult(aquifer_loss_B=float(B), well_loss_C=float(C), steps=steps, r_squared=r2)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Yield recommendation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef recommend_yield(\n test: PumpingTest,\n transmissivity: Optional[float],\n step_result: Optional[StepTestResult],\n config: PumpingConfig | None = None,\n assumed_storativity: float = 1e-3,\n effective_radius_m: float = 0.1,\n) -> YieldRecommendation:\n \"\"\"Specific capacity, sustainable yield and pump depth.\n\n The long term yield solves ``s_proj(Q) = f_avail x s_available``\n where ``s_proj`` projects Cooper-Jacob drawdown to the design\n period with the fitted T (plus well losses when a step test is\n available). The stated safety factor is then applied. Every input\n is recorded in ``basis`` so the recommendation is traceable.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or PumpingConfig()\n swl = test.static_water_level_m\n\n # observed end-of-test state\n q_last = None\n s_end = None\n if test.steps:\n last = test.steps[-1]\n q_last = last.discharge_m3_per_h\n if swl is not None:\n s_end = float(last.water_level_m[-1] - swl)\n\n specific_capacity = None\n if q_last and s_end and s_end > 0:\n specific_capacity = q_last / s_end\n\n # available drawdown: static level to pump intake less a submergence margin\n available = None\n if swl is not None and test.pump_setting_m is not None:\n available = test.pump_setting_m - swl - config.pump_submergence_min_m\n elif swl is not None and test.borehole_depth_m is not None:\n available = test.borehole_depth_m - swl - config.pump_submergence_min_m - 3.0\n\n # Reserve the dry-season water-table decline before taking the usable\n # fraction. A test run in the rains sits on a higher static level than\n # the borehole will see at the end of the dry season, so the raw\n # available drawdown would over-state the sustainable yield.\n # seasonal_allowance_m is the expected wet-to-dry decline (configurable\n # per district); it is already applied to the pump-setting depth below.\n usable = (\n max(available - config.seasonal_allowance_m, 0.0)\n * config.available_drawdown_fraction\n if available\n else None\n )\n\n if transmissivity is None or swl is None:\n # name what is actually missing: blaming the discharge when it was\n # recorded and the fit simply failed sends the crew back to the field\n # for a number that is already on the sheet\n missing = []\n if swl is None:\n missing.append(\"static water level is missing\")\n if transmissivity is None:\n missing.append(\n \"discharge is missing on the field sheet\"\n if not any(s.discharge_m3_per_h for s in test.steps)\n else \"transmissivity could not be fitted from the readings\"\n )\n reason = \" and \".join(missing)\n return YieldRecommendation(\n specific_capacity_m3hr_per_m=specific_capacity,\n available_drawdown_m=available,\n usable_drawdown_m=usable,\n projected_drawdown_m=None,\n long_term_yield_m3_per_h=None,\n safe_yield_m3_per_h=None,\n safety_factor=config.safety_factor,\n design_period_days=config.design_period_days,\n pump_installation_depth_m=None,\n basis=\"Yield recommendation pending: \" + reason + \".\",\n pending_reason=reason,\n )\n\n t_design = config.design_period_days\n log_term = math.log10(\n 2.25 * transmissivity * t_design / (effective_radius_m**2 * assumed_storativity)\n )\n\n def projected_drawdown(q_m3_per_h: float) -> float:\n q_day = q_m3_per_h * 24.0\n s = 2.303 * q_day / (4.0 * math.pi * transmissivity) * log_term\n if step_result is not None:\n # B Q + C Q^2 reflects drawdown at the step duration; add the\n # Cooper-Jacob time projection from step length to design period\n t_step_min = test.step_length_min or test.pumping_duration_min or 180.0\n s = step_result.drawdown_at(q_day)\n s += (\n 2.303\n * q_day\n / (4.0 * math.pi * transmissivity)\n * math.log10(t_design / (t_step_min / MIN_PER_DAY))\n )\n return s\n\n long_term = None\n if usable and usable > 0:\n # bisect Q so projected drawdown equals the usable drawdown\n q_lo, q_hi = 0.01, 200.0\n for _ in range(80):\n q_mid = 0.5 * (q_lo + q_hi)\n if projected_drawdown(q_mid) > usable:\n q_hi = q_mid\n else:\n q_lo = q_mid\n long_term = q_lo\n\n safe = long_term / config.safety_factor if long_term else None\n\n pump_depth = None\n if safe is not None:\n s_at_safe = projected_drawdown(safe)\n pump_depth = swl + s_at_safe + config.seasonal_allowance_m + config.pump_submergence_min_m\n if test.borehole_depth_m:\n pump_depth = min(pump_depth, test.borehole_depth_m - 3.0)\n pump_depth = math.ceil(pump_depth)\n\n basis = (\n f\"Transmissivity {transmissivity:.1f} m2/day; drawdown projected to \"\n f\"{t_design:.0f} days with storativity assumed {assumed_storativity:g} and \"\n f\"effective radius {effective_radius_m} m; usable drawdown taken as \"\n f\"{config.available_drawdown_fraction:.0%} of the available drawdown\"\n + (\n f\" {available:.1f} m (static level to pump intake less \"\n f\"{config.pump_submergence_min_m:.0f} m submergence), after \"\n f\"reserving a {config.seasonal_allowance_m:.0f} m dry-season \"\n \"water-table decline\"\n if available\n else \"\"\n )\n + (\n \"; well losses from the step test are included\"\n if step_result is not None\n else \"\"\n )\n + f\". A safety factor of {config.safety_factor} is applied to the long \"\n \"term yield.\"\n )\n return YieldRecommendation(\n specific_capacity_m3hr_per_m=specific_capacity,\n available_drawdown_m=available,\n usable_drawdown_m=usable,\n projected_drawdown_m=projected_drawdown(safe) if safe else None,\n long_term_yield_m3_per_h=long_term,\n safe_yield_m3_per_h=safe,\n safety_factor=config.safety_factor,\n design_period_days=t_design,\n pump_installation_depth_m=pump_depth,\n basis=basis,\n )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Orchestration\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\n# storativity is never resolvable from a single pumped well, the effective\n# radius depends on the gravel pack and development, and the wet-to-dry\n# decline is a regional rule of thumb. The safe yield is proportional to\n# none of them individually but sensitive to all of them, so the honest\n# output is a band. Ranges follow common basement-aquifer practice.\n_ENVELOPE_STORATIVITY = (1e-4, 1e-2)\n_ENVELOPE_RADIUS_M = (0.075, 0.15)\n_ENVELOPE_SEASONAL_M = (1.0, 4.0)\n\n\ndef attach_yield_envelope(\n analysis: \"PumpingTestAnalysis\", config: PumpingConfig | None = None\n) -> None:\n \"\"\"Fill the safe-yield band on ``analysis.yield_recommendation``.\n\n Re-runs the same recommendation over the corners of the assumption\n envelope - transmissivity across whichever methods actually fitted,\n storativity, effective well radius and the seasonal allowance - and keeps\n the lowest and highest safe yields. Reported as \"2.4 m3/h (1.8 to 3.1)\",\n so nobody reads an assumed number as a measured one.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or PumpingConfig()\n recommendation = analysis.yield_recommendation\n if recommendation is None or recommendation.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n return\n\n fitted = [\n r.transmissivity_m2_per_day\n for r in (analysis.recovery, analysis.cooper_jacob, analysis.theis)\n if r is not None and r.transmissivity_m2_per_day\n ]\n if not fitted:\n return\n # when only one method fitted there is no spread to measure, so allow the\n # factor of two that separates methods on a typical basement borehole\n t_range = (min(fitted), max(fitted)) if len(fitted) > 1 else (\n fitted[0] / 1.5, fitted[0] * 1.5\n )\n\n yields = []\n for transmissivity in t_range:\n for storativity in _ENVELOPE_STORATIVITY:\n for radius in _ENVELOPE_RADIUS_M:\n for seasonal in _ENVELOPE_SEASONAL_M:\n variant = replace(config, seasonal_allowance_m=seasonal)\n trial = recommend_yield(\n analysis.test,\n transmissivity,\n analysis.step_test,\n variant,\n assumed_storativity=storativity,\n effective_radius_m=radius,\n )\n if trial.safe_yield_m3_per_h:\n yields.append(trial.safe_yield_m3_per_h)\n if not yields:\n return\n recommendation.safe_yield_low_m3_per_h = min(yields)\n recommendation.safe_yield_high_m3_per_h = max(yields)\n recommendation.envelope_basis = (\n f\"Range over transmissivity {t_range[0]:.1f}-{t_range[1]:.1f} m2/day\"\n f\"{' (spread between the fitted methods)' if len(fitted) > 1 else ''}, \"\n f\"storativity {_ENVELOPE_STORATIVITY[0]:g}-{_ENVELOPE_STORATIVITY[1]:g}, \"\n f\"effective radius {_ENVELOPE_RADIUS_M[0]}-{_ENVELOPE_RADIUS_M[1]} m and \"\n f\"a dry-season decline of {_ENVELOPE_SEASONAL_M[0]:.0f}-\"\n f\"{_ENVELOPE_SEASONAL_M[1]:.0f} m. Design to the lower figure where the \"\n \"supply must not fail in a dry year.\"\n )\n\n\ndef analyse_pumping_test(\n test: PumpingTest,\n config: PumpingConfig | None = None,\n observation_radius_m: float | None = None,\n) -> PumpingTestAnalysis:\n \"\"\"Run every applicable analysis on a parsed pumping test.\n\n Methods that need missing inputs (discharge, static level) are\n skipped with a flag instead of failing, so partially filled sheets\n still produce curves and a report skeleton.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or PumpingConfig()\n analysis = PumpingTestAnalysis(test=test)\n # drop parse-time discharge flags that the analyst has since resolved\n flags = [\n f\n for f in test.flags\n if not (\n f.code in (\"missing_discharge\", \"discharge_ambiguous\")\n and all(s.discharge_m3_per_h is not None for s in test.steps)\n )\n ]\n # A zero or negative rate is a blank the crew wrote a 0 into, not a\n # measurement. Treat it as missing so the pending narrative and the\n # step-test guards below are right, rather than carrying it into a fit.\n for step in test.steps:\n q = step.discharge_m3_per_h\n if q is not None and not (float(q) > 0 and math.isfinite(float(q))):\n step.discharge_m3_per_h = None\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"invalid_discharge\",\n f\"Discharge recorded as {float(q):g} m3/h, which cannot be \"\n \"a pumping rate; treated as not measured. Enter the \"\n \"bucket-and-stopwatch value to get transmissivity and yield.\",\n context=step.label or f\"step {step.step_number}\",\n )\n )\n\n swl = test.static_water_level_m\n\n if test.steps and swl is not None:\n last = test.steps[-1]\n analysis.max_drawdown_m = float(np.nanmax(last.water_level_m) - swl)\n tail = last.water_level_m[-3:]\n if len(tail) >= 2 and (np.max(tail) - np.min(tail)) <= 0.05:\n analysis.stabilised_level_m = float(np.mean(tail))\n\n # ---- Cooper-Jacob and Theis on the first step -----------------------------\n # The first step pumps at a single rate from static conditions, so the\n # single well solutions apply directly (later steps would need\n # superposition of the earlier rates).\n if swl is not None and test.steps:\n step = test.steps[0]\n q = step.discharge_m3_per_h\n if q is not None:\n t = np.where(step.time_min <= 0, np.nan, step.time_min)\n s = test.drawdown(step)\n keep = np.isfinite(t) & np.isfinite(s)\n try:\n analysis.cooper_jacob = cooper_jacob(\n t[keep], s[keep], q, config,\n observation_radius_m=observation_radius_m,\n )\n except ValueError as exc:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\"warning\", \"cooper_jacob_failed\", str(exc)))\n try:\n analysis.theis = theis_fit(\n t[keep], s[keep], q,\n observation_well=observation_radius_m is not None,\n radius_m=observation_radius_m or 0.1,\n )\n except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\"warning\", \"theis_failed\", str(exc)))\n\n # ---- recovery -----------------------------------------------------------\n residual = test.residual_drawdown()\n if residual is not None and test.recovery_time_min is not None:\n q_rec = None\n for step in reversed(test.steps):\n if step.discharge_m3_per_h is not None:\n q_rec = step.discharge_m3_per_h\n break\n if q_rec is not None and test.pumping_duration_min:\n try:\n analysis.recovery = theis_recovery(\n test.recovery_time_min, residual, test.pumping_duration_min, q_rec\n )\n except ValueError as exc:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\"warning\", \"recovery_failed\", str(exc)))\n\n # ---- step test ----------------------------------------------------------\n if test.test_type.startswith(\"step\") and swl is not None and len(test.steps) >= 2:\n with_q = [s for s in test.steps if s.discharge_m3_per_h is not None]\n if len(with_q) >= 2:\n try:\n analysis.step_test = hantush_bierschenk(\n [s.discharge_m3_per_h for s in with_q],\n [float(s.water_level_m[-1] - swl) for s in with_q],\n )\n except ValueError as exc:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\"warning\", \"step_test_failed\", str(exc)))\n else:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"step_test_pending\",\n \"Step test analysis pending: discharge per step is missing.\",\n )\n )\n\n # ---- yield ---------------------------------------------------------------\n analysis.yield_recommendation = recommend_yield(\n test,\n analysis.transmissivity_m2_per_day,\n analysis.step_test,\n config,\n )\n attach_yield_envelope(analysis, config)\n\n analysis.flags = flags\n return analysis\n"}, "groundwater/hydraulics/plots.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Pumping test diagnostic plots.\n\nAll plots work from the parsed test (true drawdown recomputed from\nstatic water level) and accept the analysis results for fitted line\noverlays. Missing discharge does not block the water level and\ndrawdown curves.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import PumpingTest\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom .analysis import (\n CooperJacobResult,\n RecoveryResult,\n StepTestResult,\n TheisResult,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\n \"plot_test_overview\",\n \"plot_cooper_jacob\",\n \"plot_theis\",\n \"plot_recovery\",\n \"plot_step_test\",\n]\n\n\ndef plot_test_overview(\n test: PumpingTest,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Water level against time for the whole test including recovery.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 3.2))\n t_end = 0.0\n for step in test.steps:\n label = step.label if len(test.steps) > 1 else \"pumping phase\"\n ax.plot(step.time_min, step.water_level_m, \"-o\", ms=3,\n color=style.accent_color, lw=1.2,\n label=label if step.step_number in (1,) else None)\n t_end = max(t_end, float(step.time_min.max()))\n if test.recovery_time_min is not None:\n ax.plot(test.recovery_time_min + t_end, test.recovery_level_m, \"-s\",\n ms=3, color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.2, label=\"recovery\")\n if test.static_water_level_m is not None:\n ax.axhline(test.static_water_level_m, color=\"#666666\", lw=1.0, ls=\"--\",\n label=f\"static water level {test.static_water_level_m:.2f} m\")\n if test.pump_setting_m:\n ax.axhline(test.pump_setting_m, color=\"#999999\", lw=1.0, ls=\":\",\n label=f\"pump setting {test.pump_setting_m:.0f} m\")\n ax.invert_yaxis()\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time since pumping started (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Water level (m below datum)\")\n title = \"Pumping test overview\"\n if test.site.community:\n title += f\" - {test.site.community}\"\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_cooper_jacob(\n time_min: np.ndarray,\n drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n result: CooperJacobResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Cooper-Jacob straight line analysis\",\n):\n \"\"\"Semi-log drawdown against time with the fitted straight line.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n t = np.asarray(time_min, dtype=float)\n s = np.asarray(drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = t > 0\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax.semilogx(t[keep], s[keep], \"o\", ms=4, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.2, label=\"drawdown\")\n if result is not None:\n t_line = np.geomspace(max(result.intercept_t0_min, t[keep].min() / 3), t[keep].max() * 1.3, 50)\n s_line = result.slope_m_per_log_cycle * np.log10(t_line / result.intercept_t0_min)\n ax.semilogx(t_line, s_line, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=(\n f\"fit: {result.slope_m_per_log_cycle:.2f} m/log cycle, \"\n f\"T = {result.transmissivity_m2_per_day:.1f} m2/day\"\n ))\n ax.axvspan(*result.fit_window_min, color=style.accent_color, alpha=0.08,\n label=\"fitted window\")\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Drawdown (m)\")\n ax.invert_yaxis()\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_theis(\n time_min: np.ndarray,\n drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n result: TheisResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Theis curve fit\",\n):\n \"\"\"Log-log drawdown against time with the fitted Theis curve.\"\"\"\n from scipy.special import exp1\n\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n t = np.asarray(time_min, dtype=float)\n s = np.asarray(drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = (t > 0) & (s > 0)\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax.loglog(t[keep], s[keep], \"o\", ms=4, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.2, label=\"drawdown\")\n if result is not None:\n t_line = np.geomspace(t[keep].min(), t[keep].max(), 80)\n t_day = t_line / 1440.0\n q_day = result.discharge_m3_per_h * 24.0\n u = result.radius_m**2 * result.storativity / (\n 4.0 * result.transmissivity_m2_per_day * t_day\n )\n s_line = q_day / (4.0 * np.pi * result.transmissivity_m2_per_day) * exp1(u)\n label = (\n f\"Theis fit: T = {result.transmissivity_m2_per_day:.1f} m2/day, \"\n f\"S = {result.storativity:.1e}\"\n )\n if not result.storativity_reliable:\n label += \" (S indicative)\"\n ax.loglog(t_line, s_line, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8, label=label)\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Drawdown (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_recovery(\n recovery_time_min: np.ndarray,\n residual_drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n pumping_duration_min: float,\n result: RecoveryResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Theis recovery analysis\",\n):\n \"\"\"Residual drawdown against t/t' on a semi-log axis.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n tp = np.asarray(recovery_time_min, dtype=float)\n sp = np.asarray(residual_drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = tp > 0\n ratio = (pumping_duration_min + tp[keep]) / tp[keep]\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax.semilogx(ratio, sp[keep], \"o\", ms=4, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.2, label=\"residual drawdown\")\n if result is not None:\n r_line = np.geomspace(1.001, ratio.max() * 1.2, 50)\n # the line that was actually fitted, intercept included: forcing\n # it through the origin drew a line beside the data it claims to fit\n s_line = (\n result.slope_m_per_log_cycle * np.log10(r_line)\n + result.intercept_m\n )\n ax.semilogx(r_line, s_line, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=(\n f\"fit: {result.slope_m_per_log_cycle:.2f} m/log cycle, \"\n f\"T = {result.transmissivity_m2_per_day:.1f} m2/day\"\n ))\n ax.set_xlabel(\"t / t'\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Residual drawdown (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_step_test(\n test: PumpingTest,\n result: StepTestResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Step test figure: drawdown per step, plus the Hantush-Bierschenk\n sw/Q against Q fit when discharges are available.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n swl = test.static_water_level_m\n with figure_context(style):\n if result is not None:\n fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 3.2))\n else:\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax2 = None\n for step in test.steps:\n s = step.water_level_m - swl if swl is not None else step.water_level_m\n q_note = (\n f\", Q = {step.discharge_m3_per_h:.1f} m3/h\"\n if step.discharge_m3_per_h is not None\n else \", Q pending\"\n )\n ax.plot(step.time_min, s, \"-o\", ms=3, lw=1.2, label=f\"{step.label}{q_note}\")\n ax.invert_yaxis()\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time since test start (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Drawdown below static (m)\" if swl is not None else \"Water level (m)\")\n ax.set_title(\"Step drawdown test\")\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\", fontsize=8)\n\n if ax2 is not None and result is not None:\n q = np.array([s[\"discharge_m3_per_h\"] for s in result.steps]) * 24.0\n sq = np.array([s[\"sw_over_q_day_per_m2\"] for s in result.steps])\n ax2.plot(q, sq, \"o\", ms=5, mfc=\"white\", mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.4,\n label=\"observed\")\n q_line = np.linspace(0, q.max() * 1.15, 40)\n ax2.plot(q_line, result.aquifer_loss_B + result.well_loss_C * q_line, \"-\",\n color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=(\n f\"B = {result.aquifer_loss_B:.2e} day/m2\\n\"\n f\"C = {result.well_loss_C:.2e} day2/m5\"\n ))\n ax2.set_xlabel(\"Discharge Q (m3/day)\")\n ax2.set_ylabel(\"s_w / Q (day/m2)\")\n ax2.set_title(\"Hantush-Bierschenk\")\n ax2.legend(loc=\"best\", fontsize=8)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Data ingestion: standard templates, parsers and consistency checks.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .templates import write_all_templates\nfrom .ves import read_ves_workbook, read_ves_csv\nfrom .pumping import read_pumping_workbook, read_pumping_docx\nfrom .drilling import read_drilling_workbook\nfrom .waterquality import read_quality_workbook\nfrom .checks import check_site_consistency, check_all\n\n__all__ = [\n \"write_all_templates\",\n \"read_ves_workbook\",\n \"read_ves_csv\",\n \"read_pumping_workbook\",\n \"read_pumping_docx\",\n \"read_drilling_workbook\",\n \"read_quality_workbook\",\n \"check_site_consistency\",\n \"check_all\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/checks.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Metadata consistency checks.\n\nField sheets are often filled by copying the previous sheet, so wrong\ndistricts, communities and coordinates slip through (the Rokel survey\nreport states \"Port Loko\" for a sounding whose coordinates fall in the\nWestern Area). These checks flag such conflicts before they reach a\nreport.\n\nDistrict extents are approximate bounding boxes bundled with the\npackage (``data/sl_districts.csv``); they are meant to catch gross\ncopy-over errors, not to adjudicate points near district boundaries.\nA configurable buffer keeps borderline points from being flagged.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom typing import Iterable\n\nfrom ..geo import infer_zone_for_sierra_leone, utm_distance_m, utm_to_geographic\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, SiteMetadata\n\n_BUFFER_DEG = 0.05 # about 5.5 km; boundary points are not flagged\n\n# Sierra Leone in geographic coordinates, generous margin\n_SL_BOUNDS = (-13.6, -10.0, 6.7, 10.2) # lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max\n\n\ndef _fmt_latlon(lat: float, lon: float) -> str:\n \"\"\"Human-readable coordinates with correct hemisphere letters.\n\n Sierra Leone is in the western hemisphere, so longitudes are negative and\n must read 'W', not 'E'.\n \"\"\"\n ns = \"N\" if lat >= 0 else \"S\"\n ew = \"E\" if lon >= 0 else \"W\"\n return f\"{abs(lat):.4f} {ns}, {abs(lon):.4f} {ew}\"\n\n\ndef _load_districts() -> dict[str, dict]:\n with resources.files(\"groundwater.data\").joinpath(\"sl_districts.csv\").open(\n \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\"\n ) as fh:\n rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))\n return {\n row[\"district\"].strip().lower(): {\n \"district\": row[\"district\"],\n \"province\": row[\"province\"],\n \"lon_min\": float(row[\"lon_min\"]),\n \"lon_max\": float(row[\"lon_max\"]),\n \"lat_min\": float(row[\"lat_min\"]),\n \"lat_max\": float(row[\"lat_max\"]),\n }\n for row in rows\n }\n\n\n_DISTRICTS = None\n\n\ndef districts() -> dict[str, dict]:\n global _DISTRICTS\n if _DISTRICTS is None:\n _DISTRICTS = _load_districts()\n return _DISTRICTS\n\n\ndef _normalise_district(name: str) -> str | None:\n \"\"\"Map a stated district name onto the lookup table.\"\"\"\n key = name.strip().lower()\n if not key:\n return None\n table = districts()\n if key in table:\n return key\n # \"Western Area\" without urban/rural, \"Western Urban\", abbreviations\n candidates = [k for k in table if key in k or k in key]\n if candidates:\n return candidates[0]\n if \"western\" in key:\n return \"western area rural\"\n return None\n\n\ndef districts_containing(lat: float, lon: float, buffer_deg: float = _BUFFER_DEG) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Districts whose (approximate) box contains the point.\"\"\"\n hits = []\n for key, box in districts().items():\n if (\n box[\"lon_min\"] - buffer_deg <= lon <= box[\"lon_max\"] + buffer_deg\n and box[\"lat_min\"] - buffer_deg <= lat <= box[\"lat_max\"] + buffer_deg\n ):\n hits.append(box[\"district\"])\n return hits\n\n\ndef check_site_consistency(site: SiteMetadata, context: str = \"\") -> list[DataFlag]:\n \"\"\"Check one site record: coordinates against country, zone and district.\"\"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n ctx = context or site.community or \"\"\n\n if site.easting is None or site.northing is None:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\"info\", \"missing_coordinates\", \"No GPS coordinates recorded.\", ctx)\n )\n return flags\n\n zone = site.utm_zone\n if zone is None:\n zone = infer_zone_for_sierra_leone(site.easting)\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"utm_zone_assumed\",\n f\"UTM zone not recorded; assumed {zone}N from the easting.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n lat, lon = utm_to_geographic(site.easting, site.northing, zone)\n\n lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max = _SL_BOUNDS\n if not (lon_min <= lon <= lon_max and lat_min <= lat <= lat_max):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"coordinates_outside_country\",\n f\"Coordinates convert to {_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)} which is outside \"\n \"Sierra Leone; check easting/northing and the UTM zone.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n return flags\n\n stated = _normalise_district(site.district)\n if site.district and stated is None:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"unknown_district\",\n f\"District '{site.district}' is not a recognised Sierra Leone \"\n \"district name.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n elif stated is not None:\n box = districts()[stated]\n inside = (\n box[\"lon_min\"] - _BUFFER_DEG <= lon <= box[\"lon_max\"] + _BUFFER_DEG\n and box[\"lat_min\"] - _BUFFER_DEG <= lat <= box[\"lat_max\"] + _BUFFER_DEG\n )\n if not inside:\n likely = districts_containing(lat, lon)\n hint = f\" The point falls in {', '.join(likely)}.\" if likely else \"\"\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"district_coordinate_conflict\",\n f\"Stated district '{site.district}' does not contain the \"\n f\"coordinates ({_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)}).{hint} District \"\n \"extents are approximate; verify against the field notes.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n return flags\n\n\ndef check_group_consistency(\n sites: Iterable[tuple[str, SiteMetadata]], max_separation_km: float = 5.0\n) -> list[DataFlag]:\n \"\"\"Cross-record checks for one survey or project.\n\n Flags differing client/community/district values between sheets of\n the same project and points unexpectedly far apart.\n \"\"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n records = list(sites)\n if len(records) < 2:\n return flags\n\n for field in (\"client\", \"community\", \"district\"):\n values = {}\n for label, site in records:\n value = getattr(site, field).strip()\n if value:\n values.setdefault(value.lower(), (value, []))[1].append(label)\n if len(values) > 1:\n detail = \"; \".join(\n f\"'{v}' on {', '.join(labels)}\" for v, labels in values.values()\n )\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n f\"inconsistent_{field}\",\n f\"Different {field} values within one project: {detail}. \"\n \"This usually comes from copying the previous sheet.\",\n )\n )\n\n # Pairwise separation, measured on the ground rather than by subtracting\n # raw eastings. Sierra Leone straddles UTM zones 28N and 29N, and each\n # zone restarts its easting at its own central meridian: two sites 2 km\n # apart either side of the 12 degrees W boundary differ by about 659 km\n # on paper. Every point is converted through its own zone first.\n points = []\n for label, site in records:\n utm = site.utm # resolves the zone, inferring it when unrecorded\n if utm is not None:\n points.append((label, utm))\n for i in range(len(points)):\n for j in range(i + 1, len(points)):\n li, ui = points[i]\n lj, uj = points[j]\n try:\n dist_km = utm_distance_m(ui, uj) / 1000.0\n except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError):\n # An unconvertible coordinate is already reported per site by\n # check_site_consistency; it must not sink the whole check.\n continue\n if dist_km > max_separation_km:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"points_far_apart\",\n f\"{li} and {lj} are {dist_km:.1f} km apart, which is \"\n \"unusually far for one site; check the coordinates.\",\n )\n )\n return flags\n\n\ndef check_all(records: Iterable[tuple[str, SiteMetadata]]) -> list[DataFlag]:\n \"\"\"Per-site and cross-site checks for a set of (label, site) records.\"\"\"\n records = list(records)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n for label, site in records:\n flags.extend(check_site_consistency(site, context=label))\n flags.extend(check_group_consistency(records))\n return flags\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/common.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Shared helpers for reading field sheet layouts.\n\nField sheets use a header block of ``Label: value`` pairs followed by\none or more data tables. Labels vary between sheets (\"Field\nSupervisor\", \"Test conducted by\", \"Operator\"), values sometimes live\nin the same cell after a colon and sometimes several columns to the\nright, and numbers may be stored as text with leading zeros. The\nhelpers here deal with all of that in one place.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom openpyxl import load_workbook\n\nfrom ..models import SiteMetadata\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\n\n# Canonical header keys and the label patterns that map to them.\nLABEL_PATTERNS: dict[str, list[str]] = {\n \"client\": [r\"^client\\b\"],\n \"project\": [r\"^project(?!\\s*ref)\"],\n \"project_ref\": [r\"^project\\s*ref\", r\"^geophysics\\s*ref\"],\n \"community\": [r\"^community\\b\", r\"^village\\b\", r\"^location\\b\"],\n \"chiefdom\": [r\"^chiefdom\\b\"],\n \"district\": [r\"^district\\b\"],\n \"sounding_id\": [r\"^sounding\\s*(number|no)\", r\"^ves\\s*(point|number|no)\"],\n \"date\": [r\"^date\\b\"],\n \"supervisor\": [\n r\"^field\\s*supervisor\",\n r\"^test\\s*conducted\\s*by\",\n r\"^operator\\b\",\n r\"^supervisor\\b\",\n ],\n \"contractor\": [r\"^(drilling\\s*)?contractor\\b\"],\n \"easting\": [r\"^gps\\s*coordinate\\s*east\", r\"^east(ing)?\\b\", r\"^utm\\s*east\"],\n \"northing\": [r\"^gps\\s*coordinate\\s*north\", r\"^north(ing)?\\b\", r\"^utm\\s*north\"],\n \"utm_zone\": [r\"^utm\\s*zone\", r\"^zone\\b\"],\n \"elevation_m\": [r\"^elevation\", r\"^altitude\"],\n \"array_type\": [r\"^array\\b\", r\"^electrode\\s*(array|configuration)\"],\n \"instrument\": [r\"^instrument\\b\", r\"^equipment\\b\"],\n \"borehole_ref\": [r\"^borehole\\s*/?\\s*ref\", r\"^bh\\s*ref\", r\"^borehole\\s*(number|no)\"],\n \"borehole_depth_m\": [r\"^depth\\s*of\\s*borehole\", r\"^borehole\\s*depth\", r\"^total\\s*depth\", r\"^depth\\b\"],\n \"static_water_level_m\": [r\"^static\\s*water\\s*level\", r\"^swl\\b\"],\n \"pump_setting_m\": [r\"^pump\\s*setting\", r\"^pump\\s*installation\\s*depth\"],\n \"step_length_min\": [r\"^length\\s*of\\s*each\\s*step\", r\"^step\\s*length\"],\n \"test_type\": [r\"^test\\s*type\"],\n \"start_time\": [r\"^time\\b\", r\"^start\\s*time\"],\n \"duration\": [r\"^duration\"],\n \"drilling_method\": [r\"^(drilling\\s*)?method\\b\"],\n \"start_date\": [r\"^(drilling\\s*)?start\\s*date\"],\n \"completion_date\": [r\"^compl(etion)?\\.?\\s*date\"],\n \"status\": [r\"^(bh\\s*)?status\"],\n \"sample_id\": [r\"^sample\\s*(id|number|no|ref)\"],\n \"laboratory\": [r\"^lab(oratory)?\\b\"],\n \"sample_date\": [r\"^sample\\s*date\", r\"^date\\s*sampled\"],\n \"grouting_depth_m\": [r\"^grout(ing)?\\b\"],\n \"drill_rig\": [r\"^drill\\s*rig\"],\n}\n\n_COMPILED = {\n key: [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in pats]\n for key, pats in LABEL_PATTERNS.items()\n}\n\nNUMERIC_HEADER_KEYS = {\n \"easting\",\n \"northing\",\n \"elevation_m\",\n \"borehole_depth_m\",\n \"static_water_level_m\",\n \"pump_setting_m\",\n \"step_length_min\",\n \"grouting_depth_m\",\n}\n\n\ndef load_grid(path: str | Path, sheet: str | None = None) -> tuple[list[list], str]:\n \"\"\"Load a worksheet as a rectangular grid of raw cell values.\"\"\"\n wb = load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)\n ws = wb[sheet] if sheet else wb.worksheets[0]\n grid = [list(row) for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]\n title = ws.title\n wb.close()\n return grid, title\n\n\ndef sheet_names(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:\n wb = load_workbook(path, read_only=True)\n names = list(wb.sheetnames)\n wb.close()\n return names\n\n\ndef match_label(text: str) -> str | None:\n \"\"\"Return the canonical key for a label cell, if any.\"\"\"\n matched = match_label_priority(text)\n return matched[0] if matched else None\n\n\ndef match_label_priority(text: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n \"\"\"Return ``(key, priority)`` for a label cell.\n\n Priority is the pattern index within the key's list: 0 is the most\n specific wording (\"Depth of Borehole\"), higher numbers are generic\n fallbacks (\"Depth\"). A more specific match later in the sheet may\n overwrite a generic one.\n \"\"\"\n label = clean_text(text).rstrip(\":\").strip()\n if not label:\n return None\n best: tuple[str, int] | None = None\n for key, patterns in _COMPILED.items():\n for priority, pattern in enumerate(patterns):\n if pattern.search(label):\n if best is None or priority < best[1]:\n if priority == 0:\n return key, 0\n best = (key, priority)\n break\n return best\n\n\ndef split_inline_value(cell_text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n \"\"\"Split ``\"Community: Kuntoloh\"`` into label and inline value.\"\"\"\n text = clean_text(cell_text)\n if \":\" in text:\n label, _, value = text.partition(\":\")\n value = value.strip()\n return label, value if value else None\n return text, None\n\n\ndef extract_header_fields(grid: list[list], max_rows: int = 30) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Scan the top of a sheet for ``Label -> value`` pairs.\n\n A value is taken from the same cell after a colon when present,\n otherwise from the next non-empty cell to the right. The first\n occurrence of a key wins, except that a more specific label wording\n later in the sheet (\"Depth of Borehole\") overrides a generic one\n seen earlier (\"Depth\").\n \"\"\"\n fields: dict = {}\n priorities: dict[str, int] = {}\n for r, row in enumerate(grid[:max_rows]):\n for c, cell in enumerate(row):\n if cell is None or isinstance(cell, (int, float)):\n continue\n label_text, inline_value = split_inline_value(str(cell))\n matched = match_label_priority(label_text)\n if matched is None:\n continue\n key, priority = matched\n if key in fields and priorities.get(key, 99) <= priority:\n continue\n value = inline_value\n if value is None:\n for cc in range(c + 1, min(c + 8, len(row))):\n nxt = row[cc]\n if nxt is not None and clean_text(nxt) != \"\":\n # Stop if the neighbouring cell is itself a label\n # (with or without its own inline value).\n if not isinstance(nxt, (int, float)):\n nxt_label, _ = split_inline_value(str(nxt))\n if match_label(nxt_label):\n break\n value = nxt\n break\n if value is None:\n continue\n if key in NUMERIC_HEADER_KEYS:\n number = parse_number(value)\n if number is not None:\n fields[key] = number\n priorities[key] = priority\n else:\n fields[key] = clean_text(value)\n priorities[key] = priority\n return fields\n\n\ndef site_from_fields(fields: dict, source: str = \"\") -> SiteMetadata:\n \"\"\"Build SiteMetadata from extracted header fields.\"\"\"\n zone = fields.get(\"utm_zone\")\n if isinstance(zone, str):\n zone = parse_number(zone)\n return SiteMetadata(\n client=fields.get(\"client\", \"\"),\n project=fields.get(\"project\", \"\"),\n community=fields.get(\"community\", \"\"),\n chiefdom=fields.get(\"chiefdom\", \"\"),\n district=fields.get(\"district\", \"\"),\n project_ref=fields.get(\"project_ref\", \"\"),\n easting=fields.get(\"easting\"),\n northing=fields.get(\"northing\"),\n utm_zone=int(zone) if zone else None,\n elevation_m=fields.get(\"elevation_m\"),\n date=str(fields.get(\"date\", \"\")),\n supervisor=fields.get(\"supervisor\", \"\"),\n contractor=fields.get(\"contractor\", \"\"),\n source=source,\n )\n\n\ndef find_row(grid: list[list], predicate, start: int = 0) -> int | None:\n \"\"\"Index of the first row for which ``predicate(row)`` is true.\"\"\"\n for r in range(start, len(grid)):\n if predicate(grid[r]):\n return r\n return None\n\n\ndef row_text(row: list) -> list[str]:\n return [clean_text(c).lower() for c in row]\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/drilling.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parser for drilling log sheets (Excel template and WiNGiN style tables).\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, DrillingLog, LithologyInterval\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_depth_interval, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n\ndef _find_log_header(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n \"\"\"Locate the drilling table header row and map its columns.\"\"\"\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n if not t:\n continue\n if (\"depth\" in t and \"interval\" in t) or t.startswith(\"depth /\"):\n cols[\"interval\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"depth\") and \"interval\" not in cols:\n cols.setdefault(\"interval\", c)\n elif t.startswith(\"from\"):\n cols.setdefault(\"from_time\", c)\n elif t.startswith(\"to\"):\n cols.setdefault(\"to_time\", c)\n elif \"penetration\" in t:\n cols[\"rate\"] = c\n elif \"sample\" in t or \"litholog\" in t or \"description\" in t:\n cols.setdefault(\"description\", c)\n elif \"diameter\" in t or \"bit\" in t:\n cols.setdefault(\"diameter\", c)\n elif \"strike\" in t:\n cols[\"strike\"] = c\n if \"interval\" in cols:\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\ndef read_drilling_workbook(path: str | Path) -> DrillingLog:\n grid, _ = common.load_grid(path)\n return drilling_from_grid(grid, source=str(path))\n\n\ndef drilling_from_grid(grid: list[list], source: str = \"\") -> DrillingLog:\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid, max_rows=len(grid))\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=source)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n\n located = _find_log_header(grid)\n intervals: list[LithologyInterval] = []\n strikes: list[float] = []\n if located is not None:\n header_row, cols = located\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n def cell(key):\n c = cols.get(key)\n return row[c] if c is not None and c < len(row) else None\n\n raw_interval = cell(\"interval\")\n if clean_text(raw_interval).lower().startswith(\"note\"):\n continue\n if isinstance(raw_interval, (datetime.date, datetime.datetime)):\n # Excel turns \"5-10\" typed into a General cell into 10 May.\n # Losing the row is better than a 5 to 2026 m interval, but\n # the crew has to know a row went missing.\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"interval_read_as_date\",\n f\"Depth interval cell holds the date \"\n f\"{raw_interval:%d %b %Y} - Excel converts entries like \"\n '\"5-10\" into dates. Format the depth column as Text '\n \"and retype the interval; this row was skipped.\",\n )\n )\n continue\n interval = parse_depth_interval(raw_interval)\n if interval is None:\n continue\n top, bottom = interval\n description = clean_text(cell(\"description\"))\n intervals.append(\n LithologyInterval(\n top_m=top,\n bottom_m=bottom,\n description=description,\n from_time=clean_text(cell(\"from_time\")),\n to_time=clean_text(cell(\"to_time\")),\n penetration_rate_m_per_min=parse_number(cell(\"rate\")),\n bit_diameter_in=parse_number(cell(\"diameter\")),\n )\n )\n strike = parse_number(cell(\"strike\"))\n if strike is not None:\n strikes.append(strike)\n\n # Water strikes noted as text lines (\"First water strike: 12m\")\n for row in grid:\n for c in row:\n text = clean_text(c).lower()\n if \"water strike\" in text and not text.startswith(\"note\"):\n value = parse_number(text.split(\":\")[-1])\n if value is not None and value > 0 and value not in strikes:\n strikes.append(value)\n\n total = fields.get(\"borehole_depth_m\")\n if total is None and intervals:\n total = max(iv.bottom_m for iv in intervals)\n\n log = DrillingLog(\n site=site,\n borehole_ref=str(fields.get(\"borehole_ref\", \"\") or \"\"),\n total_depth_m=total,\n drilling_method=fields.get(\"drilling_method\", \"\"),\n intervals=sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: iv.top_m),\n water_strikes_m=sorted(strikes),\n grouting_depth_m=fields.get(\"grouting_depth_m\"),\n start_date=str(fields.get(\"start_date\", \"\")),\n completion_date=str(fields.get(\"completion_date\", \"\")),\n status=fields.get(\"status\", \"\"),\n source=str(source),\n )\n\n # consistency of the interval column\n for a, b in zip(log.intervals, log.intervals[1:]):\n if b.top_m < a.bottom_m - 1e-9:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"interval_overlap\",\n f\"Depth intervals overlap at {b.top_m} m.\",\n )\n )\n elif b.top_m > a.bottom_m + 1e-9:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"interval_gap\",\n f\"Gap in the drilling log between {a.bottom_m} m and {b.top_m} m.\",\n )\n )\n if total and log.intervals and abs(log.intervals[-1].bottom_m - total) > 1e-6:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"depth_mismatch\",\n f\"Stated total depth {total} m differs from the deepest logged \"\n f\"interval {log.intervals[-1].bottom_m} m.\",\n )\n )\n if not log.intervals:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\"error\", \"no_intervals\", \"No depth intervals found in the log.\")\n )\n missing_desc = sum(1 for iv in log.intervals if not iv.description)\n if log.intervals and missing_desc:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"missing_lithology\",\n f\"{missing_desc} interval(s) have no lithology description.\",\n )\n )\n log.flags = flags\n return log\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/pumping.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parsers for pumping test field sheets (Excel template and Word sheets).\n\nThe paper layout (WiNGiN step test sheet) records readings in side by\nside hourly column groups, each with Time (min), Water Level (m) and\nDrawdown (m), followed by a Recovery block. Two rules from the sheets\ndrive the parsing:\n\n* The recorded drawdown column is the increment between successive\n readings, not drawdown below static. Only time and water level are\n read; true drawdown is always recomputed as water level minus static\n water level.\n* Discharge is often missing. The test still parses and produces water\n level and drawdown series, but a ``missing_discharge`` flag marks all\n transmissivity and yield results as pending.\n* Units are read, not assumed. The sheet's own headings say what the\n numbers mean - \"Time (min)\", \"Discharge per step (m3/h)\" - and a crew\n that heads the column L/s or records the times in hours means exactly\n that. Both are converted to the canonical m3/h and minutes. A unit the\n toolkit cannot read is refused rather than guessed at: a discharge in an\n unreadable unit leaves the step pending, and a time column in one is\n dropped, because there is no pending state for time and every consumer\n would otherwise fit a curve to the wrong axis.\n\nTimes within each group are irregular (1, 2, 3 and 5 minute spacing);\nnothing assumes uniform sampling.\n\nTwo recovery layouts occur on real sheets and both are handled:\n\n* A dedicated recovery group with its own Time, Water Level and\n Recovery columns (Kuntolo sheet). Water level is read; the recovery\n increment column is ignored.\n* A single shared time column with a Recovery column holding water\n levels during recovery (Dr. Timbo sheet). The recovery column is\n read against the shared times, interpreted as minutes since the pump\n stopped.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, PumpingStep, PumpingTest\nfrom ..units import Quantity, convert, read_quantity, unit_from_label\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n# Free-text discharge notes: \"Constant Discharge of 2.93m3/h\", \"Q = 0.81 L/s\".\n# The unit is captured rather than assumed - the old pattern only matched an\n# m3/h tail, so a rate written in L/s was silently dropped instead of read.\n_DISCHARGE_TEXT_RE = re.compile(\n r\"discharge\\s*(?:of|0f)?\\s*[:=]?\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*\"\n r\"([a-z\u00b5\u03bc]{1,3}\\s*3?\\s*/\\s*[a-z]{1,4}|lps|lpm|lph)\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Locating the column groups\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _find_groups(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, list[dict]] | None:\n \"\"\"Find the header row of Time / Water Level / ... column groups.\n\n Returns ``(row_index, groups)``. Each group has column indices and\n ``kind`` of \"pumping\" or \"recovery\". A \"reco\" column adjacent to a\n time column forms a recovery triplet (level read from its own water\n level column); a distant \"reco\" column shares the pumping time\n column and holds water levels itself.\n \"\"\"\n best: tuple[int, list[dict]] | None = None\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n time_cols = [c for c, t in enumerate(texts) if t.startswith(\"time\")]\n if not time_cols:\n continue\n groups: list[dict] = []\n for gi, c in enumerate(time_cols):\n end = time_cols[gi + 1] if gi + 1 < len(time_cols) else len(texts)\n level_col = None\n reco_col = None\n for cc in range(c + 1, end):\n t = texts[cc]\n if not t:\n continue\n if (\"water\" in t or t.startswith(\"level\")) and level_col is None:\n level_col = cc\n elif \"reco\" in t and reco_col is None:\n reco_col = cc\n if level_col is None and reco_col is None:\n continue\n # The header text travels with the group so the time unit it\n # declares - \"Time (min)\", \"Time (h)\" - is read rather than assumed.\n header = texts[c]\n if reco_col is not None and level_col is not None:\n if reco_col - c <= 2:\n # Kuntolo style triplet: Time, Water Level, Recovery increment\n groups.append({\"time\": c, \"level\": level_col,\n \"kind\": \"recovery\", \"time_header\": header})\n else:\n # Dr. Timbo style: shared time column; recovery column holds levels\n groups.append({\"time\": c, \"level\": level_col,\n \"kind\": \"pumping\", \"time_header\": header})\n groups.append({\"time\": c, \"level\": reco_col,\n \"kind\": \"recovery\", \"time_header\": header})\n elif reco_col is not None:\n groups.append({\"time\": c, \"level\": reco_col,\n \"kind\": \"recovery\", \"time_header\": header})\n else:\n groups.append({\"time\": c, \"level\": level_col,\n \"kind\": \"pumping\", \"time_header\": header})\n if groups and (best is None or len(groups) > len(best[1])):\n best = (r, groups)\n return best\n\n\ndef _read_series(\n grid: list[list], header_row: int, group: dict\n) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, str, list[str]]:\n \"\"\"Read one Time / Water Level pair, with the times put into minutes.\n\n Returns ``(times_min, levels, time_unit, skipped)``. ``time_unit`` is the\n unit the column declared; it is empty when nothing was declared (minutes\n assumed) and ``\"?\"`` when the *header* declared one that could not\n be read - in which case the caller must drop the group rather than treat\n unknown units as minutes. Unlike discharge, there is no \"pending\" state\n for time: every consumer would silently produce wrong transmissivities.\n\n ``skipped`` lists individual cells whose own text could not be read; they\n cost one reading each rather than the column, and the caller reports\n them.\n \"\"\"\n header = group.get(\"time_header\", \"\")\n # A unit the header declares applies to the whole column, so an\n # unreadable one there costs the group. A unit written into one cell\n # applies to that cell, so an unreadable one there costs one reading -\n # otherwise a single annotated entry (\"5 (approx)\") threw away the test.\n declared, header_unit = unit_from_label(header, dimension=\"time\")\n if declared and header_unit is None:\n return (np.array([], dtype=float), np.array([], dtype=float),\n f\"?{declared}\", [])\n\n times, levels, skipped = [], [], []\n unit_text = declared\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n cell = row[group[\"time\"]] if group[\"time\"] < len(row) else None\n wl = parse_number(row[group[\"level\"]]) if group[\"level\"] < len(row) else None\n quantity = read_quantity(cell, header, dimension=\"time\")\n if quantity.status == \"absent\" or wl is None:\n continue\n if quantity.status == \"unknown\":\n # one unreadable reading, not a broken column - but never silent\n skipped.append(str(cell))\n continue\n if quantity.unit_text:\n unit_text = quantity.unit_text\n times.append(quantity.value)\n levels.append(wl)\n return (np.array(times, dtype=float), np.array(levels, dtype=float),\n unit_text, skipped)\n\n\n_STEP_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*step\\s*\\d*\\s*q\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\n\ndef _row_unit_hint(row: list) -> str:\n \"\"\"The row's own leading label, e.g. 'Discharge per step (m3/h)'.\"\"\"\n for cell in row:\n text = clean_text(cell)\n if text and \"discharge\" in text.lower():\n return text\n return \"\"\n\n\ndef _find_step_discharges(grid: list[list]) -> dict[int, \"Quantity\"]:\n \"\"\"Read per step discharge from 'Step n Q' labelled cells.\n\n Two hazards on a real sheet, both handled here:\n\n * The rate is written in whatever unit the crew used. The unit is taken\n from the value cell, then the label, then the row's discharge caption,\n and the value is converted to m3/h. A unit that cannot be read is\n refused, which routes the step into the existing \"discharge missing,\n results pending\" path rather than producing a wrong transmissivity.\n * The neighbouring cell may be the *next* step's label rather than a\n value. Scanning it blindly read \"Step 2 Q (m3/h)\" as a discharge of\n 2 m3/h whenever the first step's box was left empty, and fitted a\n transmissivity to it. Label-shaped cells are skipped.\n \"\"\"\n discharges: dict[int, Quantity] = {}\n for row in grid:\n row_hint = _row_unit_hint(row)\n for c, cell in enumerate(row):\n label = clean_text(cell)\n if not _STEP_LABEL_RE.match(label):\n continue\n num = parse_number(label.lower().split(\"q\")[0])\n if num is None:\n continue\n for cc in range(c + 1, min(c + 3, len(row))):\n neighbour = row[cc]\n if _STEP_LABEL_RE.match(clean_text(neighbour)):\n break # the next step's label, not this step's value\n quantity = read_quantity(\n neighbour, label, row_hint, dimension=\"flow\"\n )\n if quantity.status == \"absent\":\n continue\n discharges[int(num)] = quantity\n break\n return discharges\n\n\ndef _discharge_candidates_from_text(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[list[float], list[str]]:\n \"\"\"Discharge values mentioned in free text such as\n 'Constant Discharge of 2.93m3/h'.\n\n Returns ``(values_in_m3_per_h, unreadable_unit_texts)``. A note whose\n unit cannot be read is reported rather than converted, so it can be\n raised as a flag instead of quietly becoming a number in m3/h.\n \"\"\"\n found: list[float] = []\n unreadable: list[str] = []\n for row in grid:\n for cell in row:\n if cell is None or isinstance(cell, (int, float)):\n continue\n for m in _DISCHARGE_TEXT_RE.finditer(str(cell)):\n written = m.group(2).strip()\n value = convert(float(m.group(1)), written, \"m3/h\", dimension=\"flow\")\n if value is None:\n if written not in unreadable:\n unreadable.append(written)\n continue\n if value not in found:\n found.append(value)\n return found, unreadable\n\n\n# Pre-printed text that names a test kind without recording which test was\n# run: the template's own title mentions both, and its constant-discharge\n# column labels (\"Constant discharge 61-120 min\") sit on every sheet whatever\n# was pumped. Reading either as an answer turned step tests into constant ones.\n_CONSTANT_COLUMN_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"constant\\s+discharge\\s*\\d\")\n\n\ndef _sheet_test_type(grid: list[list]) -> str:\n \"\"\"Look for 'STEP TEST' or 'CONSTANT DISCHARGE' banners in the sheet.\n\n Only decisive text counts. A cell naming both kinds is a form title\n (\"PUMPING TEST FIELD SHEET (STEP / CONSTANT DISCHARGE)\"), and a\n constant-discharge column label is a heading for one of the hourly\n groups - neither says which test the crew actually ran.\n \"\"\"\n for row in grid:\n for cell in row:\n text = clean_text(cell).lower()\n if not text:\n continue\n step_words = \"step test\" in text or \"step drawdown\" in text\n constant_words = (\n \"constant discharge\" in text or \"constant rate\" in text\n )\n # \"(STEP / CONSTANT DISCHARGE)\" offers both; any mention of a step\n # alongside constant wording makes the cell a title, not an answer\n if constant_words and \"step\" in text:\n continue\n if step_words:\n return \"step\"\n if constant_words and not _CONSTANT_COLUMN_LABEL_RE.search(text):\n return \"constant\"\n return \"\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Assembling the PumpingTest\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _assemble(grid: list[list], source: str) -> PumpingTest:\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid, max_rows=len(grid))\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=source)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n\n located = _find_groups(grid)\n if located is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No Time/Water Level column groups found in {source}\")\n header_row, groups = located\n\n def _series(kind: str) -> list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]:\n \"\"\"Read every column group of one kind, dropping unreadable-unit ones.\n\n A time column whose unit cannot be read is dropped rather than taken\n as minutes: reading hours as minutes would rescale every drawdown\n curve and every transmissivity fitted to it, silently.\n \"\"\"\n out = []\n for group in groups:\n if group[\"kind\"] != kind:\n continue\n t, wl, unit_text, skipped = _read_series(grid, header_row, group)\n if unit_text.startswith(\"?\"):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"time_unit_unknown\",\n f\"The {kind} time column is headed \"\n f\"'{group.get('time_header', '')}' and its unit \"\n f\"'{unit_text[1:]}' could not be read, so the readings \"\n \"were not used. Head the column in minutes, hours or \"\n \"seconds.\",\n )\n )\n continue\n if unit_text and unit_text.lower() not in (\"min\", \"mins\", \"minute\",\n \"minutes\"):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"time_unit_converted\",\n f\"The {kind} times are recorded in '{unit_text}' and \"\n \"have been converted to minutes for the analysis.\",\n )\n )\n if skipped:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"time_reading_unreadable\",\n f\"{len(skipped)} {kind} reading(s) carried text this \"\n \"toolkit could not read as a time and were left out (\"\n + \", \".join(repr(x) for x in skipped[:3])\n + \"). Put notes outside the reading columns.\",\n )\n )\n if len(t):\n out.append((t, wl))\n return out\n\n pumping_series = _series(\"pumping\")\n recovery_series = _series(\"recovery\")\n\n test_type = str(fields.get(\"test_type\", \"\")).strip().lower()\n stated = bool(test_type)\n if not test_type:\n test_type = _sheet_test_type(grid)\n inferred_from_shape = not test_type\n if not test_type:\n test_type = \"step\" if len(pumping_series) > 1 else \"constant\"\n if inferred_from_shape and not stated and len(pumping_series) > 1:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"test_type_inferred\",\n f\"The test type cell is blank; the {len(pumping_series)} filled \"\n \"column groups have been read as the steps of a step test. If \"\n 'this was a constant discharge test, write \"constant\" in the '\n \"test type cell so the readings are analysed as one series.\",\n )\n )\n\n if test_type.startswith(\"constant\") and len(pumping_series) > 1:\n # hourly column groups are one continuous series on constant tests\n t = np.concatenate([s[0] for s in pumping_series])\n wl = np.concatenate([s[1] for s in pumping_series])\n order = np.argsort(t, kind=\"stable\")\n pumping_series = [(t[order], wl[order])]\n\n step_length = fields.get(\"step_length_min\")\n discharges = _find_step_discharges(grid)\n\n steps: list[PumpingStep] = []\n for i, (t, wl) in enumerate(pumping_series, start=1):\n quantity = discharges.get(i)\n steps.append(\n PumpingStep(\n step_number=i,\n time_min=t,\n water_level_m=wl,\n # A refused unit leaves this None, which is the existing\n # \"results pending until discharge is supplied\" path - the\n # right answer, and far better than a number in the wrong unit.\n discharge_m3_per_h=quantity.value if quantity is not None else None,\n label=f\"Step {i}\" if len(pumping_series) > 1 else \"Pumping phase\",\n )\n )\n if quantity is None:\n continue\n if quantity.status == \"unknown\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"discharge_unit_unknown\",\n f\"Step {i} discharge is written as \"\n f\"{quantity.raw_value:g} '{quantity.unit_text}', a unit \"\n \"this toolkit does not recognise, so it was not used. \"\n \"Record the rate in m3/h, L/s or L/min.\",\n )\n )\n elif quantity.status == \"converted\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"discharge_unit_converted\",\n f\"Step {i} discharge {quantity.raw_value:g} \"\n f\"{quantity.unit_text} read as {quantity.value:.3g} m3/h.\",\n )\n )\n elif quantity.status == \"assumed\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"discharge_unit_assumed\",\n f\"Step {i} discharge {quantity.raw_value:g} carries no \"\n \"unit on the sheet and was read as m3/h. Head the \"\n \"discharge row with its unit to remove the assumption.\",\n )\n )\n\n # Free-text discharge: use it only when unambiguous (one candidate, one step)\n candidates, unreadable_units = _discharge_candidates_from_text(grid)\n missing = [s for s in steps if s.discharge_m3_per_h is None]\n for written in unreadable_units:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"discharge_unit_unknown\",\n f\"A discharge note on the sheet is written in '{written}', a \"\n \"unit this toolkit does not recognise, so it was not used.\",\n )\n )\n if candidates and missing:\n if len(candidates) == 1 and len(steps) == 1:\n steps[0].discharge_m3_per_h = candidates[0]\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"discharge_from_text\",\n f\"Discharge {candidates[0]:g} m3/h taken from a text note on \"\n \"the sheet; confirm against the measured value.\",\n )\n )\n else:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"discharge_ambiguous\",\n \"Discharge mentioned in sheet text (\"\n + \", \".join(f\"{c:g} m3/h\" for c in candidates)\n + \") but not assigned per step; enter values in the template.\",\n )\n )\n\n recovery_time = recovery_level = None\n if recovery_series:\n recovery_time, recovery_level = recovery_series[0]\n\n if recovery_time is not None:\n test_type += \"+recovery\"\n\n swl = fields.get(\"static_water_level_m\")\n pumping_duration = None\n if steps:\n pumping_duration = float(max(s.time_min.max() for s in steps))\n\n test = PumpingTest(\n site=site,\n borehole_ref=str(fields.get(\"borehole_ref\", \"\") or \"\"),\n test_type=test_type,\n static_water_level_m=swl,\n borehole_depth_m=fields.get(\"borehole_depth_m\"),\n pump_setting_m=fields.get(\"pump_setting_m\"),\n step_length_min=step_length,\n steps=steps,\n recovery_time_min=recovery_time,\n recovery_level_m=recovery_level,\n pumping_duration_min=pumping_duration,\n source=str(source),\n )\n\n # ---- data quality flags ------------------------------------------------\n if swl is None:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"missing_static_water_level\",\n \"Static water level is missing; drawdown cannot be computed.\",\n )\n )\n missing_q = [s.step_number for s in steps if s.discharge_m3_per_h is None]\n if missing_q:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"missing_discharge\",\n \"Discharge not recorded for step(s) \"\n + \", \".join(str(n) for n in missing_q)\n + \". Drawdown and recovery curves are produced, but transmissivity \"\n \"and yield results are pending until discharge values are supplied.\",\n )\n )\n if swl is not None and steps:\n if any(np.any(s.water_level_m < swl - 0.01) for s in steps):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"water_level_above_static\",\n \"Some pumping water levels are above the stated static water \"\n \"level, giving negative drawdown. Check the static level and \"\n \"the measuring datum on the sheet.\",\n )\n )\n for s in steps:\n if np.any(np.diff(s.time_min) <= 0):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"time_not_increasing\",\n f\"Times are not strictly increasing in {s.label}.\",\n s.label,\n )\n )\n if test.borehole_depth_m and test.pump_setting_m:\n if test.pump_setting_m > test.borehole_depth_m:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"pump_below_borehole\",\n \"Pump setting is deeper than the borehole depth.\",\n )\n )\n if test.borehole_depth_m and steps:\n max_wl = max(float(np.nanmax(s.water_level_m)) for s in steps)\n if max_wl > test.borehole_depth_m:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"level_below_borehole\",\n f\"Recorded water level {max_wl:.2f} m exceeds the stated \"\n f\"borehole depth {test.borehole_depth_m:.0f} m; check the sheet.\",\n )\n )\n test.flags = flags\n return test\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Entry points\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef read_pumping_workbook(path: str | Path) -> PumpingTest:\n \"\"\"Read a pumping test from the Excel template layout.\"\"\"\n grid, _ = common.load_grid(path)\n return _assemble(grid, source=str(path))\n\n\ndef read_pumping_docx(path: str | Path) -> PumpingTest:\n \"\"\"Read a pumping test from a Word field sheet (Kuntolo style).\n\n Paragraph text supplies the header block; the
