table whose header\n contains Time / Water Level column groups supplies the readings.\n \"\"\"\n import docx # python-docx\n\n path = Path(path)\n document = docx.Document(str(path))\n\n header_grid: list[list] = []\n for para in document.paragraphs:\n text = para.text.strip()\n if not text:\n continue\n parts = [p for p in re.split(r\"\\t+|\\s{3,}\", text) if p.strip()]\n header_grid.append(parts)\n\n best_table: list[list] | None = None\n best_count = 0\n for table in document.tables:\n grid = [[cell.text for cell in row.cells] for row in table.rows]\n located = _find_groups(grid)\n if located and len(located[1]) > best_count:\n best_table = grid\n best_count = len(located[1])\n if best_table is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No pumping test table found in {path}\")\n\n return _assemble(header_grid + best_table, source=str(path))\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/templates.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Generate the standard Excel field data templates.\n\nThe templates mirror the paper field sheets in use (Rokel VES sheet,\nWiNGiN step test sheet) so the field team can transcribe data cell for\ncell, while adding the fields that are often missing on paper, such as\ndischarge per step and the UTM zone.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom openpyxl import Workbook\nfrom openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Border, Font, PatternFill, Side\nfrom openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter\n\nACCENT = \"1F5C8B\"\nLIGHT = \"DCE6F1\"\n\n_thin = Side(style=\"thin\", color=\"9BB3C8\")\nBORDER = Border(left=_thin, right=_thin, top=_thin, bottom=_thin)\n\n\ndef _label(ws, cell: str, text: str) -> None:\n ws[cell] = text\n ws[cell].font = Font(bold=True, size=10)\n ws[cell].fill = PatternFill(\"solid\", fgColor=LIGHT)\n ws[cell].border = BORDER\n\n\ndef _value(ws, cell: str, text: str = \"\") -> None:\n ws[cell] = text\n ws[cell].border = BORDER\n\n\ndef _title(ws, cell: str, text: str, span: str | None = None) -> None:\n ws[cell] = text\n ws[cell].font = Font(bold=True, size=12, color=ACCENT)\n if span:\n ws.merge_cells(span)\n ws[cell].alignment = Alignment(horizontal=\"center\")\n\n\ndef _table_header(ws, row: int, headers: list[str], start_col: int = 1) -> None:\n for i, h in enumerate(headers):\n cell = ws.cell(row=row, column=start_col + i, value=h)\n cell.font = Font(bold=True, size=10, color=\"FFFFFF\")\n cell.fill = PatternFill(\"solid\", fgColor=ACCENT)\n cell.alignment = Alignment(horizontal=\"center\", wrap_text=True)\n cell.border = BORDER\n\n\ndef write_ves_template(path: str | Path, n_soundings: int = 2, n_rows: int = 24) -> Path:\n \"\"\"VES field data template, one worksheet per sounding.\"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n for s in range(1, n_soundings + 1):\n ws = wb.active if s == 1 else wb.create_sheet()\n ws.title = f\"VES {s}\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"SCHLUMBERGER ARRAY VES FIELD DATA\", \"A1:D1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Client\", \"B2\"), (\"C2\", \"Community\", \"D2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Project\", \"B3\"), (\"C3\", \"Sounding Number\", \"D3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"District\", \"B4\"), (\"C4\", \"GPS Coordinate East\", \"D4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"Date\", \"B5\"), (\"C5\", \"GPS Coordinate North\", \"D5\"),\n (\"A6\", \"Field Supervisor\", \"B6\"), (\"C6\", \"Elevation (m)\", \"D6\"),\n (\"A7\", \"Chiefdom\", \"B7\"), (\"C7\", \"UTM Zone (28N or 29N)\", \"D7\"),\n (\"A8\", \"Array\", \"B8\"), (\"C8\", \"Instrument\", \"D8\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n ws[\"B8\"] = \"Schlumberger\"\n ws[\"D8\"] = \"Syscal Junior\"\n ws[\"D3\"] = s\n _table_header(ws, 10, [\"No.\", \"AB/2 (m)\", \"MN (m)\", \"Apparent Resistivity (ohm-m)\"])\n for r in range(11, 11 + n_rows):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=r - 10).border = BORDER\n for c in range(2, 5):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n note = (\n \"Notes: MN is the full potential electrode spacing. Repeat the same AB/2 \"\n \"with the old and new MN at every segment change.\"\n )\n ws.cell(row=12 + n_rows, column=1, value=note).font = Font(italic=True, size=9)\n for col, width in zip(\"ABCD\", (22, 16, 16, 28)):\n ws.column_dimensions[col].width = width\n wb.save(path)\n return Path(path)\n\n\ndef write_pumping_template(path: str | Path) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Pumping test template: header, four step groups and recovery.\"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Pumping Test\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"PUMPING TEST FIELD SHEET (STEP / CONSTANT DISCHARGE)\", \"A1:O1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Community\", \"B2\"), (\"D2\", \"Date\", \"E2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Client\", \"B3\"), (\"D3\", \"Length of each step (min)\", \"E3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"Test conducted by\", \"B4\"), (\"D4\", \"Start time\", \"E4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"Borehole Ref. No.\", \"B5\"), (\"D5\", \"Depth of Borehole (m)\", \"E5\"),\n (\"A6\", \"Static water level (m)\", \"B6\"), (\"D6\", \"Pump setting (m)\", \"E6\"),\n (\"A7\", \"Test type (step or constant)\", \"B7\"), (\"D7\", \"District\", \"E7\"),\n (\"G2\", \"GPS Coordinate East\", \"H2\"), (\"G3\", \"GPS Coordinate North\", \"H3\"),\n (\"G4\", \"UTM Zone (28N or 29N)\", \"H4\"), (\"G5\", \"Elevation (m)\", \"H5\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n\n # Discharge row: one value per step group; leave blank if not measured\n _label(ws, \"A9\", \"Discharge per step (m3/h)\")\n for i, col in enumerate((\"B\", \"E\", \"H\", \"K\")):\n _label(ws, f\"{col}9\", f\"Step {i + 1} Q\")\n _value(ws, f\"{chr(ord(col) + 1)}9\")\n\n groups = [\"0-60 min\", \"61-120 min\", \"121-180 min\", \"181-240 min\"]\n start_cols = [1, 4, 7, 10]\n header_row = 11\n for g, (label, c0) in enumerate(zip(groups, start_cols)):\n cell = ws.cell(row=header_row - 1, column=c0, value=f\"Constant discharge {label}\")\n cell.font = Font(bold=True, size=10, color=ACCENT)\n _table_header(\n ws, header_row, [\"Time (min)\", \"Water Level (m)\", \"Drawdown (m)\"], start_col=c0\n )\n cell = ws.cell(row=header_row - 1, column=13, value=\"Recovery\")\n cell.font = Font(bold=True, size=10, color=ACCENT)\n _table_header(\n ws, header_row, [\"Time (min)\", \"Water Level (m)\", \"Recovery (m)\"], start_col=13\n )\n for r in range(header_row + 1, header_row + 41):\n for c in list(range(1, 12 + 1)) + [13, 14, 15]:\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n note = (\n \"Notes: record depth to water in metres below the measuring point. The Drawdown \"\n \"and Recovery columns are the change between successive readings; the analysis \"\n \"recomputes true drawdown from the static water level. Recovery time is minutes \"\n \"since the pump stopped. Record the discharge of every step; results stay \"\n \"provisional until discharge is supplied.\"\n )\n ws.cell(row=header_row + 42, column=1, value=note).font = Font(italic=True, size=9)\n for c in range(1, 16):\n ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(c)].width = 13\n wb.save(path)\n return Path(path)\n\n\ndef write_drilling_template(path: str | Path, n_rows: int = 20) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Drilling log template.\"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Drilling Log\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"BOREHOLE DRILLING LOG\", \"A1:G1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Community\", \"B2\"), (\"D2\", \"Client\", \"E2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Contractor\", \"B3\"), (\"D3\", \"Borehole Ref. No.\", \"E3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"Drilling start date\", \"B4\"), (\"D4\", \"Completion date\", \"E4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"Drilling method\", \"B5\"), (\"D5\", \"Total depth (m)\", \"E5\"),\n (\"A6\", \"District\", \"B6\"), (\"D6\", \"BH status\", \"E6\"),\n (\"A7\", \"GPS Coordinate East\", \"B7\"), (\"D7\", \"GPS Coordinate North\", \"E7\"),\n (\"A8\", \"UTM Zone (28N or 29N)\", \"B8\"), (\"D8\", \"Elevation (m)\", \"E8\"),\n (\"A9\", \"Grouting depth (m)\", \"B9\"), (\"D9\", \"Drill rig\", \"E9\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n _table_header(\n ws,\n 11,\n [\n \"Depth interval (m)\",\n \"From time\",\n \"To time\",\n \"Penetration rate (m/min)\",\n \"Sample / lithology description\",\n \"Drilling diameter (in)\",\n \"Water strike depth (m)\",\n ],\n )\n for r in range(12, 12 + n_rows):\n for c in range(1, 8):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n ws.cell(row=13 + n_rows, column=1, value=(\n \"Notes: write depth intervals as 0-5, 5-10 and so on. Enter a water strike \"\n \"depth on the row of the interval where water was struck.\"\n )).font = Font(italic=True, size=9)\n for col, width in zip(\"ABCDEFG\", (18, 10, 10, 20, 42, 18, 20)):\n ws.column_dimensions[col].width = width\n wb.save(path)\n return Path(path)\n\n\ndef write_daily_log_template(path: str | Path, n_rows: int = 14) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Driller's daily report template.\n\n The daily record the supervision guidance expects: per interval\n times, depths, formation, water strikes and airlift yield, plus\n the day totals, standing time and the double signature (rig\n operator and supervisor) that makes the log auditable against\n invoiced metres.\n \"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Daily Log\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"DRILLER'S DAILY REPORT\", \"A1:G1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Community\", \"B2\"), (\"D2\", \"Borehole Ref. No.\", \"E2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Date\", \"B3\"), (\"D3\", \"Drill rig\", \"E3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"Contractor\", \"B4\"), (\"D4\", \"Supervisor\", \"E4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"Weather / site conditions\", \"B5\"), (\"D5\", \"Record taker\", \"E5\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n _table_header(\n ws,\n 7,\n [\n \"Time from\",\n \"Time to\",\n \"Depth from (m)\",\n \"Depth to (m)\",\n \"Formation / activity\",\n \"Water strike (m)\",\n \"Airlift yield (L/s)\",\n ],\n )\n for r in range(8, 8 + n_rows):\n for c in range(1, 8):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n totals_row = 9 + n_rows\n for cell, label in (\n (f\"A{totals_row}\", \"Metres drilled today\"),\n (f\"C{totals_row}\", \"Cumulative metres\"),\n (f\"E{totals_row}\", \"Casing installed today (m)\"),\n (f\"A{totals_row + 1}\", \"Standing / breakdown hours\"),\n (f\"C{totals_row + 1}\", \"Reason\"),\n ):\n _label(ws, cell, label)\n for cell in (f\"B{totals_row}\", f\"D{totals_row}\", f\"F{totals_row}\",\n f\"B{totals_row + 1}\", f\"D{totals_row + 1}\"):\n _value(ws, cell)\n sign_row = totals_row + 3\n for cell, label in (\n (f\"A{sign_row}\", \"Rig operator signature\"),\n (f\"D{sign_row}\", \"Supervisor signature\"),\n ):\n _label(ws, cell, label)\n _value(ws, cell.replace(\"A\", \"B\").replace(\"D\", \"E\"))\n ws.cell(row=sign_row + 2, column=1, value=(\n \"Notes: one row per drilled interval or activity (moving, standing, \"\n \"casing). Both signatures are required every day; the office checks \"\n \"invoiced metres against these logs.\"\n )).font = Font(italic=True, size=9)\n for col, width in zip(\"ABCDEFG\", (12, 12, 14, 14, 40, 16, 16)):\n ws.column_dimensions[col].width = width\n wb.save(path)\n return Path(path)\n\n\nSTANDARD_PARAMETERS = [\n (\"pH\", \"pH units\"), (\"Electrical conductivity\", \"uS/cm\"), (\"TDS\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Turbidity\", \"NTU\"), (\"Temperature\", \"deg C\"), (\"Total hardness\", \"mg/L as CaCO3\"),\n (\"Alkalinity\", \"mg/L as CaCO3\"), (\"Calcium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Magnesium\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Sodium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Potassium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Bicarbonate\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Chloride\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Sulfate\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Nitrate (as NO3)\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Nitrite (as NO2)\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Ammonia (as N)\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Fluoride\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Iron\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Manganese\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Arsenic\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Lead\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Copper\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Zinc\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Chromium (total)\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Cadmium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"E. coli\", \"CFU/100 mL\"), (\"Total coliforms\", \"CFU/100 mL\"),\n]\n\n\ndef write_quality_template(path: str | Path) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Water quality laboratory results template.\"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Water Quality\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"WATER QUALITY LABORATORY RESULTS\", \"A1:E1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Community\", \"B2\"), (\"D2\", \"Client\", \"E2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Sample ID\", \"B3\"), (\"D3\", \"Borehole Ref. No.\", \"E3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"Sample date\", \"B4\"), (\"D4\", \"Laboratory\", \"E4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"District\", \"B5\"), (\"D5\", \"Project\", \"E5\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n _table_header(\n ws, 7, [\"Parameter\", \"Unit\", \"Value\", \"Detection limit\", \"Method\"]\n )\n for i, (param, unit) in enumerate(STANDARD_PARAMETERS):\n r = 8 + i\n ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=param).border = BORDER\n ws.cell(row=r, column=2, value=unit).border = BORDER\n for c in (3, 4, 5):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n ws.cell(row=9 + len(STANDARD_PARAMETERS), column=1, value=(\n \"Notes: for results below detection write
list[Path]:\n \"\"\"Write every field template into ``folder`` and return the paths.\"\"\"\n folder = Path(folder)\n folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n return [\n write_ves_template(folder / \"template_ves.xlsx\"),\n write_pumping_template(folder / \"template_pumping_test.xlsx\"),\n write_drilling_template(folder / \"template_drilling_log.xlsx\"),\n write_quality_template(folder / \"template_water_quality.xlsx\"),\n write_daily_log_template(folder / \"template_daily_drilling_report.xlsx\"),\n ]\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/ves.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parser for VES field data sheets (Excel and CSV).\n\nReads the Rokel style layout: a header block (client, community,\ndistrict, sounding number, GPS east/north, elevation, date, field\nsupervisor) followed by a table with columns No., AB/2 (m), MN (m) and\napparent resistivity (ohm-m). Values stored as text with leading\nzeros (for example ``078.7`` or GPS ``0708958``) parse cleanly.\n\nDuplicate AB/2 values with different MN mark Schlumberger segment\nchanges; both readings are kept.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, VESSounding\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n# \"MN/2\", \"MN / 2\", \"MN /2 (m)\" - a typed header keeps its spaces\n_MN_HALF_RE = re.compile(r\"mn\\s*/\\s*2\")\n\n\ndef _find_data_header(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n \"\"\"Locate the data table header row and map columns.\n\n Returns (row_index, {\"no\": c, \"ab2\": c, \"mn\": c, \"rho\": c}).\n \"\"\"\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n if not t:\n continue\n if \"ab/2\" in t or t == \"ab2\" or \"ab / 2\" in t:\n cols[\"ab2\"] = c\n # half-MN first, and tolerant of the spaces a typed header carries:\n # \"MN / 2 (m)\" does not contain the literal \"/2\", so it used to fall\n # through to the full-MN branch and halve every potential spacing\n elif t.startswith(\"mn\") and _MN_HALF_RE.search(t):\n cols[\"mn_half\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"mn\"):\n cols[\"mn\"] = c\n elif \"resistivity\" in t or t.startswith(\"rho\") or \"ohm\" in t:\n cols[\"rho\"] = c\n elif t in (\"no.\", \"no\", \"reading\", \"n\"):\n cols[\"no\"] = c\n if \"ab2\" in cols and \"rho\" in cols:\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\ndef _sounding_from_grid(\n grid: list[list], source: str, sheet_name: str = \"\"\n) -> VESSounding | None:\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid)\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=source)\n located = _find_data_header(grid)\n if located is None:\n return None\n header_row, cols = located\n\n ab2, mn, rho = [], [], []\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n mn_is_half = \"mn\" not in cols and \"mn_half\" in cols\n mn_col = cols.get(\"mn\", cols.get(\"mn_half\"))\n blank_run = 0\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n a = parse_number(row[cols[\"ab2\"]]) if cols[\"ab2\"] < len(row) else None\n r = parse_number(row[cols[\"rho\"]]) if cols[\"rho\"] < len(row) else None\n m = (\n parse_number(row[mn_col])\n if mn_col is not None and mn_col < len(row)\n else None\n )\n if a is None and r is None:\n fully_blank = all(v is None or clean_text(v) == \"\" for v in row)\n if ab2 and fully_blank:\n # Tolerate an isolated blank spacer row inside the table -\n # field sheets routinely leave one at a Schlumberger MN segment\n # change. Only two consecutive fully-blank rows mark the true\n # end of the table, so the deep branch after a spacer is kept.\n blank_run += 1\n if blank_run >= 2:\n break\n continue\n if a is None or r is None:\n continue\n blank_run = 0\n if m is not None and mn_is_half:\n m = 2.0 * m\n ab2.append(a)\n mn.append(m if m is not None else np.nan)\n rho.append(r)\n\n if not ab2:\n return None\n\n sounding_id = str(fields.get(\"sounding_id\", \"\") or sheet_name or \"VES 1\")\n sounding = VESSounding(\n site=site,\n sounding_id=sounding_id if sounding_id else \"VES 1\",\n ab2=np.array(ab2),\n mn=np.array(mn),\n rho_app=np.array(rho),\n array_type=str(fields.get(\"array_type\", \"schlumberger\")).lower() or \"schlumberger\",\n instrument=fields.get(\"instrument\", \"\"),\n source=str(source),\n )\n\n # Data quality checks\n if np.any(sounding.rho_app <= 0):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"nonpositive_resistivity\",\n \"Apparent resistivity values must be positive.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n if np.any(np.diff(sounding.ab2) < 0):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"ab2_not_sorted\",\n \"AB/2 values are not in increasing order; check the sheet.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n finite_mn = sounding.mn[np.isfinite(sounding.mn)]\n if len(finite_mn) and np.any(sounding.ab2[np.isfinite(sounding.mn)] <= finite_mn / 2):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"mn_exceeds_ab\",\n \"MN/2 is not smaller than AB/2 for some readings.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n dup = _duplicate_ab2_count(sounding.ab2)\n if dup:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"segment_overlap\",\n f\"{dup} AB/2 value(s) repeated with different MN (segment changes); \"\n \"both readings kept.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n sounding.flags = flags\n return sounding\n\n\ndef _duplicate_ab2_count(ab2: np.ndarray) -> int:\n unique, counts = np.unique(ab2, return_counts=True)\n return int(np.sum(counts > 1))\n\n\ndef read_ves_workbook(path: str | Path) -> list[VESSounding]:\n \"\"\"Read every sounding in a VES workbook (one worksheet per sounding).\"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n soundings = []\n for name in common.sheet_names(path):\n grid, title = common.load_grid(path, sheet=name)\n sounding = _sounding_from_grid(grid, source=str(path), sheet_name=title)\n if sounding is not None:\n soundings.append(sounding)\n return soundings\n\n\ndef read_ves_csv(path: str | Path) -> VESSounding:\n \"\"\"Read a single sounding from CSV (same layout as one worksheet).\"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8-sig\") as fh:\n grid = [row for row in csv.reader(fh)]\n grid = [[cell if cell != \"\" else None for cell in row] for row in grid]\n sounding = _sounding_from_grid(grid, source=str(path), sheet_name=path.stem)\n if sounding is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No VES data table found in {path}\")\n return sounding\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/waterquality.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parser for water quality laboratory result sheets.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualityResult, WaterQualitySample\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n\ndef _find_results_header(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n if not t:\n continue\n if t.startswith(\"parameter\") or t.startswith(\"determinand\"):\n cols[\"parameter\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"unit\"):\n cols[\"unit\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"value\") or t.startswith(\"result\"):\n cols[\"value\"] = c\n elif \"detection\" in t or t == \"dl\":\n cols[\"dl\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"method\"):\n cols[\"method\"] = c\n if \"parameter\" in cols and \"value\" in cols:\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\ndef read_quality_workbook(path: str | Path) -> WaterQualitySample:\n grid, _ = common.load_grid(path)\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid)\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=str(path))\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n\n located = _find_results_header(grid)\n if located is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No results table (Parameter/Value) found in {path}\")\n header_row, cols = located\n\n results: list[WaterQualityResult] = []\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n def cell(key):\n c = cols.get(key)\n return row[c] if c is not None and c < len(row) else None\n\n parameter = clean_text(cell(\"parameter\"))\n if not parameter or parameter.lower().startswith(\"note\"):\n continue\n raw_value = cell(\"value\")\n text_value = clean_text(raw_value)\n below_detection = text_value.startswith(\"<\")\n value = parse_number(raw_value)\n dl = parse_number(cell(\"dl\"))\n if below_detection:\n # A \" Path:\n \"\"\"Write survey points as a WGS84 GeoJSON FeatureCollection.\n\n ``extra_properties`` maps point label to additional attribute\n dictionaries (for example layer tables or water zones).\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for p in points:\n lat, lon = utm_to_geographic(p.easting, p.northing, zone)\n props = {\n \"label\": p.label,\n \"kind\": p.kind,\n \"easting_utm\": p.easting,\n \"northing_utm\": p.northing,\n \"utm_zone\": f\"{zone}N\",\n }\n if p.value is not None:\n props[\"value\"] = p.value\n if extra_properties and p.label in extra_properties:\n props.update(extra_properties[p.label])\n features.append(\n {\n \"type\": \"Feature\",\n \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [round(lon, 6), round(lat, 6)]},\n \"properties\": props,\n }\n )\n collection = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}\n path = Path(path)\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n json.dump(collection, fh, indent=2)\n return path\n\n\ndef export_gpkg(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path,\n layer: str = \"survey_points\",\n) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Write survey points to a GeoPackage (requires geopandas).\"\"\"\n try:\n import geopandas as gpd\n from shapely.geometry import Point\n except ImportError as exc:\n raise ImportError(\n \"GeoPackage export needs geopandas; install with \"\n \"'pip install groundwater-toolkit[gis]' or use export_geojson()\"\n ) from exc\n\n records = []\n geometry = []\n for p in points:\n records.append(\n {\n \"label\": p.label,\n \"kind\": p.kind,\n \"value\": p.value,\n \"easting_utm\": p.easting,\n \"northing_utm\": p.northing,\n }\n )\n geometry.append(Point(p.easting, p.northing))\n epsg = 32600 + zone # WGS84 / UTM north\n gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(records, geometry=geometry, crs=f\"EPSG:{epsg}\")\n path = Path(path)\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n gdf.to_file(path, layer=layer, driver=\"GPKG\")\n return path\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/maps.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Publication-quality static maps without heavy GIS dependencies.\n\nMaps are drawn in projected UTM coordinates (metres), which keeps\nscale bars honest. Administrative or geological boundary layers can be\noverlaid from user-supplied GeoJSON files (in geographic WGS84\ncoordinates; they are projected on the fly). District boundary data\nfor Sierra Leone can be downloaded from GADM or HDX; the toolkit does\nnot bundle these datasets.\n\nEvery map gets a scale bar, north arrow, legend, coordinate grid and\nthe UTM zone note, per the house mapping rules.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.interpolate import griddata\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..geo import geographic_to_utm\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MapPoint:\n label: str\n easting: float\n northing: float\n value: float | None = None # attribute for interpolated maps\n kind: str = \"VES point\"\n\n\ndef _scale_bar(ax, style: HouseStyle) -> None:\n \"\"\"Draw a scale bar sized to a round number near 1/4 of the width.\"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n span = x1 - x0\n target = span / 4.0\n nice = 10 ** np.floor(np.log10(target))\n for mult in (5, 2, 1):\n if nice * mult <= target:\n nice *= mult\n break\n bx = x0 + span * 0.06\n by = y0 + (y1 - y0) * 0.05\n ax.plot([bx, bx + nice], [by, by], color=\"#222222\", lw=3, solid_capstyle=\"butt\")\n ax.plot([bx, bx + nice / 2], [by, by], color=\"white\", lw=1.4, solid_capstyle=\"butt\")\n label = f\"{nice / 1000:g} km\" if nice >= 1000 else f\"{nice:g} m\"\n ax.text(bx + nice / 2, by + (y1 - y0) * 0.015, label, ha=\"center\", fontsize=8)\n\n\ndef _north_arrow(ax) -> None:\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n x = x1 - (x1 - x0) * 0.07\n y = y1 - (y1 - y0) * 0.16\n dy = (y1 - y0) * 0.09\n ax.annotate(\n \"\", xy=(x, y + dy), xytext=(x, y),\n arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle=\"-|>\", color=\"#222222\", lw=1.6),\n )\n ax.text(x, y + dy * 1.15, \"N\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=10, fontweight=\"bold\")\n\n\ndef _plot_boundary(ax, geojson_path: str | Path, zone: int, color=\"#888888\") -> None:\n \"\"\"Overlay polygon/line features from a WGS84 GeoJSON file.\"\"\"\n with open(geojson_path, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n data = json.load(fh)\n features = data.get(\"features\", [data] if data.get(\"type\") == \"Feature\" else [])\n\n def draw_ring(ring):\n coords = np.array(\n [\n (geographic_to_utm(lat, lon, zone).easting,\n geographic_to_utm(lat, lon, zone).northing)\n for lon, lat in ring\n ]\n )\n ax.plot(coords[:, 0], coords[:, 1], color=color, lw=1.0)\n\n for feature in features:\n geom = feature.get(\"geometry\", {})\n gtype = geom.get(\"type\")\n coords = geom.get(\"coordinates\", [])\n if gtype == \"Polygon\":\n for ring in coords:\n draw_ring(ring)\n elif gtype == \"MultiPolygon\":\n for poly in coords:\n for ring in poly:\n draw_ring(ring)\n elif gtype == \"LineString\":\n draw_ring(coords)\n elif gtype == \"MultiLineString\":\n for line in coords:\n draw_ring(line)\n\n\ndef _format_grid(ax, zone: int) -> None:\n ax.ticklabel_format(style=\"plain\", useOffset=False)\n ax.tick_params(labelsize=7.5)\n for label in ax.get_yticklabels():\n label.set_rotation(90)\n label.set_va(\"center\")\n ax.set_xlabel(f\"Easting (m), UTM zone {zone}N / WGS84\", fontsize=8.5)\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Northing (m)\", fontsize=8.5)\n ax.grid(True, color=\"#CCCCCC\", lw=0.5)\n ax.set_aspect(\"equal\")\n\n\ndef _pad_limits(ax, points: list[MapPoint], pad_frac=0.25, min_pad=150.0) -> None:\n e = np.array([p.easting for p in points])\n n = np.array([p.northing for p in points])\n pe = max((e.max() - e.min()) * pad_frac, min_pad)\n pn = max((n.max() - n.min()) * pad_frac, min_pad)\n pad = max(pe, pn)\n ax.set_xlim(e.min() - pad, e.max() + pad)\n ax.set_ylim(n.min() - pad, n.max() + pad)\n\n\ndef site_location_map(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Site location map\",\n boundary_geojson: str | Path | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Survey point location map on a UTM grid.\"\"\"\n if not points:\n raise ValueError(\"site_location_map needs at least one survey point\")\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.4))\n _pad_limits(ax, points)\n if boundary_geojson:\n _plot_boundary(ax, boundary_geojson, zone)\n kinds = {}\n markers = {\"VES point\": \"o\", \"borehole\": \"^\", \"water point\": \"s\"}\n for p in points:\n marker = markers.get(p.kind, \"o\")\n handle, = ax.plot(\n p.easting, p.northing, marker, ms=8, mfc=style.secondary_color,\n mec=\"white\", mew=1.0, zorder=5,\n )\n kinds.setdefault(p.kind, handle)\n ax.annotate(\n p.label, xy=(p.easting, p.northing), xytext=(6, 6),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=8.5, fontweight=\"bold\",\n color=style.accent_color,\n )\n _format_grid(ax, zone)\n _scale_bar(ax, style)\n _north_arrow(ax)\n ax.legend(kinds.values(), kinds.keys(), loc=\"lower right\", fontsize=8)\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef _interpolated_map(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n title: str,\n cbar_label: str,\n path: str | Path | None,\n style: HouseStyle | None,\n log_scale: bool = False,\n cmap: str = \"viridis\",\n):\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n valued = [p for p in points if p.value is not None]\n if len(valued) < 3:\n raise ValueError(\n \"Interpolated maps need at least three points with values; \"\n f\"got {len(valued)}. Produce a site location map instead.\"\n )\n e = np.array([p.easting for p in valued])\n n = np.array([p.northing for p in valued])\n v = np.array([p.value for p in valued], dtype=float)\n if log_scale:\n v = np.log10(v)\n pad = max(max(e.max() - e.min(), n.max() - n.min()) * 0.25, 100.0)\n gx, gy = np.meshgrid(\n np.linspace(e.min() - pad, e.max() + pad, 220),\n np.linspace(n.min() - pad, n.max() + pad, 220),\n )\n grid_lin = griddata((e, n), v, (gx, gy), method=\"linear\")\n grid_near = griddata((e, n), v, (gx, gy), method=\"nearest\")\n grid = np.where(np.isnan(grid_lin), grid_near, grid_lin)\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.4))\n cs = ax.contourf(gx, gy, grid, levels=12, cmap=cmap, alpha=0.9)\n lines = ax.contour(gx, gy, grid, levels=cs.levels, colors=\"white\", linewidths=0.5)\n cbar = fig.colorbar(cs, ax=ax, pad=0.02, shrink=0.85)\n if log_scale:\n ticks = cbar.get_ticks()\n cbar.set_ticks(ticks)\n cbar.set_ticklabels([f\"{10**t:.0f}\" for t in ticks])\n cbar.set_label(cbar_label)\n for p in valued:\n ax.plot(p.easting, p.northing, \"o\", ms=7, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=\"#222222\", mew=1.2, zorder=5)\n ax.annotate(\n p.label, xy=(p.easting, p.northing), xytext=(6, 6),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=8.5, fontweight=\"bold\",\n color=\"#222222\",\n )\n ax.set_xlim(gx.min(), gx.max())\n ax.set_ylim(gy.min(), gy.max())\n _format_grid(ax, zone)\n _scale_bar(ax, style)\n _north_arrow(ax)\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef suitability_map(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Drill-target suitability\",\n):\n \"\"\"Drill-target suitability map from scored VES points.\n\n Each point carries its 0-100 suitability as ``value`` and its grade as\n ``kind``. Points are coloured red (poor) to green (good). With three or\n more points a suitability surface is interpolated, but it is masked to\n the convex hull of the surveyed points so it never extrapolates a\n drill-target confidence beyond where data actually exists.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n valued = [p for p in points if p.value is not None]\n if not points:\n raise ValueError(\"suitability_map needs at least one point\")\n cmap = plt.get_cmap(\"RdYlGn\")\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.4))\n _pad_limits(ax, points)\n if len(valued) >= 3:\n e = np.array([p.easting for p in valued])\n n = np.array([p.northing for p in valued])\n v = np.array([p.value for p in valued], dtype=float)\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n gx, gy = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(x0, x1, 200), np.linspace(y0, y1, 200))\n grid_lin = griddata((e, n), v, (gx, gy), method=\"linear\")\n grid_near = griddata((e, n), v, (gx, gy), method=\"nearest\")\n grid = np.where(np.isnan(grid_lin), grid_near, grid_lin)\n try:\n from matplotlib.path import Path as MplPath\n from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull\n\n hull = ConvexHull(np.column_stack([e, n]))\n poly = np.column_stack([e, n])[hull.vertices]\n inside = MplPath(poly).contains_points(\n np.column_stack([gx.ravel(), gy.ravel()])\n ).reshape(gx.shape)\n grid = np.where(inside, grid, np.nan)\n except Exception:\n pass # collinear points: show the unmasked surface\n cs = ax.contourf(\n gx, gy, grid, levels=np.linspace(0, 100, 11),\n cmap=cmap, alpha=0.75, vmin=0, vmax=100,\n )\n cbar = fig.colorbar(cs, ax=ax, pad=0.02, shrink=0.85)\n cbar.set_label(\"Drilling suitability (0-100)\")\n for p in points:\n colour = cmap(p.value / 100.0) if p.value is not None else \"#888888\"\n ax.plot(p.easting, p.northing, \"o\", ms=12, mfc=colour,\n mec=\"#222222\", mew=1.3, zorder=6)\n label = p.label + (f\"\\n{p.value:.0f} - {p.kind}\" if p.value is not None else \"\")\n ax.annotate(\n label, xy=(p.easting, p.northing), xytext=(9, 6),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=8.5, fontweight=\"bold\",\n color=\"#222222\", zorder=7,\n )\n _format_grid(ax, zone)\n _scale_bar(ax, style)\n _north_arrow(ax)\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef iso_resistivity_map(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n ab2: float,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Iso-apparent-resistivity map for one AB/2 spacing.\n\n ``points`` carry the apparent resistivity at that spacing as their\n value. Needs at least three sounding positions.\n \"\"\"\n return _interpolated_map(\n points,\n zone,\n title=f\"Iso-resistivity map at AB/2 = {ab2:g} m\",\n cbar_label=\"Apparent resistivity (ohm-m)\",\n path=path,\n style=style,\n log_scale=True,\n )\n\n\ndef overburden_thickness_map(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Overburden (depth to bedrock) thickness map from the VES models.\"\"\"\n return _interpolated_map(\n points,\n zone,\n title=\"Overburden thickness map\",\n cbar_label=\"Overburden thickness (m)\",\n path=path,\n style=style,\n log_scale=False,\n cmap=\"YlGnBu\",\n )\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/regional.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Regional context maps: geological setting and administrative location.\n\nBoth maps draw from real, freely licensed datasets bundled as package\ndata (see ``web/build_geodata.py`` for the reproducible preparation):\n\n- ``data/sl_geology_usgs.geojson``: the USGS Geologic Map of Africa\n (geo2_7g, Open-File Report 97-470A; public domain, 1:5,000,000\n scale) clipped to the Sierra Leone window, keeping the dataset's\n own unit codes, names, eras and colours.\n- ``data/sl_admin_geoboundaries.geojson``: national outline and\n district polygons from geoBoundaries (CC BY 4.0). The release\n predates the 2017 creation of Karene and Falaba districts.\n\nEvery figure carries the attribution of its sources. Both loaders\naccept a replacement GeoJSON path, so newer or survey grade data can\nbe dropped in without code changes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport math\nimport textwrap\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nfrom matplotlib.patches import PathPatch\nfrom matplotlib.path import Path as MplPath\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import SiteMetadata\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\n\nGEOLOGY_CREDIT = \"Geology: USGS Geologic Map of Africa (1:5M), public domain\"\nHYDRO_CREDIT = (\n \"Hydrogeology: BGS Africa Groundwater Atlas (OR/21/063), CC BY-SA 4.0\"\n)\nADMIN_CREDIT = (\n \"Boundaries: geoBoundaries, CC BY 4.0 (predates the 2017 \"\n \"Karene and Falaba districts)\"\n)\n\n# Order for the geology legend, oldest last.\n_ERA_ORDER = (\"Cenozoic\", \"Mesozoic\", \"Paleozoic\", \"Precambrian\", \"Non-geological\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass GeologyUnit:\n \"\"\"One polygon of the geological map.\"\"\"\n\n glg: str # USGS unit code, e.g. \"pCm\"\n unit: str # unit name from the dataset, e.g. \"Precambrian\"\n era: str\n color: str\n ring: np.ndarray # (n, 2) lon/lat outer ring\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass AdminArea:\n level: str # \"ADM0\" | \"ADM2\" | \"ADM3\"\n name: str\n rings: list[np.ndarray] = field(default_factory=list)\n district: str = \"\" # parent district, for ADM3 chiefdoms\n # interior rings per part, aligned with ``rings``. Only the point tests\n # use them: Nongowa encloses Kenema Town, and ignoring the hole labelled\n # every site in the town with the rural chiefdom around it.\n holes: list[list[np.ndarray]] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def label_point(self) -> tuple[float, float]:\n \"\"\"Centroid of the largest ring (shoelace).\"\"\"\n best = max(self.rings, key=lambda r: abs(_ring_area(r)))\n return _ring_centroid(best)\n\n\ndef _ring_area(ring: np.ndarray) -> float:\n x, y = ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1]\n return 0.5 * float(np.sum(x[:-1] * y[1:] - x[1:] * y[:-1]))\n\n\ndef _ring_centroid(ring: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float]:\n x, y = ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1]\n cross = x[:-1] * y[1:] - x[1:] * y[:-1]\n area = np.sum(cross) / 2.0\n if abs(area) < 1e-12:\n return float(x.mean()), float(y.mean())\n cx = np.sum((x[:-1] + x[1:]) * cross) / (6.0 * area)\n cy = np.sum((y[:-1] + y[1:]) * cross) / (6.0 * area)\n return float(cx), float(cy)\n\n\ndef _read_geojson(name: str, path: str | Path | None) -> dict:\n if path is not None:\n text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n else:\n text = (resources.files(\"groundwater\") / \"data\" / name).read_text(\n encoding=\"utf-8\"\n )\n return json.loads(text)\n\n\ndef load_geology(path: str | Path | None = None) -> list[GeologyUnit]:\n \"\"\"The USGS geology polygons for the Sierra Leone window.\"\"\"\n data = _read_geojson(\"sl_geology_usgs.geojson\", path)\n units: list[GeologyUnit] = []\n for feature in data.get(\"features\", []):\n props = feature.get(\"properties\", {})\n geom = feature.get(\"geometry\", {})\n polys = (\n geom[\"coordinates\"]\n if geom.get(\"type\") == \"MultiPolygon\"\n else [geom.get(\"coordinates\", [])]\n )\n for poly in polys:\n if not poly:\n continue\n units.append(\n GeologyUnit(\n glg=props.get(\"glg\", \"\"),\n unit=props.get(\"unit\", props.get(\"glg\", \"unit\")),\n era=props.get(\"era\", \"\"),\n color=props.get(\"color\", \"#CCCCCC\"),\n ring=np.asarray(poly[0], dtype=float),\n )\n )\n return units\n\n\ndef load_hydrogeology(path: str | Path | None = None) -> list[GeologyUnit]:\n \"\"\"The BGS aquifer type and productivity polygons.\n\n Returned as :class:`GeologyUnit` items: ``glg`` carries the BGS\n combined code (for example ``B-L``), ``unit`` the readable label\n and ``era`` the underlying geology class.\n \"\"\"\n data = _read_geojson(\"sl_hydrogeology_bgs.geojson\", path)\n units: list[GeologyUnit] = []\n for feature in data.get(\"features\", []):\n props = feature.get(\"properties\", {})\n geom = feature.get(\"geometry\", {})\n polys = (\n geom[\"coordinates\"]\n if geom.get(\"type\") == \"MultiPolygon\"\n else [geom.get(\"coordinates\", [])]\n )\n for poly in polys:\n if not poly:\n continue\n units.append(\n GeologyUnit(\n glg=props.get(\"code\", \"\"),\n unit=props.get(\"unit\", \"unit\"),\n era=props.get(\"geology\", \"\"),\n color=props.get(\"color\", \"#CCCCCC\"),\n ring=np.asarray(poly[0], dtype=float),\n )\n )\n return units\n\n\ndef load_admin(path: str | Path | None = None) -> tuple[AdminArea, list[AdminArea]]:\n \"\"\"The national outline and the district polygons.\"\"\"\n data = _read_geojson(\"sl_admin_geoboundaries.geojson\", path)\n outline: AdminArea | None = None\n districts: list[AdminArea] = []\n for feature in data.get(\"features\", []):\n props = feature.get(\"properties\", {})\n geom = feature.get(\"geometry\", {})\n polys = (\n geom[\"coordinates\"]\n if geom.get(\"type\") == \"MultiPolygon\"\n else [geom.get(\"coordinates\", [])]\n )\n area = AdminArea(\n level=props.get(\"level\", \"ADM2\"),\n name=props.get(\"name\", \"\"),\n rings=[np.asarray(p[0], dtype=float) for p in polys if p],\n )\n if area.level == \"ADM0\":\n outline = area\n else:\n districts.append(area)\n if outline is None:\n raise ValueError(\"admin dataset has no ADM0 outline feature\")\n return outline, districts\n\n\ndef _point_in_ring(lon: float, lat: float, ring: np.ndarray) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Ray casting point-in-polygon test.\"\"\"\n inside = False\n for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(ring[:-1], ring[1:]):\n if (y1 > lat) != (y2 > lat):\n x_cross = x1 + (lat - y1) * (x2 - x1) / (y2 - y1)\n if lon < x_cross:\n inside = not inside\n return inside\n\n\ndef district_of(\n lat: float, lon: float, admin_path: str | Path | None = None\n) -> str:\n \"\"\"The district containing a point, from the boundary polygons.\n\n Returns an empty string when the point falls outside every\n district (offshore, across the border, or wrong coordinates).\n \"\"\"\n _, districts = load_admin(admin_path)\n for district in districts:\n for ring in district.rings:\n if _point_in_ring(lon, lat, ring):\n return district.name\n return \"\"\n\n\ndef load_chiefdoms(path: str | Path | None = None) -> list[AdminArea]:\n \"\"\"The chiefdom (ADM3) polygons, each carrying its parent district.\n\n From geoBoundaries (gbOpen, CC BY 4.0), simplified for bundling.\n \"\"\"\n data = _read_geojson(\"sl_chiefdoms_geoboundaries.geojson\", path)\n areas: list[AdminArea] = []\n for feature in data.get(\"features\", []):\n props = feature.get(\"properties\", {})\n geom = feature.get(\"geometry\", {})\n polys = (\n geom[\"coordinates\"]\n if geom.get(\"type\") == \"MultiPolygon\"\n else [geom.get(\"coordinates\", [])]\n )\n rings = [np.asarray(p[0], dtype=float) for p in polys if p]\n holes = [\n [np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in p[1:]] for p in polys if p\n ]\n if rings:\n areas.append(\n AdminArea(\n level=\"ADM3\",\n name=props.get(\"name\", \"\"),\n rings=rings,\n district=props.get(\"district\", \"\"),\n holes=holes,\n )\n )\n return areas\n\n\ndef chiefdom_of(\n lat: float, lon: float, path: str | Path | None = None\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"The chiefdom and its district containing a point.\n\n Returns ``(chiefdom, district)`` or ``(\"\", \"\")`` when the point falls\n outside every chiefdom.\n \"\"\"\n for area in load_chiefdoms(path):\n for i, ring in enumerate(area.rings):\n if not _point_in_ring(lon, lat, ring):\n continue\n inner = area.holes[i] if i < len(area.holes) else []\n if any(_point_in_ring(lon, lat, hole) for hole in inner):\n continue # inside an enclave: it belongs to the chiefdom there\n return area.name, area.district\n return \"\", \"\"\n\n\ndef _site_lonlat(site: SiteMetadata) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n latlon = site.latlon\n if latlon is None:\n return None\n lat, lon = latlon\n return lon, lat\n\n\ndef _mask_outside_country(ax, outline: AdminArea, style: HouseStyle) -> None:\n \"\"\"White out everything beyond the national boundary.\n\n A compound path (a large rectangle with the country rings as\n holes, even-odd filled) hides the neighbouring countries' geology\n without needing polygon clipping.\n \"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n pad = 2.0\n rect = np.array(\n [\n [x0 - pad, y0 - pad], [x1 + pad, y0 - pad],\n [x1 + pad, y1 + pad], [x0 - pad, y1 + pad],\n [x0 - pad, y0 - pad],\n ]\n )\n vertices = [rect] # counter-clockwise outer rectangle\n codes = [\n [MplPath.MOVETO] + [MplPath.LINETO] * (len(rect) - 2) + [MplPath.CLOSEPOLY]\n ]\n for ring in outline.rings:\n # holes must wind opposite to the outer ring or they fill solid\n hole = ring[::-1] if _ring_area(ring) > 0 else ring\n vertices.append(hole)\n codes.append(\n [MplPath.MOVETO] + [MplPath.LINETO] * (len(hole) - 2) + [MplPath.CLOSEPOLY]\n )\n compound = MplPath(\n np.concatenate(vertices), np.concatenate(codes).tolist()\n )\n ax.add_patch(\n PathPatch(compound, facecolor=style.background, edgecolor=\"none\", zorder=4)\n )\n\n\ndef _geo_axes_finish(ax, mean_lat: float, credit: str) -> None:\n \"\"\"Aspect, scale bar, north arrow, grid and attribution.\"\"\"\n ax.set_aspect(1.0 / math.cos(math.radians(mean_lat)))\n ax.grid(True, color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.5)\n ax.tick_params(labelsize=7.5)\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Longitude\", fontsize=8.5)\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Latitude\", fontsize=8.5)\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n km_per_deg = 111.32 * math.cos(math.radians(mean_lat))\n span_km = (x1 - x0) * km_per_deg\n target = span_km / 4.0\n nice = 10 ** math.floor(math.log10(target)) if target > 0 else 1.0\n for mult in (5, 2, 1):\n if nice * mult <= target:\n nice *= mult\n break\n bar_deg = nice / km_per_deg\n bx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * 0.06\n by = y0 + (y1 - y0) * 0.05\n ax.plot([bx, bx + bar_deg], [by, by], color=\"#222222\", lw=3,\n solid_capstyle=\"butt\", zorder=9)\n ax.plot([bx, bx + bar_deg / 2], [by, by], color=\"white\", lw=1.4,\n solid_capstyle=\"butt\", zorder=9)\n ax.text(bx + bar_deg / 2, by + (y1 - y0) * 0.018, f\"{nice:g} km\",\n ha=\"center\", fontsize=8, zorder=9)\n nx = x1 - (x1 - x0) * 0.07\n ny = y1 - (y1 - y0) * 0.16\n dy = (y1 - y0) * 0.09\n ax.annotate(\"\", xy=(nx, ny + dy), xytext=(nx, ny),\n arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle=\"-|>\", color=\"#222222\", lw=1.6))\n ax.text(nx, ny + dy * 1.15, \"N\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=10,\n fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(0.99, 0.005, credit, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=6.0,\n ha=\"right\", va=\"bottom\", color=\"#888888\", style=\"italic\",\n zorder=9)\n\n\ndef _mark_site(ax, site: SiteMetadata, color: str) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n lonlat = _site_lonlat(site)\n if lonlat is None:\n return None\n lon, lat = lonlat\n ax.plot(lon, lat, marker=\"*\", ms=16, mfc=color, mec=\"white\", mew=1.2,\n zorder=8)\n ax.annotate(site.community or \"Site\", xy=(lon, lat), xytext=(8, 8),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=9, fontweight=\"bold\",\n color=color, zorder=8)\n return lonlat\n\n\ndef _plot_units_map(\n units: list[GeologyUnit],\n credit: str,\n legend_title: str,\n scope_word: str,\n site: SiteMetadata | None,\n path: str | Path | None,\n style: HouseStyle | None,\n radius_km: float | None,\n admin_path: str | Path | None,\n title: str | None,\n label_with_code: bool,\n):\n \"\"\"Shared renderer for the unit-coloured maps (geology, hydrogeology).\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n outline, _ = load_admin(admin_path)\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.6))\n legend_handles: dict[str, PathPatch] = {}\n legend_order: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {}\n for unit in units:\n patch = plt.Polygon(\n unit.ring, closed=True, facecolor=unit.color,\n edgecolor=\"#666666\", lw=0.4, zorder=2,\n )\n ax.add_patch(patch)\n label = (\n f\"{unit.unit} ({unit.glg})\" if label_with_code and unit.glg\n else unit.unit\n )\n legend_handles.setdefault(label, patch)\n era_rank = (\n _ERA_ORDER.index(unit.era) if unit.era in _ERA_ORDER else 99\n )\n legend_order.setdefault(label, (era_rank, unit.glg))\n\n site_lonlat = _mark_site(ax, site, \"#C1272D\") if site else None\n if radius_km and site_lonlat is not None:\n lon, lat = site_lonlat\n dlat = radius_km / 111.32\n dlon = radius_km / (111.32 * math.cos(math.radians(lat)))\n ax.set_xlim(lon - dlon, lon + dlon)\n ax.set_ylim(lat - dlat, lat + dlat)\n else:\n all_pts = np.concatenate(outline.rings)\n ax.set_xlim(all_pts[:, 0].min() - 0.15, all_pts[:, 0].max() + 0.15)\n ax.set_ylim(all_pts[:, 1].min() - 0.12, all_pts[:, 1].max() + 0.12)\n\n _mask_outside_country(ax, outline, style)\n for ring in outline.rings:\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.1, zorder=5)\n\n mean_lat = float(np.mean(ax.get_ylim()))\n _geo_axes_finish(ax, mean_lat, f\"{credit}. {ADMIN_CREDIT}\")\n ordered = sorted(legend_handles, key=lambda k: legend_order[k])\n # legend outside the axes so it never covers the map; the tight\n # bounding box at save time grows the canvas around it\n ax.legend(\n [legend_handles[k] for k in ordered],\n [textwrap.fill(k, 24) for k in ordered],\n loc=\"upper left\", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),\n fontsize=6.5, framealpha=0.95, borderaxespad=0.0,\n title=textwrap.fill(legend_title, 24), title_fontsize=7.5,\n )\n if title is None:\n where = (site.community or \"the site\") if site else \"Sierra Leone\"\n scope = (\n f\"Local {scope_word.lower()} setting\" if radius_km\n else f\"{scope_word} map\"\n )\n title = f\"{scope} - {where}\" if site else f\"{scope} of Sierra Leone\"\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_geological_map(\n site: SiteMetadata | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n radius_km: float | None = None,\n geology_path: str | Path | None = None,\n admin_path: str | Path | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Geological map from the USGS data, national or zoomed to the site.\n\n ``radius_km`` zooms to a window around the site (local geological\n setting); leave it ``None`` for the national map.\n \"\"\"\n return _plot_units_map(\n load_geology(geology_path),\n GEOLOGY_CREDIT,\n \"Geological units (USGS)\",\n \"Geological\",\n site, path, style, radius_km, admin_path, title,\n label_with_code=True,\n )\n\n\ndef plot_hydrogeology_map(\n site: SiteMetadata | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n radius_km: float | None = None,\n hydro_path: str | Path | None = None,\n admin_path: str | Path | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Aquifer type and productivity map from the BGS Atlas data.\"\"\"\n return _plot_units_map(\n load_hydrogeology(hydro_path),\n HYDRO_CREDIT,\n \"Aquifer type and productivity (BGS)\",\n \"Hydrogeological\",\n site, path, style, radius_km, admin_path, title,\n label_with_code=False,\n )\n\n\ndef plot_portfolio_map(\n points: list[dict],\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n admin_path: str | Path | None = None,\n title: str = \"Borehole portfolio\",\n):\n \"\"\"National map of all boreholes coloured by status.\n\n ``points`` are dicts ``{label, lat, lon, status}`` as produced by\n :func:`groundwater.portfolio.portfolio_points`.\n \"\"\"\n from ..portfolio import STATUS_COLORS, STATUS_LABELS\n\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n outline, districts = load_admin(admin_path)\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.8))\n for district in districts:\n for ring in district.rings:\n ax.add_patch(\n plt.Polygon(ring, closed=True, facecolor=\"#F2F6FA\",\n edgecolor=\"#8FA6B8\", lw=0.7, zorder=2)\n )\n for ring in outline.rings:\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.2, zorder=5)\n handles: dict[str, object] = {}\n for point in points:\n status = point.get(\"status\", \"other\")\n colour = STATUS_COLORS.get(status, STATUS_COLORS[\"other\"])\n handle, = ax.plot(\n point[\"lon\"], point[\"lat\"], \"o\", ms=8, mfc=colour,\n mec=\"white\", mew=1.0, zorder=7,\n )\n handles.setdefault(status, handle)\n ax.text(-11.2, 9.82, \"GUINEA\", fontsize=8, color=\"#999999\", fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(-10.95, 7.15, \"LIBERIA\", fontsize=8, color=\"#999999\", fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(-13.25, 7.45, \"Atlantic\\nOcean\", fontsize=8, color=\"#7FA8C9\",\n style=\"italic\", ha=\"center\")\n all_pts = np.concatenate(outline.rings)\n ax.set_xlim(all_pts[:, 0].min() - 0.2, all_pts[:, 0].max() + 0.15)\n ax.set_ylim(all_pts[:, 1].min() - 0.15, all_pts[:, 1].max() + 0.12)\n _geo_axes_finish(ax, float(np.mean(ax.get_ylim())), ADMIN_CREDIT)\n if handles:\n ax.legend(\n list(handles.values()),\n [STATUS_LABELS.get(s, s) for s in handles],\n loc=\"lower right\", fontsize=7, framealpha=0.95,\n )\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_admin_map(\n site: SiteMetadata | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n admin_path: str | Path | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Administrative location map from the geoBoundaries polygons.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n outline, districts = load_admin(admin_path)\n highlight = (site.district or \"\").strip().lower() if site else \"\"\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.6))\n for district in districts:\n is_home = district.name.strip().lower() == highlight\n for ring in district.rings:\n ax.add_patch(\n plt.Polygon(\n ring, closed=True,\n facecolor=style.accent_color if is_home else \"#F2F6FA\",\n alpha=0.35 if is_home else 1.0,\n edgecolor=\"#8FA6B8\", lw=0.7, zorder=2,\n )\n )\n lx, ly = district.label_point\n ax.annotate(\n district.name, xy=(lx, ly), ha=\"center\", va=\"center\",\n fontsize=7.5 if is_home else 6.5,\n fontweight=\"bold\" if is_home else \"normal\",\n color=style.accent_color if is_home else \"#555555\",\n zorder=6,\n )\n for ring in outline.rings:\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.2, zorder=5)\n if site is not None:\n _mark_site(ax, site, \"#C1272D\")\n ax.text(-11.2, 9.82, \"GUINEA\", fontsize=8, color=\"#999999\",\n fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(-10.95, 7.15, \"LIBERIA\", fontsize=8, color=\"#999999\",\n fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(-13.25, 7.45, \"Atlantic\\nOcean\", fontsize=8, color=\"#7FA8C9\",\n style=\"italic\", ha=\"center\")\n all_pts = np.concatenate(outline.rings)\n ax.set_xlim(all_pts[:, 0].min() - 0.2, all_pts[:, 0].max() + 0.15)\n ax.set_ylim(all_pts[:, 1].min() - 0.15, all_pts[:, 1].max() + 0.12)\n mean_lat = float(np.mean(ax.get_ylim()))\n _geo_axes_finish(ax, mean_lat, ADMIN_CREDIT)\n if title is None:\n title = (\n f\"Location map - {site.community}\"\n + (f\", {site.district} District\" if site.district else \"\")\n if site and site.community\n else \"Administrative map of Sierra Leone\"\n )\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_coverage_choropleth(\n chiefdom_values: dict[str, float],\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n chiefdom_path: str | Path | None = None,\n admin_path: str | Path | None = None,\n title: str = \"Water coverage gap by district\",\n legend_label: str = \"People per functional water point\",\n credit: str = ADMIN_CREDIT,\n group_labels: dict[str, str] | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Choropleth of unmet water need, one colour per chiefdom polygon.\n\n Each chiefdom polygon is filled by ``chiefdom_values[name]``. Warmer =\n worse; ``None`` is drawn grey (no data) and an infinite value dark (no\n functional source). For the district view, pass district values expanded\n onto every chiefdom (see ``coverage.expand_district_values``) with\n ``group_labels`` mapping each chiefdom to its district, so the district\n names are annotated once at their centroid; for the chiefdom view, omit\n ``group_labels`` (166 labels would be unreadable).\n \"\"\"\n from matplotlib.cm import ScalarMappable\n from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, Normalize\n\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n outline, _ = load_admin(admin_path)\n areas = load_chiefdoms(chiefdom_path)\n finite = [\n v for v in chiefdom_values.values() if v is not None and math.isfinite(v)\n ]\n norm = Normalize(min(finite), max(finite)) if finite else Normalize(0.0, 1.0)\n cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(\n \"unmet_need\", [\"#FBF1E9\", style.secondary_color]\n )\n no_data = \"#E9E9E9\"\n no_source = \"#5A1A12\" # dark laterite: no functional source mapped\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.8))\n label_pts: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = {}\n for area in areas:\n value = chiefdom_values.get(area.name)\n if value is None:\n face = no_data\n elif not math.isfinite(value):\n face = no_source\n else:\n face = cmap(norm(value))\n for ring in area.rings:\n ax.add_patch(\n plt.Polygon(ring, closed=True, facecolor=face,\n edgecolor=\"#8FA6B8\", lw=0.3, zorder=2)\n )\n group = group_labels.get(area.name) if group_labels else None\n if group:\n label_pts.setdefault(group, []).append(area.label_point)\n for ring in outline.rings:\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.2, zorder=5)\n for district, pts in label_pts.items():\n lx = sum(p[0] for p in pts) / len(pts)\n ly = sum(p[1] for p in pts) / len(pts)\n ax.annotate(district, xy=(lx, ly), ha=\"center\", va=\"center\",\n fontsize=6.0, color=\"#222222\", fontweight=\"bold\",\n zorder=6)\n ax.text(-11.2, 9.82, \"GUINEA\", fontsize=8, color=\"#999999\",\n fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(-10.95, 7.15, \"LIBERIA\", fontsize=8, color=\"#999999\",\n fontweight=\"bold\")\n ax.text(-13.25, 7.45, \"Atlantic\\nOcean\", fontsize=8, color=\"#7FA8C9\",\n style=\"italic\", ha=\"center\")\n all_pts = np.concatenate(outline.rings)\n ax.set_xlim(all_pts[:, 0].min() - 0.2, all_pts[:, 0].max() + 0.15)\n ax.set_ylim(all_pts[:, 1].min() - 0.15, all_pts[:, 1].max() + 0.12)\n _geo_axes_finish(ax, float(np.mean(ax.get_ylim())), credit)\n mappable = ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap)\n mappable.set_array([])\n fig.colorbar(mappable, ax=ax, shrink=0.6, label=legend_label)\n # legend keys for the two out-of-ramp classes, so a reader can tell the\n # dark districts are the worst case (no source), not the ramp maximum\n from matplotlib.patches import Patch\n\n ax.legend(\n handles=[\n Patch(facecolor=no_source, edgecolor=\"#8FA6B8\",\n label=\"No functional source\"),\n Patch(facecolor=no_data, edgecolor=\"#8FA6B8\", label=\"No data\"),\n ],\n loc=\"lower right\", fontsize=7, framealpha=0.95,\n )\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/models.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Core data structures shared across the toolkit.\n\nEvery parser returns one of these objects and every analysis module\nconsumes them, so the raw-data-to-report chain stays traceable: each\nobject keeps a ``source`` path and parsers attach ``flags`` describing\nanything that needs analyst attention (missing discharge, inconsistent\nmetadata, negative drawdown and so on).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom .geo import UTMCoordinate, infer_zone_for_sierra_leone, utm_to_geographic\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Flags raised during parsing and checking\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass DataFlag:\n \"\"\"A data quality or consistency issue that needs analyst review.\"\"\"\n\n level: str # \"info\" | \"warning\" | \"error\"\n code: str # short machine readable code, e.g. \"missing_discharge\"\n message: str # human readable explanation\n context: str = \"\" # e.g. \"VES 2\", \"step 3\"\n\n def __str__(self) -> str:\n prefix = f\"[{self.level.upper()}] {self.code}\"\n ctx = f\" ({self.context})\" if self.context else \"\"\n return f\"{prefix}{ctx}: {self.message}\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Site metadata\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass SiteMetadata:\n \"\"\"Header block information shared by all field sheets.\"\"\"\n\n client: str = \"\"\n project: str = \"\"\n community: str = \"\"\n chiefdom: str = \"\"\n district: str = \"\"\n country: str = \"Sierra Leone\"\n project_ref: str = \"\"\n easting: Optional[float] = None\n northing: Optional[float] = None\n utm_zone: Optional[int] = None\n elevation_m: Optional[float] = None\n date: str = \"\"\n supervisor: str = \"\"\n contractor: str = \"\"\n source: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def utm(self) -> Optional[UTMCoordinate]:\n if self.easting is None or self.northing is None:\n return None\n # A fixed fallback puts half the country in the Atlantic: the two\n # zones are 6 degrees (about 660 km) apart. The easting alone\n # identifies the zone in Sierra Leone, so infer it rather than guess.\n zone = self.utm_zone or infer_zone_for_sierra_leone(self.easting)\n return UTMCoordinate(self.easting, self.northing, zone)\n\n @property\n def latlon(self) -> Optional[tuple[float, float]]:\n utm = self.utm\n if utm is None:\n return None\n return utm_to_geographic(utm.easting, utm.northing, utm.zone)\n\n def merged_with(self, other: \"SiteMetadata\") -> \"SiteMetadata\":\n \"\"\"Fill blank fields from another metadata record.\n\n A field is \"blank\" only when it is None or an empty string. A genuine\n numeric zero - a sea-level elevation, or a zero UTM ordinate - counts\n as present and is never overwritten, so merging two records does not\n lose a real 0.0 datum.\n \"\"\"\n merged = SiteMetadata(**self.__dict__)\n for key, value in other.__dict__.items():\n current = getattr(merged, key)\n if (current is None or current == \"\") and value not in (None, \"\"):\n setattr(merged, key, value)\n return merged\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# VES\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass VESSounding:\n \"\"\"A single vertical electrical sounding.\n\n ``mn`` stores the full potential electrode spacing MN (not MN/2),\n matching the field sheets. Duplicate ``ab2`` values with different\n ``mn`` mark Schlumberger segment changes and are preserved.\n \"\"\"\n\n site: SiteMetadata\n sounding_id: str\n ab2: np.ndarray # AB/2 in metres\n mn: np.ndarray # full MN spacing in metres\n rho_app: np.ndarray # apparent resistivity, ohm-m\n array_type: str = \"schlumberger\"\n instrument: str = \"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.ab2 = np.asarray(self.ab2, dtype=float)\n self.mn = np.asarray(self.mn, dtype=float)\n self.rho_app = np.asarray(self.rho_app, dtype=float)\n # The array type decides which forward model is used, and the\n # inversion and forward code match it with a bare startswith().\n # \"Wenner\" from a hand-built sounding or a scanned sheet would\n # otherwise be inverted as Schlumberger - silently wrong by tens\n # of percent - so normalise it once, here.\n self.array_type = str(self.array_type or \"schlumberger\").strip().lower()\n\n @property\n def n_readings(self) -> int:\n return len(self.ab2)\n\n @property\n def label(self) -> str:\n return self.sounding_id or \"VES\"\n\n def segments(self) -> list[np.ndarray]:\n \"\"\"Indices of readings grouped by MN spacing, in field order.\n\n A new segment starts at each change of MN spacing. A blank/NaN MN is\n treated as a continuation of the current segment (its spacing is\n unknown, carried forward from the last real value) rather than\n starting a new one, so a single missing MN cell does not inject a\n spurious one-point segment and an absent MN column does not split\n every reading into its own segment.\n \"\"\"\n out: list[list[int]] = []\n last_mn: float | None = None\n for idx, mn in enumerate(self.mn):\n is_nan = mn != mn # NaN is the only value not equal to itself\n new_segment = not out or (\n not is_nan and last_mn is not None and mn != last_mn\n )\n if new_segment:\n out.append([])\n out[-1].append(idx)\n if not is_nan:\n last_mn = mn\n return [np.array(g, dtype=int) for g in out]\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass LayeredModel:\n \"\"\"A 1D layered earth model (the IPI2Win style result).\n\n ``thicknesses`` has one entry fewer than ``resistivities``; the\n last layer is the half-space (its thickness is infinite).\n \"\"\"\n\n resistivities: np.ndarray # ohm-m, length n\n thicknesses: np.ndarray # m, length n-1\n fit_error_percent: Optional[float] = None # RMS misfit, like IPI2Win ERR\n method: str = \"\" # \"ipi2win-import\" | \"damped-lsq\" | ...\n sounding_id: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.resistivities = np.asarray(self.resistivities, dtype=float)\n self.thicknesses = np.asarray(self.thicknesses, dtype=float)\n if len(self.thicknesses) != len(self.resistivities) - 1:\n raise ValueError(\n \"thicknesses must have exactly one entry fewer than resistivities\"\n )\n\n @property\n def n_layers(self) -> int:\n return len(self.resistivities)\n\n @property\n def depths_top(self) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Depth to the top of each layer (first entry 0).\"\"\"\n return np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(self.thicknesses)])\n\n @property\n def depths_bottom(self) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Depth to the bottom of each layer (last entry inf).\"\"\"\n return np.concatenate([np.cumsum(self.thicknesses), [np.inf]])\n\n def as_table(self) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Rows in the IPI2Win layout: N, rho, h, z (depth to top).\"\"\"\n rows = []\n tops = self.depths_top\n for i in range(self.n_layers):\n h = self.thicknesses[i] if i < len(self.thicknesses) else None\n z = \"0/0\" if i == 0 else tops[i]\n rows.append(\n {\n \"N\": i + 1,\n \"rho_ohm_m\": float(self.resistivities[i]),\n \"h_m\": None if h is None else float(h),\n \"z_m\": z,\n }\n )\n return rows\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Pumping test\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass PumpingStep:\n \"\"\"One step of a step-drawdown or constant discharge test.\"\"\"\n\n step_number: int\n time_min: np.ndarray # minutes since the start of the whole test\n water_level_m: np.ndarray # depth to water below datum\n discharge_m3_per_h: Optional[float] = None # None when missing on sheet\n label: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.time_min = np.asarray(self.time_min, dtype=float)\n self.water_level_m = np.asarray(self.water_level_m, dtype=float)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass PumpingTest:\n \"\"\"A pumping test record built from the field sheet.\n\n The field sheets record an incremental \"drawdown\" column (change\n between successive readings). Parsers keep only time and water\n level; true drawdown below static is always recomputed here.\n \"\"\"\n\n site: SiteMetadata\n borehole_ref: str = \"\"\n test_type: str = \"step\" # \"step\" | \"constant\" | \"constant+recovery\"\n static_water_level_m: Optional[float] = None\n borehole_depth_m: Optional[float] = None\n pump_setting_m: Optional[float] = None\n step_length_min: Optional[float] = None\n steps: list[PumpingStep] = field(default_factory=list)\n recovery_time_min: Optional[np.ndarray] = None # minutes since pump stop\n recovery_level_m: Optional[np.ndarray] = None\n pumping_duration_min: Optional[float] = None # total pumping before recovery\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def has_discharge(self) -> bool:\n return any(s.discharge_m3_per_h is not None for s in self.steps)\n\n def drawdown(self, step: PumpingStep) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"True drawdown below static water level, metres.\"\"\"\n if self.static_water_level_m is None:\n raise ValueError(\"static water level is required to compute drawdown\")\n return step.water_level_m - self.static_water_level_m\n\n def all_times_levels(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n \"\"\"Concatenated pumping phase time series.\"\"\"\n t = np.concatenate([s.time_min for s in self.steps]) if self.steps else np.array([])\n wl = (\n np.concatenate([s.water_level_m for s in self.steps])\n if self.steps\n else np.array([])\n )\n order = np.argsort(t, kind=\"stable\")\n return t[order], wl[order]\n\n def residual_drawdown(self) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:\n if self.recovery_level_m is None or self.static_water_level_m is None:\n return None\n return self.recovery_level_m - self.static_water_level_m\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Drilling log\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass LithologyInterval:\n top_m: float\n bottom_m: float\n description: str = \"\"\n from_time: str = \"\"\n to_time: str = \"\"\n penetration_rate_m_per_min: Optional[float] = None\n bit_diameter_in: Optional[float] = None\n\n @property\n def thickness_m(self) -> float:\n return self.bottom_m - self.top_m\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass DrillingLog:\n site: SiteMetadata\n borehole_ref: str = \"\"\n total_depth_m: Optional[float] = None\n drilling_method: str = \"\"\n intervals: list[LithologyInterval] = field(default_factory=list)\n water_strikes_m: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)\n grouting_depth_m: Optional[float] = None\n start_date: str = \"\"\n completion_date: str = \"\"\n status: str = \"\" # e.g. \"Successful\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Water quality\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterQualityResult:\n parameter: str\n value: Optional[float]\n unit: str = \"\"\n detection_limit: Optional[float] = None\n below_detection: bool = False\n method: str = \"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterQualitySample:\n site: SiteMetadata\n sample_id: str = \"\"\n borehole_ref: str = \"\"\n sample_date: str = \"\"\n laboratory: str = \"\"\n results: list[WaterQualityResult] = field(default_factory=list)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n def get(self, parameter: str) -> Optional[WaterQualityResult]:\n key = parameter.strip().lower()\n for r in self.results:\n if r.parameter.strip().lower() == key:\n return r\n return None\n"}, "groundwater/planning.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Coverage as a planning figure rather than an archive figure.\n\nThe coverage-gap view divides a district's population by the number of\nfunctional water points in it. Both halves of that fraction are older than\nthey look, and the ranking it produces is used to decide where next year's\nboreholes go.\n\n**The population is from 2015.** Sierra Leone's census is a decade old.\nDividing today's need by a decade-old population understates it everywhere,\nand quoting a figure as \"people per water point\" without saying which year's\npeople is how a planning number becomes a wrong number nobody notices.\nProjection does not, on its own, change the *ranking* - a single national\nrate is a uniform multiplier and leaves the order untouched - so the value\nhere is in the magnitudes being current and in the year being stated. Where\na programme has district rates, entering them is what makes the ranking\nmove, and it should: Western Area Urban does not grow at the rural rate.\n\n**The water points were surveyed on various dates.** A point reported\nfunctional in 2016 is evidence about 2016. Treating it as a working source\ntoday counts a supply that may have been broken for years, which is exactly\nthe direction that hides an unserved population. So freshness is measured\nand reported, and coverage is offered over recent surveys as well as over\nall of them - the gap between the two is the size of the assumption.\n\n**A point that dries up is not a water point in the dry season.** Where the\nsurvey recorded how many months of the year a source yields water, a\nseasonal source is separated from a year-round one. Most records do not say,\nand silence is not a year-round supply: the dry-season figure is therefore a\nband between counting the unknowns and not counting them, never a single\nnumber that quietly picks one.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Iterable, Optional\n\nfrom .waterpoints import WaterPoint\n\n__all__ = [\n \"CENSUS_TOTAL\",\n \"CENSUS_YEAR\",\n \"DEFAULT_GROWTH_RATE\",\n \"FRESHNESS_LABELS\",\n \"Freshness\",\n \"PlanningRow\",\n \"PopulationProjection\",\n \"SeasonalCoverage\",\n \"intercensal_growth_rate\",\n \"planning_rows\",\n \"planning_stats\",\n \"point_freshness\",\n \"project_population\",\n \"seasonal_coverage\",\n]\n\n#: The census the bundled district populations come from.\nCENSUS_YEAR = 2015\nCENSUS_TOTAL = 7_092_113\n\n#: The census before it, used only to derive a growth rate that can be\n#: checked against two published totals rather than asserted.\nPREVIOUS_CENSUS_YEAR = 2004\nPREVIOUS_CENSUS_TOTAL = 4_976_871\n\n\ndef intercensal_growth_rate() -> float:\n \"\"\"The annual rate implied by the two census totals.\n\n Derived rather than quoted, so the number can be checked against two\n figures anyone can look up. It is higher than recent international\n projections for the country - the 2004 count followed the civil war and\n the period that followed included large returnee movements - so a\n programme with its own projection should use it instead. That is what\n the ``rate`` argument is for, and every projected figure says which rate\n produced it.\n \"\"\"\n years = CENSUS_YEAR - PREVIOUS_CENSUS_YEAR\n return (CENSUS_TOTAL / PREVIOUS_CENSUS_TOTAL) ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0\n\n\nDEFAULT_GROWTH_RATE = intercensal_growth_rate()\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass PopulationProjection:\n \"\"\"A projected population and, always with it, how it was projected.\"\"\"\n\n base_year: int\n target_year: int\n rate: float\n uniform: bool\n factor: float\n\n @property\n def note(self) -> str:\n if self.target_year == self.base_year:\n return (f\"Populations are the {self.base_year} census figures, \"\n \"not projected.\")\n text = (f\"Populations are projected from the {self.base_year} census \"\n f\"to {self.target_year} at {self.rate * 100:.2f}% a year, a \"\n f\"factor of {self.factor:.3f}.\")\n if self.uniform:\n text += (\" The same rate is applied to every district, so the \"\n \"ranking is unchanged by the projection - only the \"\n \"magnitudes move. District rates would change it, and \"\n \"an urban district does not grow at the rural rate.\")\n return text\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\"base_year\": self.base_year, \"target_year\": self.target_year,\n \"rate\": self.rate, \"uniform\": self.uniform,\n \"factor\": self.factor, \"note\": self.note}\n\n\ndef project_population(population: dict[str, float], to_year: int, *,\n rate: float | None = None,\n rates: dict[str, float] | None = None,\n ) -> tuple[dict[str, float], PopulationProjection]:\n \"\"\"Project census populations forward, and say how.\n\n ``rates`` gives per-area annual rates where a programme has them;\n anything not named falls back to ``rate``. The returned projection\n carries the wording every surface prints, so no figure appears without\n the year and rate that produced it.\n \"\"\"\n national = DEFAULT_GROWTH_RATE if rate is None else float(rate)\n years = int(to_year) - CENSUS_YEAR\n if years < 0:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{to_year} is before the {CENSUS_YEAR} census; this projects \"\n \"forward, it does not reconstruct the past\")\n per_area = {str(k).strip().lower(): float(v) for k, v in (rates or {}).items()}\n projected = {}\n for name, value in population.items():\n area_rate = per_area.get(str(name).strip().lower(), national)\n projected[name] = float(value) * (1.0 + area_rate) ** years\n return projected, PopulationProjection(\n base_year=CENSUS_YEAR, target_year=int(to_year), rate=national,\n uniform=not per_area, factor=(1.0 + national) ** years,\n )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# How old the survey is\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: How stale a survey has to be before the label changes. A borehole that\n#: worked three years ago is a fair bet; one last seen eight years ago is a\n#: record, not an observation.\nFRESH_YEARS = 3\nAGEING_YEARS = 7\n\nFRESHNESS_LABELS = {\n \"fresh\": \"Surveyed recently\",\n \"ageing\": \"Survey is getting old\",\n \"stale\": \"Survey is out of date\",\n \"unknown\": \"Survey dates not recorded\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Freshness:\n \"\"\"When the points in an area were last actually looked at.\"\"\"\n\n n_points: int\n n_dated: int\n latest_year: Optional[int]\n median_age_years: Optional[float]\n n_recent: int\n state: str\n\n @property\n def label(self) -> str:\n return FRESHNESS_LABELS.get(self.state, FRESHNESS_LABELS[\"unknown\"])\n\n @property\n def detail(self) -> str:\n if self.state == \"unknown\":\n return (\"No survey dates are recorded for these points, so how \"\n \"current this coverage figure is cannot be established.\")\n return (f\"{self.n_dated} of {self.n_points} points carry a survey \"\n f\"date; the most recent is {self.latest_year} and the median \"\n f\"is {self.median_age_years:.0f} years old. \"\n f\"{self.n_recent} were surveyed in the last {FRESH_YEARS} years.\")\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\"n_points\": self.n_points, \"n_dated\": self.n_dated,\n \"latest_year\": self.latest_year,\n \"median_age_years\": self.median_age_years,\n \"n_recent\": self.n_recent, \"state\": self.state,\n \"label\": self.label, \"detail\": self.detail}\n\n\ndef point_freshness(points: Iterable[WaterPoint], as_of_year: int) -> Freshness:\n \"\"\"Summarise how old the survey behind a set of points is.\"\"\"\n points = list(points)\n years = sorted(p.report_year for p in points if p.report_year)\n if not years:\n return Freshness(len(points), 0, None, None, 0, \"unknown\")\n ages = [as_of_year - y for y in years]\n middle = len(ages) // 2\n median = (float(ages[middle]) if len(ages) % 2\n else (ages[middle - 1] + ages[middle]) / 2.0)\n recent = sum(1 for age in ages if age <= FRESH_YEARS)\n if median <= FRESH_YEARS:\n state = \"fresh\"\n elif median <= AGEING_YEARS:\n state = \"ageing\"\n else:\n state = \"stale\"\n return Freshness(len(points), len(years), max(years), median, recent, state)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Whether the source lasts the dry season\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SeasonalCoverage:\n \"\"\"Year-round service, as a band rather than a number.\n\n ``low`` counts only the points a survey confirmed work all year; ``high``\n also counts the ones nobody asked about. The true figure is between them,\n and how far apart they are is how much of this is guesswork.\n \"\"\"\n\n n_year_round: int\n n_seasonal: int\n n_unknown: int\n people_per_point_low: Optional[float]\n people_per_point_high: Optional[float]\n\n @property\n def is_established(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether seasonality was recorded often enough to mean anything.\"\"\"\n known = self.n_year_round + self.n_seasonal\n return known > 0 and known >= (known + self.n_unknown) * 0.5\n\n @property\n def people_per_point_band(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"The dry-season band as a planner reads it: best case to worst.\n\n ``people_per_point_high`` is the kinder end - it credits the points\n nobody asked about with working all year - so it comes first.\n \"\"\"\n best, worst = self.people_per_point_high, self.people_per_point_low\n if best is None and worst is None:\n return \"n/a\"\n if worst is None:\n return f\"{best:,.0f} to no confirmed point\"\n if best is None or round(best) == round(worst):\n return f\"{worst:,.0f}\"\n return f\"{best:,.0f} to {worst:,.0f}\"\n\n @property\n def detail(self) -> str:\n total = self.n_year_round + self.n_seasonal + self.n_unknown\n if not total:\n return \"There are no functional points here to ask about.\"\n if self.n_year_round + self.n_seasonal == 0:\n return (\"No survey recorded how many months of the year these \"\n \"points yield water, so dry-season service cannot be \"\n \"separated from wet-season service.
