verdict(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"One line suitability statement for reports.\"\"\"\n state = self.verdict_state\n health = self.health_exceedances\n national = self.national_exceedances\n acceptability = self.aesthetic_exceedances\n\n if state == \"health_fail\":\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in health)\n return (\n \"The water does not meet the health based guideline value(s) \"\n f\"for: {names}. Treatment or an alternative source is required \"\n \"before the water is used for drinking.\"\n )\n if state == \"national_fail\":\n # A national limit can be stricter than, or exist without, a WHO\n # health value - it is a legal compliance failure, not a matter of\n # taste, so it must not be reported as merely aesthetic.\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in national)\n extra = (\n \" Acceptability limits are also exceeded for: \"\n + \", \".join(r.parameter for r in acceptability)\n + \".\"\n if acceptability\n else \"\"\n )\n return (\n \"The water meets the WHO health based guideline values, but \"\n f\"does not comply with the national standard limit(s) for: \"\n f\"{names}.{extra} Treatment is required before the supply can \"\n \"be accepted against the national standard; check whether the \"\n \"limit exceeded is a health or an acceptability limit.\"\n )\n if state == \"indeterminate\":\n reasons = \"; \".join(self.uncertainties)\n extra = (\n \" Acceptability limits are exceeded for: \"\n + \", \".join(r.parameter for r in acceptability)\n + \".\"\n if acceptability\n else \"\"\n )\n return (\n \"The water cannot be declared suitable for drinking on these \"\n f\"results: {reasons}.{extra} Resolve the outstanding \"\n \"parameters - re-sample, or ask the laboratory for the units \"\n \"and detection limits used - before the supply is signed off.\"\n )\n if state == \"aesthetic\":\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in acceptability)\n return (\n \"The water meets all health based guideline values. \"\n f\"Acceptability (aesthetic) limits are exceeded for: {names}. \"\n \"The water is usable for drinking, although taste, odour or \"\n \"staining complaints may arise; simple treatment is advisable.\"\n )\n return (\n \"All measured parameters comply with the WHO guideline values and \"\n \"the national standard limits applied. The water is suitable for \"\n \"drinking on the basis of the parameters tested.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _limit_maximums(entry: StandardEntry) -> list[float]:\n \"\"\"Every upper limit that applies to a parameter, in the guideline unit.\"\"\"\n out = []\n for limit in (entry.who_health, entry.sl_standard, entry.who_aesthetic):\n if limit is not None and limit.maximum is not None:\n out.append(limit.maximum)\n return out\n\n\n#: Shared with the aggregate indices, so one conversion rule serves the row\n#: comparison, the WQI, the hazard index, the ionic balance and corrosivity.\n_convert_to_guideline_unit = to_standard_unit\n\n\ndef _assess_result(result, entry: Optional[StandardEntry]) -> ParameterAssessment:\n \"\"\"Grade one laboratory result against its guideline entry.\"\"\"\n who_h = str(entry.who_health) if entry and entry.who_health else \"\"\n who_a = str(entry.who_aesthetic) if entry and entry.who_aesthetic else \"\"\n sl = str(entry.sl_standard) if entry and entry.sl_standard else \"\"\n guideline_unit = entry.unit if entry else \"\"\n\n row = ParameterAssessment(\n parameter=result.parameter,\n value=result.value,\n unit=result.unit or guideline_unit,\n below_detection=result.below_detection,\n who_health=who_h,\n who_aesthetic=who_a,\n sl_standard=sl,\n status=\"not_measured\",\n remark=\"no value reported\",\n guideline_unit=guideline_unit,\n detection_limit=result.detection_limit,\n )\n\n if result.value is None and not result.below_detection:\n return row\n\n if entry is None:\n # An unrecognised determinand is an open question, not a clean bill.\n row.status = \"no_guideline\"\n row.reason = \"unknown_parameter\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.remark = (\n \"parameter not in the standards table, so it was not checked \"\n \"against any limit\"\n )\n return row\n\n limits = _limit_maximums(entry)\n\n if result.below_detection and result.value is None:\n return _assess_below_detection(row, result, entry, limits)\n\n converted, reason = _convert_to_guideline_unit(\n float(result.value), result.unit, entry\n )\n if converted is None:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = reason\n row.remark = (\n f\"reported in '{result.unit}' but the guideline is in \"\n f\"'{guideline_unit}': {INDETERMINATE_REASONS[reason]}. The value \"\n \"was not compared against any limit.\"\n )\n return row\n\n row.value_in_guideline_unit = converted\n row.reason = reason\n if reason == \"unit_assumed\":\n unit_note = f\" (read as {guideline_unit}; the reported unit was '{result.unit}')\" \\\n if result.unit else f\" (read as {guideline_unit}; no unit was reported)\"\n elif converted != result.value:\n unit_note = (\n f\" ({result.value:g} {result.unit} = {converted:g} {guideline_unit})\"\n )\n else:\n unit_note = \"\"\n _grade(row, entry, converted, unit_note)\n return row\n\n\ndef _assess_below_detection(\n row: ParameterAssessment, result, entry: StandardEntry, limits: list[float]\n) -> ParameterAssessment:\n \"\"\"A \"< X\" result proves compliance only when X is under the limit.\"\"\"\n if not limits:\n row.status = \"below_detection\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"below detection limit ({result.detection_limit:g})\"\n if result.detection_limit is not None\n else \"below detection limit\"\n )\n return row\n\n strictest = min(limits)\n if result.detection_limit is None:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = \"detection_limit_unknown\"\n row.remark = (\n \"reported below the detection limit, but the limit itself was not \"\n f\"reported, so compliance with {strictest:g} {entry.unit} cannot \"\n \"be shown. Ask the laboratory for the detection limit.\"\n )\n return row\n\n dl, reason = _convert_to_guideline_unit(\n float(result.detection_limit), result.unit, entry\n )\n if dl is None:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = reason\n row.remark = (\n f\"reported below a detection limit of {result.detection_limit:g} \"\n f\"'{result.unit}', which cannot be compared with the guideline in \"\n f\"'{entry.unit}': {INDETERMINATE_REASONS[reason]}.\"\n )\n return row\n\n row.value_in_guideline_unit = None\n if dl > strictest:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = \"detection_limit_above_guideline\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"below a detection limit of {dl:g} {entry.unit}, which is above \"\n f\"the limit of {strictest:g} {entry.unit}. The method cannot see \"\n \"the guideline value, so the result does not show compliance; \"\n \"re-test with a more sensitive method.\"\n )\n return row\n\n row.status = \"below_detection\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"below detection limit ({dl:g} {entry.unit}), which is at or under \"\n f\"the limit of {strictest:g} {entry.unit}\"\n )\n return row\n\n\ndef _grade(\n row: ParameterAssessment, entry: StandardEntry, value: float, unit_note: str\n) -> None:\n \"\"\"Apply the limit hierarchy to a converted value.\"\"\"\n is_micro = (entry.category or \"\").strip().lower() == \"microbiological\"\n if entry.who_health and entry.who_health.exceeded_by(value):\n row.status = \"exceeds_health\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the WHO health based guideline ({entry.who_health})\"\n f\"{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif is_micro and (\n (entry.sl_standard and entry.sl_standard.exceeded_by(value))\n or (entry.who_aesthetic and entry.who_aesthetic.exceeded_by(value))\n ):\n # A microbiological indicator (E. coli, total coliforms) is a health\n # concern, never an aesthetic one, even when its limit happens to be\n # carried in the national/acceptability column rather than the\n # WHO-health column. Treat any detection above the limit as a health\n # exceedance so the verdict never calls faecally-indicated water\n # \"usable for drinking\".\n row.status = \"exceeds_health\"\n limit = entry.sl_standard or entry.who_aesthetic\n row.remark = (\n f\"microbiological indicator detected above the limit ({limit}); \"\n f\"a health (faecal contamination) concern, not aesthetic{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif entry.sl_standard and entry.sl_standard.exceeded_by(value):\n if entry.who_health:\n # WHO sets a health value and the national limit is stricter:\n # failing it is a compliance failure, not a matter of taste, and\n # must not be reported as aesthetic.\n row.status = \"exceeds_national\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the national standard limit ({entry.sl_standard}), \"\n f\"which is stricter than the WHO health based guideline \"\n f\"({entry.who_health}){unit_note}\"\n )\n else:\n # No WHO health value exists for this parameter, so the national\n # limit is an acceptability one (iron staining, chloride taste,\n # turbidity).\n row.status = \"exceeds_aesthetic\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the national acceptability limit \"\n f\"({entry.sl_standard}){unit_note}\"\n )\n elif entry.who_aesthetic and entry.who_aesthetic.exceeded_by(value):\n row.status = \"exceeds_aesthetic\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the WHO acceptability value ({entry.who_aesthetic})\"\n f\"{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif not (entry.who_health or entry.who_aesthetic or entry.sl_standard):\n row.status = \"no_guideline\"\n row.remark = entry.note or \"no guideline value\"\n else:\n row.status = \"within_limits\"\n row.remark = unit_note.strip() if unit_note else \"\"\n\n\ndef _missing_essential(rows: list[ParameterAssessment], table: dict) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Essential health parameters with no evaluable result in the sample.\"\"\"\n graded = {\n normalise_parameter(r.parameter)\n for r in rows\n if r.evaluable\n and r.status\n in (\n \"exceeds_health\",\n \"exceeds_national\",\n \"exceeds_aesthetic\",\n \"within_limits\",\n \"below_detection\",\n )\n }\n missing = []\n for key in ESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS:\n if key in graded:\n continue\n entry = table.get(key)\n missing.append(entry.parameter if entry is not None else key)\n return missing\n\n\ndef assess_sample(\n sample: WaterQualitySample,\n standards_path: str | Path | None = None,\n) -> WaterQualityAssessment:\n \"\"\"Assess every result in a sample against the standards table.\"\"\"\n table = load_standards(standards_path)\n rows: list[ParameterAssessment] = []\n flags: list[DataFlag] = list(sample.flags)\n\n for result in sample.results:\n entry = table.get(normalise_parameter(result.parameter))\n row = _assess_result(result, entry)\n rows.append(row)\n\n if row.reason == \"unknown_parameter\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"unknown_parameter\",\n f\"No guideline entry for '{result.parameter}'; it was not \"\n \"checked against any limit and keeps the sample out of a \"\n \"'suitable for drinking' verdict. Add it to the standards \"\n \"CSV if a limit applies.\",\n )\n )\n elif row.reason == \"unit_assumed\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"unit_not_reported\",\n f\"'{result.parameter}' carries no usable unit\"\n + (f\" ('{result.unit}')\" if result.unit else \"\")\n + f\"; it was read as {row.guideline_unit}. Confirm against \"\n \"the laboratory certificate.\",\n )\n )\n elif row.reason == \"unit_basis_assumed\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"unit_basis_assumed\",\n f\"'{result.parameter}' is reported in '{result.unit}' but \"\n f\"the guideline is written in '{row.guideline_unit}'. The \"\n \"values were taken as the same basis; confirm with the \"\n \"laboratory, since an 'as CaCO3' figure is about 2.5 times \"\n \"the same concentration expressed as the element.\",\n )\n )\n elif row.status == \"indeterminate\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n f\"indeterminate_{row.reason}\",\n f\"'{result.parameter}' could not be assessed: {row.remark}\",\n )\n )\n\n # WHO combined nitrate + nitrite rule: the sum of the ratio of each to\n # its own guideline value must not exceed 1. A sample can pass both\n # single-parameter checks yet fail this combined limit, so it is applied\n # only when neither ion is individually in exceedance (the individual\n # exceedance is already reported on its own row).\n combined = _nitrate_nitrite_index(rows, table)\n if combined is not None:\n ratio, no3, no2, gv3, gv2, bounded = combined\n if ratio > 1.0 and no3 <= gv3 and no2 <= gv2:\n # A bounded index is an upper bound, not a measurement: it says\n # the rule *may* be breached, which is a question rather than a\n # finding, so it is reported as indeterminate rather than as a\n # health exceedance the laboratory never demonstrated.\n rows.append(\n ParameterAssessment(\n parameter=\"Nitrate + nitrite (combined)\",\n value=round(ratio, 2),\n unit=\"ratio\",\n below_detection=False,\n who_health=\"<= 1\",\n who_aesthetic=\"\",\n sl_standard=\"\",\n status=\"indeterminate\" if bounded else \"exceeds_health\",\n remark=(\n f\"An upper bound on the combined index \"\n f\"({no3:g}/{gv3:g} + {no2:g}/{gv2:g} = {ratio:.2f}) \"\n \"exceeds 1, taking the below-detection component at \"\n \"its detection limit. The WHO combined nitrate and \"\n \"nitrite limit cannot be shown to be met; ask the \"\n \"laboratory for a lower detection limit.\"\n if bounded else\n f\"The combined index ({no3:g}/{gv3:g} + {no2:g}/{gv2:g} \"\n f\"= {ratio:.2f}) exceeds 1; the WHO combined nitrate and \"\n \"nitrite limit is not met even though each is within its \"\n \"own guideline value.\"\n ),\n guideline_unit=\"ratio\",\n value_in_guideline_unit=None if bounded else round(ratio, 2),\n evaluable=not bounded,\n reason=\"detection_limit_above_guideline\" if bounded else \"\",\n )\n )\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\" if bounded else \"warning\",\n \"nitrate_nitrite_combined_unproven\" if bounded\n else \"nitrate_nitrite_combined\",\n \"The combined nitrate + nitrite index cannot be shown to \"\n \"meet the WHO limit: one component is below detection and \"\n \"its detection limit is high enough that the sum may \"\n \"exceed 1.\"\n if bounded else\n \"Combined nitrate + nitrite index exceeds 1 (WHO); treat as \"\n \"a health exceedance.\",\n )\n )\n\n missing_essential = _missing_essential(rows, table)\n if missing_essential:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"incomplete_health_panel\",\n \"No evaluable result for \" + \", \".join(missing_essential) + \". \"\n \"The sample cannot show the water is safe to drink until the \"\n \"health panel is complete.\",\n )\n )\n if not [r for r in rows if r.evaluable and r.status != \"not_measured\"]:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"nothing_evaluable\",\n \"No result in this sample could be graded against a guideline \"\n \"value, so no suitability verdict can be given.\",\n )\n )\n\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is not None and ionic.flag is not None:\n flags.append(ionic.flag)\n\n corrosivity = assess_corrosivity(sample)\n flags.extend(corrosivity.flags)\n\n wqi = compute_wqi(sample, standards_path)\n health_risk = assess_health_risk(sample)\n if health_risk is not None:\n flags.extend(health_risk.flags)\n\n return WaterQualityAssessment(\n sample=sample,\n rows=rows,\n ionic=ionic,\n corrosivity=corrosivity,\n wqi=wqi,\n health_risk=health_risk,\n flags=flags,\n missing_essential=missing_essential,\n )\n\n\ndef _nitrate_nitrite_index(rows: list[ParameterAssessment], table):\n \"\"\"The WHO combined nitrate + nitrite index.\n\n Returns ``(ratio, no3, no2, gv3, gv2, bounded)`` where ``ratio`` is\n ``no3/gv3 + no2/gv2``, or ``None`` when a value or guideline is missing\n altogether. Both concentrations are the unit-converted ones, so a result\n reported in ug/L is not silently added as though it were mg/L.\n\n A component reported below detection is taken at its detection limit,\n and ``bounded`` says so. That reading is deliberately the pessimistic\n one: \"< 3 mg/L nitrite\" beside 49 mg/L nitrate cannot rule out a\n combined index of 1.98, and treating the unknown as zero turned a\n sample that might fail the rule into one that passed it silently.\n \"\"\"\n\n def _value_and_gv(key):\n entry = table.get(key)\n gv = entry.who_health.maximum if entry and entry.who_health else None\n for row in rows:\n if normalise_parameter(row.parameter) != key:\n continue\n if row.value_in_guideline_unit is not None:\n return float(row.value_in_guideline_unit), gv, False\n if row.below_detection and entry is not None:\n dl, reason = to_standard_unit(\n float(row.detection_limit), row.unit, entry\n ) if row.detection_limit is not None else (None, \"\")\n if dl is not None:\n return float(dl), gv, True\n return None, gv, False\n return None, gv, False\n\n no3, gv3, b3 = _value_and_gv(\"nitrate (as no3)\")\n no2, gv2, b2 = _value_and_gv(\"nitrite (as no2)\")\n if no3 is None or no2 is None or not gv3 or not gv2:\n return None\n return no3 / gv3 + no2 / gv2, no3, no2, gv3, gv2, (b3 or b2)\n"}, "groundwater/quality/corrosivity.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Corrosivity and scaling indices, and a materials recommendation.\n\nSoft, low-alkalinity, low-pH water from crystalline basement aquifers is\nchemically aggressive and corrodes galvanised iron and mild-steel rising\nmains and pump parts, which is a leading cause of premature handpump\nfailure across West Africa. The water can be aggressive even when the pH\nis inside the 6.5 to 8.5 acceptability range, so a pH check alone is not\nenough.\n\nThis module computes the classical indices from parameters the toolkit\nalready parses (pH, calcium, alkalinity, TDS or EC, temperature) and\nturns them into a plain-language verdict and a rising-main / pump material\nrecommendation:\n\n* Langelier Saturation Index (LSI) - CaCO3 saturation; < 0 is corrosive.\n* Ryznar Stability Index (RSI) - practical corrosion/scaling scale.\n* Aggressive Index (AI) - AWWA index for asbestos-cement, a\n useful aggressiveness check.\n* Larson-Skold Index - chloride/sulfate attack on steel.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .standards import canonical_values, normalise_parameter\n\n# milli-equivalents per mg for the Larson-Skold ratio\n_MEQ = {\n \"chloride\": 1 / 35.453,\n \"sulfate\": 2 / 96.06,\n \"bicarbonate\": 1 / 61.017,\n \"carbonate\": 2 / 60.009,\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass CorrosivityAssessment:\n lsi: Optional[float] = None\n rsi: Optional[float] = None\n aggressive_index: Optional[float] = None\n larson_skold: Optional[float] = None\n classification: str = \"Insufficient data\"\n is_aggressive: bool = False\n verdict: str = \"\"\n materials_note: str = \"\"\n assumptions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\ndef _value(sample: WaterQualitySample, key: str) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"One parameter on the standards table's scale.\n\n The Langelier and Ryznar indices take log10 of concentrations in mg/L, so\n a value on another scale does not shift the index - it invalidates it. A\n conductivity given in mS/cm produced a TDS estimate of 0 mg/L and an\n index pair computed from it.\n \"\"\"\n canonical = canonical_values(sample)\n if key in canonical:\n return canonical[key]\n for result in sample.results:\n if normalise_parameter(result.parameter) == key:\n if result.value is not None:\n # present but not convertible: refuse it rather than use the\n # raw number on an unknown scale\n return None\n if result.value is not None:\n return float(result.value)\n return 0.0 if result.below_detection else None\n return None\n\n\ndef _classify_rsi(rsi: float) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n \"\"\"Map a Ryznar index to a class and an is-aggressive flag.\"\"\"\n if rsi < 6.0:\n return \"Scale-forming\", False\n if rsi <= 7.0:\n return \"Balanced (near CaCO3 equilibrium)\", False\n if rsi <= 8.0:\n return \"Corrosive\", True\n return \"Strongly corrosive\", True\n\n\ndef assess_corrosivity(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> CorrosivityAssessment:\n \"\"\"Assess corrosivity/scaling from a water quality sample.\n\n Returns an assessment with whichever indices the available data\n supports. When pH, calcium and alkalinity are all present the\n saturation indices are computed; the Larson-Skold ratio additionally\n needs chloride and sulfate.\n \"\"\"\n assessment = CorrosivityAssessment()\n assumptions = assessment.assumptions\n\n ph = _value(sample, \"ph\")\n calcium = _value(sample, \"calcium\")\n alkalinity = _value(sample, \"alkalinity\")\n tds = _value(sample, \"tds\")\n ec = _value(sample, \"electrical conductivity\")\n temp = _value(sample, \"temperature\")\n\n # TDS: measured, else estimated from EC, else a soft-water default\n if tds is None or tds <= 0:\n if ec and ec > 0:\n tds = 0.64 * ec\n assumptions.append(\n f\"TDS estimated as 0.64 x EC = {tds:.0f} mg/L (TDS not reported).\"\n )\n else:\n tds = 250.0\n assumptions.append(\"TDS assumed 250 mg/L (neither TDS nor EC reported).\")\n if temp is None or temp <= 0:\n temp = 25.0\n assumptions.append(\"Temperature assumed 25 C (not reported).\")\n\n if ph is None or calcium is None or alkalinity is None or calcium <= 0 or alkalinity <= 0:\n assessment.verdict = (\n \"Corrosivity could not be assessed: pH, calcium and alkalinity are \"\n \"all required. Supply them to obtain a materials recommendation.\"\n )\n return assessment\n\n # calcium hardness as CaCO3 (Ca mg/L x 100.09/40.08)\n ca_hardness = calcium * 2.497\n\n # Langelier: pHs = (9.3 + A + B) - (C + D)\n a = (math.log10(tds) - 1.0) / 10.0\n b = -13.12 * math.log10(temp + 273.15) + 34.55\n c = math.log10(ca_hardness) - 0.4\n d = math.log10(alkalinity)\n ph_s = (9.3 + a + b) - (c + d)\n lsi = ph - ph_s\n rsi = 2 * ph_s - ph\n ai = ph + math.log10(alkalinity * ca_hardness)\n\n assessment.lsi = round(lsi, 2)\n assessment.rsi = round(rsi, 2)\n assessment.aggressive_index = round(ai, 2)\n\n # Larson-Skold (optional): (Cl + SO4) / (HCO3 + CO3) in meq/L\n chloride = _value(sample, \"chloride\")\n sulfate = _value(sample, \"sulfate\")\n bicarbonate = _value(sample, \"bicarbonate\")\n carbonate = _value(sample, \"carbonate\")\n if bicarbonate is None:\n # alkalinity (as CaCO3) -> bicarbonate equivalent meq/L\n hco3_meq = alkalinity / 50.04\n else:\n hco3_meq = bicarbonate * _MEQ[\"bicarbonate\"]\n co3_meq = (carbonate or 0.0) * _MEQ[\"carbonate\"]\n if chloride is not None and sulfate is not None and (hco3_meq + co3_meq) > 0:\n ls = (chloride * _MEQ[\"chloride\"] + sulfate * _MEQ[\"sulfate\"]) / (\n hco3_meq + co3_meq\n )\n assessment.larson_skold = round(ls, 2)\n\n classification, aggressive = _classify_rsi(rsi)\n # corroborate with LSI and AI\n if lsi < -0.5:\n aggressive = True\n if assessment.aggressive_index is not None and assessment.aggressive_index < 10:\n aggressive = True\n # Keep the class label consistent with the flag and verdict: when the\n # LSI/AI corroboration promotes borderline water to aggressive, the RSI\n # class (\"Balanced\", \"Scale-forming\") must not still say otherwise, else\n # a report shows a \"Balanced\" label beside an \"aggressive\" verdict.\n if aggressive and classification not in (\"Corrosive\", \"Strongly corrosive\"):\n classification = \"Corrosive\"\n assessment.classification = classification\n assessment.is_aggressive = aggressive\n\n if aggressive:\n assessment.verdict = (\n f\"The water is chemically aggressive (Ryznar index {rsi:.1f}, \"\n f\"Langelier index {lsi:+.1f}). It will corrode metal fittings, and \"\n \"it can be aggressive even though the pH is within the acceptability \"\n \"range, which is typical of soft basement groundwater.\"\n )\n assessment.materials_note = (\n \"Specify uPVC or stainless steel (grade 304 or 316) for the rising \"\n \"main and pump components, and avoid galvanised iron and mild steel, \"\n \"which corrode rapidly in this water and are a leading cause of \"\n \"premature handpump failure. Inspect the rising main and pump rods \"\n \"for corrosion at each service.\"\n )\n if assessment.larson_skold is not None and assessment.larson_skold > 0.8:\n assessment.materials_note += (\n f\" The Larson-Skold ratio ({assessment.larson_skold:.1f}) is \"\n \"elevated, so chloride and sulfate add to the attack on steel.\"\n )\n assessment.flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"aggressive_water\",\n \"Water is chemically aggressive; specify uPVC or stainless rising \"\n \"main and pump components.\",\n )\n )\n elif classification == \"Scale-forming\":\n assessment.verdict = (\n f\"The water tends to deposit calcium carbonate scale (Ryznar index \"\n f\"{rsi:.1f}, Langelier index {lsi:+.1f}).\"\n )\n assessment.materials_note = (\n \"Monitor the screen and pump for encrustation and de-scale as needed; \"\n \"corrosion of metal parts is a lesser concern.\"\n )\n else:\n assessment.verdict = (\n f\"The water is close to calcium carbonate equilibrium (Ryznar index \"\n f\"{rsi:.1f}, Langelier index {lsi:+.1f}); neither strong corrosion nor \"\n \"scaling is expected.\"\n )\n assessment.materials_note = (\n \"Standard materials are acceptable; inspect fittings for corrosion \"\n \"during routine maintenance.\"\n )\n return assessment\n"}, "groundwater/quality/diagrams.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Hydrochemical facies diagrams: Piper and Stiff.\n\nBoth work from the meq/L values produced by the ionic balance module,\nso they need the major ions to be present in the sample. Multiple\nsamples can be plotted on one Piper diagram for comparison.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import WaterQualitySample\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom .ionic import ionic_balance\n\n_SQ3 = np.sqrt(3.0)\n\n\ndef _ternary_xy(a: float, b: float, c: float, origin=(0.0, 0.0), size=1.0):\n \"\"\"Barycentric (a bottom-left, b bottom-right, c top) to xy.\"\"\"\n total = a + b + c\n if total <= 0:\n return None\n a, b, c = a / total, b / total, c / total\n x = origin[0] + (b + 0.5 * c) * size\n y = origin[1] + (_SQ3 / 2.0) * c * size\n return x, y\n\n\ndef _triangle(ax, origin, size, labels, ticks=True):\n x0, y0 = origin\n verts = np.array(\n [[x0, y0], [x0 + size, y0], [x0 + 0.5 * size, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size], [x0, y0]]\n )\n ax.plot(verts[:, 0], verts[:, 1], color=\"#444444\", lw=1.2)\n for frac in (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8):\n # grid lines parallel to each side\n ax.plot(\n [x0 + frac * size, x0 + 0.5 * size + 0.5 * frac * size],\n [y0, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * (1 - frac)],\n color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.6, zorder=0,\n )\n ax.plot(\n [x0 + (1 - frac) * size, x0 + 0.5 * size - 0.5 * frac * size],\n [y0, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * (1 - frac)],\n color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.6, zorder=0,\n )\n ax.plot(\n [x0 + 0.5 * frac * size, x0 + size - 0.5 * frac * size],\n [y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * frac, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * frac],\n color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.6, zorder=0,\n )\n la, lb, lc = labels\n ax.text(x0 - 0.03, y0 - 0.05, la, ha=\"right\", va=\"top\", fontsize=9)\n ax.text(x0 + size + 0.03, y0 - 0.05, lb, ha=\"left\", va=\"top\", fontsize=9)\n ax.text(x0 + 0.5 * size, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size + 0.04, lc, ha=\"center\", fontsize=9)\n\n\ndef plot_piper(\n samples: list[WaterQualitySample],\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Piper diagram\",\n):\n \"\"\"Piper trilinear diagram for one or more samples.\n\n The diamond point is the classical construction: the intersection\n of the +60 degree line through the cation point and the -60 degree\n line through the anion point. Samples without a complete major ion\n analysis are skipped.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n size = 1.0\n gap = 0.18\n cat_origin = (0.0, 0.0)\n an_origin = (size + gap, 0.0)\n\n # diamond vertices from the projection geometry\n x_mid = size + gap / 2.0\n y_bot = _SQ3 / 2.0 * gap\n diamond = np.array(\n [\n [x_mid, y_bot], # bottom: Ca+Mg with HCO3\n [x_mid + size / 2.0, y_bot + _SQ3 / 2.0 * size], # right: Na+K with SO4+Cl\n [x_mid, y_bot + _SQ3 * size], # top: Ca+Mg with SO4+Cl\n [x_mid - size / 2.0, y_bot + _SQ3 / 2.0 * size], # left\n [x_mid, y_bot],\n ]\n )\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.9, 5.6))\n ax.set_aspect(\"equal\")\n ax.axis(\"off\")\n _triangle(ax, cat_origin, size, (\"Ca\", \"Na+K\", \"Mg\"))\n _triangle(ax, an_origin, size, (\"HCO3\", \"Cl\", \"SO4\"))\n ax.plot(diamond[:, 0], diamond[:, 1], color=\"#444444\", lw=1.2)\n ax.annotate(\n \"SO4 + Cl increases upward; Na + K increases to the right\",\n xy=(x_mid, y_bot + _SQ3 * size + 0.06),\n ha=\"center\", fontsize=7.5, color=\"#555555\",\n )\n\n markers = [\"o\", \"s\", \"^\", \"D\", \"v\", \"P\", \"X\"]\n plotted = []\n for i, sample in enumerate(samples):\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is None:\n continue\n cat = ionic.cations_meq\n an = ionic.anions_meq\n ca, mg = cat.get(\"calcium\", 0), cat.get(\"magnesium\", 0)\n nak = cat.get(\"sodium\", 0) + cat.get(\"potassium\", 0)\n cl = an.get(\"chloride\", 0)\n so4 = an.get(\"sulfate\", 0)\n hco3 = an.get(\"bicarbonate\", 0) + an.get(\"carbonate\", 0)\n\n p_cat = _ternary_xy(ca, nak, mg, cat_origin, size)\n p_an = _ternary_xy(hco3, cl, so4, an_origin, size)\n if p_cat is None or p_an is None:\n continue\n # intersection of +60 deg line through the cation point and\n # -60 deg line through the anion point\n xc, yc = p_cat\n xa, ya = p_an\n xd = 0.5 * (xc + xa) + (ya - yc) / (2.0 * _SQ3)\n yd = yc + _SQ3 * (xd - xc)\n marker = markers[i % len(markers)]\n label = sample.sample_id or sample.site.community or f\"sample {i + 1}\"\n color = style.accent_color if i % 2 == 0 else style.secondary_color\n first = True\n for px, py in ((xc, yc), (xa, ya), (xd, yd)):\n ax.plot(px, py, marker, ms=6, mfc=color, mec=\"white\", mew=0.8,\n label=label if first else None)\n first = False\n plotted.append(label)\n if plotted:\n ax.legend(loc=\"upper left\", fontsize=8, frameon=True)\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_stiff(\n sample: WaterQualitySample,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Stiff diagram: Na+K / Ca / Mg on the left, Cl / HCO3 / SO4 right.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Stiff diagram needs the major ions (Ca, Mg, Na, Cl, HCO3)\")\n cat = ionic.cations_meq\n an = ionic.anions_meq\n rows = [\n (cat.get(\"sodium\", 0) + cat.get(\"potassium\", 0), an.get(\"chloride\", 0), \"Na+K\", \"Cl\"),\n (cat.get(\"calcium\", 0), an.get(\"bicarbonate\", 0) + an.get(\"carbonate\", 0), \"Ca\", \"HCO3\"),\n (cat.get(\"magnesium\", 0), an.get(\"sulfate\", 0), \"Mg\", \"SO4\"),\n ]\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.7, 2.8))\n ys = [2, 1, 0]\n xs_left = [-r[0] for r in rows]\n xs_right = [r[1] for r in rows]\n poly_x = xs_left + xs_right[::-1]\n poly_y = ys + ys[::-1]\n ax.fill(poly_x, poly_y, color=style.accent_color, alpha=0.25, lw=0)\n ax.plot(poly_x + [poly_x[0]], poly_y + [poly_y[0]], color=style.accent_color, lw=1.6)\n ax.axvline(0, color=\"#555555\", lw=1.0)\n for y, (c_meq, a_meq, c_label, a_label) in zip(ys, rows):\n ax.plot([-c_meq], [y], \"o\", ms=4, color=style.accent_color)\n ax.plot([a_meq], [y], \"o\", ms=4, color=style.accent_color)\n ax.text(ax.get_xlim()[0], y, \"\", fontsize=8)\n span = max(max(map(abs, xs_left)), max(xs_right), 0.5) * 1.3\n ax.set_xlim(-span, span)\n ax.set_ylim(-0.6, 2.6)\n for y, (c, a, c_label, a_label) in zip(ys, rows):\n ax.text(-span * 0.98, y, c_label, ha=\"left\", va=\"center\", fontsize=9)\n ax.text(span * 0.98, y, a_label, ha=\"right\", va=\"center\", fontsize=9)\n ax.set_yticks([])\n ax.set_xlabel(\"meq/L (cations left, anions right)\")\n ax.set_title(title or f\"Stiff diagram - {sample.sample_id or sample.site.community}\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/quality/indices.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Aggregate water quality index and health-risk scoring.\n\nTwo summary numbers a district water office can use to rank many\nboreholes and prioritise treatment or rehabilitation:\n\n* Water Quality Index (WQI) - a weighted-arithmetic 0-based index over the\n physico-chemical parameters, with the usual rating classes (Excellent to\n Unsuitable). One number per borehole for comparison.\n\n* Health Hazard Index (HI) - the sum of hazard quotients (chronic daily\n intake over the oral reference dose) for the toxicants that matter for\n long-term ingestion (arsenic, fluoride, nitrate, manganese, lead,\n uranium and others), plus a lifetime carcinogenic risk for arsenic. HI\n below 1 is generally acceptable; at or above 1 there is a potential\n non-carcinogenic health concern.\n\nBoth are computed from the values and guideline limits the toolkit already\ncarries, and both degrade gracefully when parameters are missing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .standards import (\n Limit,\n StandardEntry,\n canonical_values,\n load_standards,\n normalise_parameter,\n)\n\n# adult chronic exposure (WHO/EPA default)\n_INTAKE_L_PER_DAY = 2.0\n_BODY_WEIGHT_KG = 70.0\n\n# oral reference doses, mg/kg/day (EPA IRIS / WHO), for the toxicants that\n# drive long-term ingestion risk in this setting\n_RFD = {\n \"arsenic\": 3.0e-4,\n \"fluoride\": 0.06,\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": 1.6,\n \"nitrite (as no2)\": 0.1,\n \"manganese\": 0.14,\n \"lead\": 3.5e-3,\n \"cadmium\": 5.0e-4,\n \"chromium (total)\": 3.0e-3,\n \"uranium\": 3.0e-3,\n \"nickel\": 0.02,\n \"copper\": 0.04,\n \"zinc\": 0.3,\n \"barium\": 0.2,\n \"selenium\": 5.0e-3,\n \"antimony\": 4.0e-4,\n}\n# oral cancer slope factors, (mg/kg/day)^-1\n_CANCER_SLOPE = {\"arsenic\": 1.5}\n\n# The EPA IRIS reference doses for nitrate (1.6) and nitrite (0.1) are\n# expressed as nitrogen (NO3-N / NO2-N), but the toolkit records nitrate and\n# nitrite as the whole ion (as NO3 / as NO2). Convert the measured \"as ion\"\n# concentration to a nitrogen basis before dividing by the RfD, else the\n# hazard quotient is overstated by the mass ratio (NO3/N = 62/14 = 4.43,\n# NO2/N = 46/14 = 3.29).\n_AS_NITROGEN_FACTOR = {\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": 62.004 / 14.007,\n \"nitrite (as no2)\": 46.005 / 14.007,\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterQualityIndex:\n value: float\n rating: str\n n_parameters: int\n top_contributors: list[tuple[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass HealthRiskAssessment:\n hazard_index: float\n hazard_quotients: dict # parameter -> HQ\n cancer_risk: Optional[float] # lifetime, arsenic\n rating: str\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\ndef _measured(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> dict[str, float]:\n \"\"\"Every measured value, converted onto the standards table's scale.\n\n The reference doses and the index weights below are all mg/L figures, so\n a laboratory reporting in ug/L used to produce a hazard index a thousand\n times too high - \"High\" risk and a 0.4 lifetime cancer risk for water\n that is well inside every guideline. A value whose unit cannot be\n reconciled is left out rather than used raw.\n \"\"\"\n return canonical_values(sample)\n\n\ndef _wqi_limit(entry: StandardEntry) -> Optional[Limit]:\n for limit in (entry.who_health, entry.who_aesthetic, entry.sl_standard):\n if limit is not None:\n return limit\n return None\n\n\ndef _wqi_rating(value: float) -> str:\n if value <= 50:\n return \"Excellent\"\n if value <= 100:\n return \"Good\"\n if value <= 200:\n return \"Poor\"\n if value <= 300:\n return \"Very poor\"\n return \"Unsuitable for drinking\"\n\n\ndef compute_wqi(sample: WaterQualitySample, standards_path=None) -> Optional[WaterQualityIndex]:\n \"\"\"Weighted-arithmetic Water Quality Index over physico-chemical data.\n\n Returns None when fewer than three usable parameters are available.\n \"\"\"\n table = load_standards(standards_path)\n values = _measured(sample)\n weight_sum = 0.0\n weighted_q = 0.0\n contributors: list[tuple[str, float]] = []\n n = 0\n for key, value in values.items():\n entry = table.get(key)\n if entry is None or entry.category == \"microbiological\":\n continue\n if key in _RFD:\n # Health-based trace toxicants (arsenic, lead, fluoride, nitrate,\n # ...) have tiny standards, so 1/s weighting and the value/s\n # sub-index let a single one dominate and drown out the general\n # chemistry this index is meant to summarise. They are reported\n # through the separate Hazard Index instead; excluding them keeps\n # the WQI a physico-chemical/acceptability measure as documented.\n continue\n limit = _wqi_limit(entry)\n if limit is None or not limit.maximum or limit.maximum <= 0:\n continue\n s_i = limit.maximum\n if key == \"ph\":\n ideal = 7.0\n denom = s_i - ideal\n q_i = 100.0 * abs(value - ideal) / denom if denom else 0.0\n else:\n q_i = 100.0 * value / s_i\n w_i = 1.0 / s_i\n weight_sum += w_i\n weighted_q += w_i * q_i\n contributors.append((entry.parameter, w_i * q_i))\n n += 1\n if n < 3 or weight_sum <= 0:\n return None\n wqi = weighted_q / weight_sum\n contributors.sort(key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)\n return WaterQualityIndex(\n value=round(wqi, 1),\n rating=_wqi_rating(wqi),\n n_parameters=n,\n top_contributors=[(name, round(c / weight_sum, 1)) for name, c in contributors[:3]],\n )\n\n\ndef assess_health_risk(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> Optional[HealthRiskAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Non-carcinogenic Hazard Index and arsenic carcinogenic risk.\n\n Returns None when none of the scored toxicants were measured.\n \"\"\"\n values = _measured(sample)\n hq: dict[str, float] = {}\n intake_factor = _INTAKE_L_PER_DAY / _BODY_WEIGHT_KG\n for key, rfd in _RFD.items():\n if key in values and rfd > 0:\n conc = values[key]\n factor = _AS_NITROGEN_FACTOR.get(key)\n if factor:\n conc = conc / factor # the RfD is expressed as nitrogen\n cdi = conc * intake_factor # mg/kg/day\n hq[key] = cdi / rfd\n if not hq:\n return None\n hazard_index = sum(hq.values())\n cancer_risk = None\n if \"arsenic\" in values:\n cdi_as = values[\"arsenic\"] * intake_factor\n cancer_risk = cdi_as * _CANCER_SLOPE[\"arsenic\"]\n\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n if hazard_index >= 1.0:\n worst = max(hq, key=hq.get)\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"hazard_index\",\n f\"Non-carcinogenic Hazard Index {hazard_index:.1f} is at or above \"\n f\"1 (dominated by {worst}); chronic ingestion poses a potential \"\n \"health concern.\",\n )\n )\n if cancer_risk is not None and cancer_risk > 1e-4:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"cancer_risk\",\n f\"Estimated lifetime arsenic cancer risk {cancer_risk:.1e} exceeds \"\n \"the 1e-4 screening level.\",\n )\n )\n\n if hazard_index < 1.0:\n rating = \"Acceptable (Hazard Index below 1)\"\n elif hazard_index < 4.0:\n rating = \"Elevated (Hazard Index at or above 1)\"\n else:\n rating = \"High (Hazard Index at or above 4)\"\n\n return HealthRiskAssessment(\n hazard_index=round(hazard_index, 2),\n hazard_quotients={k: round(v, 2) for k, v in sorted(hq.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)},\n cancer_risk=cancer_risk,\n rating=rating,\n flags=flags,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/quality/ionic.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Ionic balance check for major ion analyses.\n\nThe charge balance error is ``100 x (sum cations - sum anions) /\n(sum cations + sum anions)`` in meq/L. Errors within 5 percent are\nnormal laboratory practice; 5 to 10 percent is flagged for review and\nmore than 10 percent indicates an unreliable analysis or a missing\nmajor ion.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .standards import canonical_values, normalise_parameter\n\n# meq per mg: charge / molar mass\n_CATIONS = {\n \"calcium\": 2 / 40.078,\n \"magnesium\": 2 / 24.305,\n \"sodium\": 1 / 22.990,\n \"potassium\": 1 / 39.098,\n \"iron\": 2 / 55.845, # ferrous, minor\n \"manganese\": 2 / 54.938, # minor\n}\n_ANIONS = {\n \"chloride\": 1 / 35.453,\n \"sulfate\": 2 / 96.06,\n \"bicarbonate\": 1 / 61.017,\n \"carbonate\": 2 / 60.009,\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": 1 / 62.004,\n \"fluoride\": 1 / 18.998,\n}\n\n# the four majors on each side that make a balance meaningful\n_REQUIRED_CATIONS = (\"calcium\", \"magnesium\", \"sodium\")\n_REQUIRED_ANIONS = (\"chloride\", \"bicarbonate\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass IonicBalanceResult:\n sum_cations_meq: float\n sum_anions_meq: float\n error_percent: float\n cations_meq: dict\n anions_meq: dict\n used_alkalinity_for_bicarbonate: bool\n flag: Optional[DataFlag]\n\n\ndef _value(sample: WaterQualitySample, key: str) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"One ion in milliequivalents-ready mg/L.\n\n The meq factors above are per mg/L, so the value has to be on that scale\n before it is multiplied: the same chemistry reported in ug/L gave a\n charge balance error of 8.7% and was flagged as a laboratory problem.\n \"\"\"\n canonical = canonical_values(sample)\n if key in canonical:\n return canonical[key]\n for result in sample.results:\n if normalise_parameter(result.parameter) == key:\n if result.value is not None:\n # present but not convertible: refuse it rather than use the\n # raw number on an unknown scale\n return None\n return 0.0 if result.below_detection else None\n return None\n\n\ndef ionic_balance(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> Optional[IonicBalanceResult]:\n \"\"\"Compute the charge balance; returns None when the major ions are\n not sufficiently covered by the analysis.\"\"\"\n cations: dict[str, float] = {}\n anions: dict[str, float] = {}\n\n for key, factor in _CATIONS.items():\n value = _value(sample, key)\n if value is not None:\n cations[key] = value * factor\n\n used_alk = False\n for key, factor in _ANIONS.items():\n value = _value(sample, key)\n if value is not None:\n anions[key] = value * factor\n if \"bicarbonate\" not in anions:\n alk = _value(sample, \"alkalinity\")\n if alk is not None:\n # alkalinity as CaCO3 -> bicarbonate equivalent: meq = mg/L / 50.04\n anions[\"bicarbonate\"] = alk / 50.04\n used_alk = True\n\n if not all(k in cations for k in _REQUIRED_CATIONS) or not all(\n k in anions for k in _REQUIRED_ANIONS\n ):\n return None\n\n total_cat = sum(cations.values())\n total_an = sum(anions.values())\n if total_cat + total_an <= 0:\n return None\n error = 100.0 * (total_cat - total_an) / (total_cat + total_an)\n\n flag = None\n if abs(error) > 10:\n flag = DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"ionic_balance\",\n f\"Charge balance error {error:+.1f}% exceeds 10%; the analysis is \"\n \"unreliable or a major ion is missing.\",\n )\n elif abs(error) > 5:\n flag = DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"ionic_balance\",\n f\"Charge balance error {error:+.1f}% is between 5% and 10%; review \"\n \"the laboratory analysis.\",\n )\n return IonicBalanceResult(\n sum_cations_meq=total_cat,\n sum_anions_meq=total_an,\n error_percent=error,\n cations_meq=cations,\n anions_meq=anions,\n used_alkalinity_for_bicarbonate=used_alk,\n flag=flag,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/quality/standards.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Guideline and standard values for drinking water parameters.\n\nThe bundled table (``data/who_guidelines.csv``) carries WHO Guidelines\nfor Drinking-water Quality values (4th edition with addenda) split\ninto health based and acceptability values, plus a Sierra Leone\nstandard column. Where a confirmed national value is not to hand the\nnational column mirrors the WHO/regional figure; confirm the values\nagainst the current Sierra Leone Standards Bureau specification and\nedit the CSV (or pass a custom file) - no code change is needed.\n\nRange values such as pH are written ``6.5-8.5`` and evaluated as an\nallowed interval.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..units import _normalise as normalise_unit_text\nfrom ..units import comparable, convert, parse_unit\n\n_RANGE_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*-\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*$\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Limit:\n \"\"\"A guideline limit: either a maximum or an allowed range.\"\"\"\n\n maximum: Optional[float] = None\n minimum: Optional[float] = None\n\n @classmethod\n def parse(cls, text: str) -> Optional[\"Limit\"]:\n text = (text or \"\").strip()\n if not text:\n return None\n match = _RANGE_RE.match(text)\n if match:\n return cls(minimum=float(match.group(1)), maximum=float(match.group(2)))\n try:\n return cls(maximum=float(text))\n except ValueError:\n return None\n\n def exceeded_by(self, value: float) -> bool:\n if self.minimum is not None and value < self.minimum:\n return True\n if self.maximum is not None and value > self.maximum:\n return True\n return False\n\n def __str__(self) -> str:\n if self.minimum is not None:\n return f\"{self.minimum:g}-{self.maximum:g}\"\n if self.maximum is not None:\n return f\"{self.maximum:g}\"\n return \"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StandardEntry:\n parameter: str\n unit: str\n who_health: Optional[Limit]\n who_aesthetic: Optional[Limit]\n sl_standard: Optional[Limit]\n category: str\n note: str\n #: Where the national value came from. ``\"provisional\"`` means it has not\n #: been checked against the Sierra Leone Standards Bureau specification -\n #: it is a WHO figure carried across, or one adopted from regional\n #: practice. Set it to the issuing specification once confirmed.\n sl_source: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def sl_provisional(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether the national value is unconfirmed against the SLSB spec.\"\"\"\n return self.sl_standard is not None and self.sl_source == \"provisional\"\n\n\n#: Said wherever a national verdict is shown, while any national value is\n#: still provisional. A compliance failure against an unconfirmed limit is a\n#: prompt to check the specification, not a finding to put in front of a\n#: regulator.\nPROVISIONAL_NATIONAL_NOTE = (\n \"The national column in the standards table is provisional: its values \"\n \"are WHO guideline figures carried across, or limits adopted from \"\n \"regional practice, and have not been confirmed against the Sierra Leone \"\n \"Standards Bureau drinking water specification. Confirm the figures \"\n \"before treating a national exceedance as a compliance finding.\"\n)\n\n\ndef provisional_national_parameters(\n table: dict[str, \"StandardEntry\"] | None = None,\n) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Parameters whose national limit is still unconfirmed.\"\"\"\n entries = (table or load_standards()).values()\n return sorted(e.parameter for e in entries if e.sl_provisional)\n\n\n_ALIASES = {\n \"ec\": \"electrical conductivity\",\n \"conductivity\": \"electrical conductivity\",\n \"total dissolved solids\": \"tds\",\n \"hardness\": \"total hardness\",\n \"nitrate\": \"nitrate (as no3)\",\n \"no3\": \"nitrate (as no3)\",\n \"nitrite\": \"nitrite (as no2)\",\n \"no2\": \"nitrite (as no2)\",\n \"ammonia\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"ammonium\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"nh3\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"nh4\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"chromium\": \"chromium (total)\",\n \"cr\": \"chromium (total)\",\n \"faecal coliforms\": \"e. coli\",\n \"fecal coliforms\": \"e. coli\",\n \"e.coli\": \"e. coli\",\n \"escherichia coli\": \"e. coli\",\n \"coliforms\": \"total coliforms\",\n \"sulphate\": \"sulfate\",\n \"so4\": \"sulfate\",\n \"aluminum\": \"aluminium\",\n}\n\n\ndef normalise_parameter(name: str) -> str:\n key = re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", name.strip().lower())\n return _ALIASES.get(key, key)\n\n\n_PARAMETER_BASIS_RE = re.compile(r\"\\(\\s*as\\s+([^)]+?)\\s*\\)\")\n\n\ndef _parameter_basis(parameter: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"The chemical basis a parameter name states: \"Nitrate (as NO3)\" -> \"no3\".\"\"\"\n match = _PARAMETER_BASIS_RE.search(str(parameter or \"\"))\n return match.group(1).lower().replace(\" \", \"\") if match else \"\"\n\n\ndef to_standard_unit(\n value: float, reported_unit: str, entry: StandardEntry\n) -> tuple[Optional[float], str]:\n \"\"\"Put a reported value on the scale the standards table uses.\n\n Returns ``(converted, reason)``. ``converted`` is ``None`` when the value\n must not be used against this parameter's limits - an unreadable unit, or\n one that measures something else. That is never the same as zero, and a\n caller must drop the value rather than fall back to the raw number.\n\n ``reason`` is ``\"\"`` on a clean conversion, ``\"unit_assumed\"`` when the\n laboratory reported no usable unit and the guideline's own was assumed,\n ``\"unit_basis_assumed\"`` when one side names a chemical basis the other\n does not, or an ``INDETERMINATE_REASONS`` code on refusal.\n \"\"\"\n reported = str(reported_unit or \"\").strip()\n guideline = str(entry.unit or \"\").strip()\n\n # \"-\", \"n/a\" and friends normalise away to nothing: they are how a sheet\n # writes \"no unit here\", so they take the no-unit path rather than the\n # unreadable one.\n if reported and not normalise_unit_text(reported):\n reported = \"\"\n\n if not reported:\n # No unit on the sheet. The guideline's own unit is the only reading\n # under which the number means anything; the assumption is recorded\n # rather than hidden.\n return float(value), \"unit_assumed\"\n if not guideline:\n # The standards table itself names no unit, so there is no scale to\n # convert onto and nothing to disagree about.\n return float(value), \"\"\n if normalise_unit_text(reported) == normalise_unit_text(guideline):\n # Written the same way: same scale, whether or not the unit module has\n # ever heard of the unit. Keeps a newly added guideline unit from\n # making every sample indeterminate.\n return float(value), \"\"\n\n source = parse_unit(reported)\n target = parse_unit(guideline)\n\n if target is not None and target.dimension == \"ph\":\n # pH is the one absolute scale here with no rival: there is no such\n # thing as pH in another unit, so a sheet carrying \"mg/L\" beside a pH\n # of 7.2 is a template artefact, not a different measurement.\n if source is None or source.dimension != \"ph\":\n return float(value), \"unit_assumed\"\n return float(value), \"\"\n\n if source is None or target is None:\n return None, \"unit_unreadable\"\n if not comparable(source, target):\n return None, \"unit_mismatch\"\n converted = convert(value, reported, guideline)\n if converted is None: # pragma: no cover - comparable() already checked\n return None, \"unit_mismatch\"\n if source.basis and not target.basis:\n # The unit names a chemical reference the guideline's unit does not.\n # The parameter name often carries it instead, so look there before\n # deciding: \"Nitrate (as NO3)\" reported in \"mg/L as N\" is a different\n # number by a factor of 4.4, and grading it at face value passed a\n # sample at 44 mg/L as NO3 that the guideline puts over its limit.\n named = _parameter_basis(entry.parameter)\n if named and named != source.basis:\n return None, \"unit_basis_conflict\"\n if not named:\n # Nothing states the guideline's basis, so the reading is taken\n # but it is worth an analyst's eye: calcium as Ca and calcium as\n # CaCO3 differ by a factor of 2.5.\n return converted, \"unit_basis_assumed\"\n elif target.basis and not source.basis:\n return converted, \"unit_basis_assumed\"\n return converted, \"\"\n\n\ndef canonical_values(\n sample, table: dict[str, StandardEntry] | None = None\n) -> dict[str, float]:\n \"\"\"Every measured result in the sample, on the standards table's scale.\n\n Keyed by normalised parameter name. A result whose unit cannot be\n reconciled with its guideline is *left out* rather than passed through\n raw: the aggregate indices built on these numbers - the water quality\n index, the hazard index, the ionic balance, the corrosivity indices -\n all assume mg/L, and a sample reported in ug/L quietly produced a hazard\n index a thousand times too high and an \"unsuitable for drinking\" rating\n for clean water.\n \"\"\"\n table = table if table is not None else load_standards()\n values: dict[str, float] = {}\n for result in getattr(sample, \"results\", []):\n if result.value is None:\n continue\n key = normalise_parameter(result.parameter)\n entry = table.get(key)\n if entry is None:\n # No guideline entry, so no declared scale to convert onto. The\n # value is carried as written; nothing downstream has a limit for\n # it either.\n values[key] = float(result.value)\n continue\n converted, _ = to_standard_unit(float(result.value), result.unit, entry)\n if converted is not None:\n values[key] = converted\n return values\n\n\ndef load_standards(path: str | Path | None = None) -> dict[str, StandardEntry]:\n \"\"\"Load the standards table keyed by normalised parameter name.\"\"\"\n if path is None:\n source = resources.files(\"groundwater.data\").joinpath(\"who_guidelines.csv\")\n fh = source.open(\"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n else:\n fh = open(path, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n with fh:\n rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))\n table: dict[str, StandardEntry] = {}\n for row in rows:\n entry = StandardEntry(\n parameter=row[\"parameter\"],\n unit=row[\"unit\"],\n who_health=Limit.parse(row.get(\"who_health_gv\", \"\")),\n who_aesthetic=Limit.parse(row.get(\"who_aesthetic\", \"\")),\n sl_standard=Limit.parse(row.get(\"sl_standard\", \"\")),\n category=row.get(\"category\", \"\"),\n note=row.get(\"note\", \"\"),\n sl_source=(row.get(\"sl_source\") or \"\").strip(),\n )\n table[normalise_parameter(entry.parameter)] = entry\n return table\n"}, "groundwater/readiness.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Whether a project's results are complete enough to certify.\n\nA completion report is the document a borehole is handed over on. It gets\nfiled, invoiced against, and read years later by someone deciding whether\nthe village still has water. The toolkit will write one from whatever it\nhas - and it should, because an interim report is a real need - but it must\nnot let a document that rests on missing evidence look like one that does\nnot.\n\nSo every report carries its own provenance. This module answers one\nquestion, over the results the project already holds: which of the things a\ncertifiable report needs are actually established? The answer is a list of\n:class:`Requirement` records, each either met, unmet, not applicable, or\noverridden by a named person with a stated reason. A report built from a\nproject that is not ready is stamped PROVISIONAL on its cover and carries\nthe list; a report built from one that is ready is not stamped at all.\nNothing is blocked, and nothing is quietly passed off as final.\n\n**Completeness, not outcome.** A borehole whose water fails the arsenic\nguideline is a perfectly certifiable borehole: the finding is the point of\nthe report. What is not certifiable is a borehole whose arsenic result\ncould not be read. The requirements here ask \"do we know?\", never \"is the\nanswer the one we wanted?\" - a gate that failed bad news would teach people\nto leave the bad news out.\n\nThe signals are not re-derived. Every module in the toolkit already raises\n:class:`~groundwater.models.DataFlag` for what it could not do, and the\nwater quality assessment already exposes its own uncertainties; this module\nreads those. A requirement that invented its own check would drift from the\nanalysis it is supposed to describe.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable, Optional\n\n__all__ = [\n \"Requirement\",\n \"Readiness\",\n \"REPORTS\",\n \"REQUIREMENTS\",\n \"assess_readiness\",\n]\n\n#: Flag codes that mean a reading was refused, converted from an unreadable\n#: unit, or otherwise could not be used. Raised by ingestion/pumping.py and\n#: quality/assess.py; listed here so the gate and the parsers cannot drift.\n_UNIT_BLOCKERS = (\n \"time_unit_unknown\",\n \"discharge_unit_unknown\",\n \"discharge_ambiguous\",\n \"time_reading_unreadable\",\n)\n\n#: Codes that say a value was assumed rather than read. Not blocking - the\n#: assumption is stated in the report - but worth surfacing beside the gate.\n_UNIT_ASSUMPTIONS = (\n \"discharge_unit_assumed\",\n \"unit_not_reported\",\n \"unit_basis_assumed\",\n \"utm_zone_assumed\",\n \"test_type_inferred\",\n)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Requirement:\n \"\"\"One thing a certifiable report needs, and whether it is established.\"\"\"\n\n key: str\n title: str\n #: \"met\" | \"unmet\" | \"not_applicable\" | \"overridden\"\n state: str\n #: What was found, in a sentence an analyst can act on.\n detail: str\n #: Who overrode it and why, when ``state`` is \"overridden\".\n override_reason: str = \"\"\n override_by: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def satisfied(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether this requirement stops holding the report back.\n\n An override satisfies it for the purpose of issuing the document and\n is recorded in the document; it does not make the evidence exist.\n \"\"\"\n return self.state in (\"met\", \"not_applicable\", \"overridden\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Readiness:\n \"\"\"The readiness of one project for one kind of report.\"\"\"\n\n report: str\n requirements: list[Requirement] = field(default_factory=list)\n #: Assumptions the analysis made that the reader should see. Never\n #: blocking; a stated assumption is not a missing result.\n assumptions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def unmet(self) -> list[Requirement]:\n return [r for r in self.requirements if r.state == \"unmet\"]\n\n @property\n def overridden(self) -> list[Requirement]:\n return [r for r in self.requirements if r.state == \"overridden\"]\n\n @property\n def state(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"``\"ready\"``, ``\"ready_with_overrides\"`` or ``\"not_ready\"``.\"\"\"\n if self.unmet:\n return \"not_ready\"\n return \"ready_with_overrides\" if self.overridden else \"ready\"\n\n @property\n def is_certifiable(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether the document may be issued without a PROVISIONAL stamp.\n\n An override is deliberately *not* certifiable. Overriding says \"issue\n it anyway, on my authority\", which is a legitimate thing to need and\n a different thing from the evidence being there.\n \"\"\"\n return self.state == \"ready\"\n\n @property\n def summary(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"One line for a cover stamp or a status chip.\"\"\"\n if self.state == \"ready\":\n return \"All certification requirements are met.\"\n if self.state == \"ready_with_overrides\":\n names = \", \".join(r.title for r in self.overridden)\n return f\"Issued on override: {names}.\"\n names = \", \".join(r.title for r in self.unmet)\n return f\"Not ready to certify - outstanding: {names}.\"\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n \"\"\"JSON- and YAML-safe, so it round-trips in a saved project.\"\"\"\n return {\n \"report\": self.report,\n \"state\": self.state,\n \"requirements\": [\n {\n \"key\": r.key, \"title\": r.title, \"state\": r.state,\n \"detail\": r.detail, \"override_reason\": r.override_reason,\n \"override_by\": r.override_by,\n }\n for r in self.requirements\n ],\n \"assumptions\": list(self.assumptions),\n }\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The requirements themselves\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _flags(*objects) -> list:\n \"\"\"Every DataFlag carried by the objects given, skipping the absent.\"\"\"\n out = []\n for obj in objects:\n if obj is None:\n continue\n out.extend(getattr(obj, \"flags\", None) or [])\n return out\n\n\ndef _has(flags: Iterable, codes: Iterable[str]) -> list:\n wanted = set(codes)\n return [f for f in flags if getattr(f, \"code\", \"\") in wanted]\n\n\ndef _project_site(state: dict):\n \"\"\"The site, merged across whatever the project holds.\n\n Field crews write the position on one sheet and not the others, so a\n project can be perfectly well located while the drilling log's own header\n block is blank. ``SiteMetadata.merged_with`` fills blanks without\n overwriting anything, which is the same rule the app's header uses.\n \"\"\"\n site = state.get(\"site\")\n for obj in (state.get(\"drilling_log\"), state.get(\"wq_assessment\"),\n state.get(\"borehole_design\")):\n other = getattr(obj, \"site\", None) or getattr(\n getattr(obj, \"sample\", None), \"site\", None)\n if other is not None:\n site = other if site is None else site.merged_with(other)\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is not None:\n site = analysis.test.site if site is None else site.merged_with(\n analysis.test.site)\n return site\n\n\ndef _site_located(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n site = _project_site(state)\n if site is None or site.easting is None or site.northing is None:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"No GPS position is recorded on any sheet in this project. A \"\n \"borehole that cannot be found again on the ground cannot be \"\n \"certified, revisited or maintained.\"\n )\n from .ingestion.checks import check_site_consistency\n\n errors = [f for f in check_site_consistency(site) if f.level == \"error\"]\n if errors:\n return \"unmet\", errors[0].message\n return \"met\", f\"Position recorded: {site.utm}.\"\n\n\ndef _borehole_logged(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n log = state.get(\"drilling_log\")\n if log is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No drilling log has been loaded.\"\n if not log.total_depth_m:\n return \"unmet\", \"The drilling log records no total depth.\"\n if not log.intervals:\n return \"unmet\", \"The drilling log records no lithology.\"\n return \"met\", (\n f\"Logged to {log.total_depth_m:.0f} m with {len(log.intervals)} \"\n \"lithological interval(s).\"\n )\n\n\ndef _pumping_measured(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No pumping test has been analysed.\"\n test = analysis.test\n if test.static_water_level_m is None:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"The static water level is missing, so no drawdown can be \"\n \"computed from the test.\"\n )\n if not test.has_discharge:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"No discharge is recorded for the test, so transmissivity and \"\n \"yield stay pending.\"\n )\n missing = [s.step_number for s in test.steps if s.discharge_m3_per_h is None]\n if missing:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"Discharge is missing for step(s) \"\n + \", \".join(str(n) for n in missing) + \".\"\n )\n return \"met\", (\n f\"{len(test.steps)} step(s) with discharge, static water level \"\n f\"{test.static_water_level_m:.2f} m.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _readings_usable(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"No reading was refused for a unit the toolkit could not read.\"\"\"\n flags = _flags(state.get(\"pump_analysis\"), state.get(\"drilling_log\"))\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is not None:\n flags += analysis.test.flags or []\n refused = _has(flags, _UNIT_BLOCKERS)\n if refused:\n return \"unmet\", \"; \".join(f.message for f in refused)\n return \"met\", \"Every reading carried a unit the toolkit could read.\"\n\n\ndef _yield_established(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is None or analysis.yield_recommendation is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No yield recommendation has been derived.\"\n rec = analysis.yield_recommendation\n if rec.pending_reason:\n return \"unmet\", rec.pending_reason\n if rec.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"The safe yield could not be derived from this test.\"\n return \"met\", f\"Safe yield {rec.yield_range_text}.\"\n\n\ndef _water_quality_evaluable(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Every determinand in the sample was graded against a limit.\n\n Deliberately not \"the verdict state is not indeterminate\". A health\n exceedance outranks uncertainty in the *verdict* - and rightly, since a\n demonstrated failure is a finding - but it does not make an unreadable\n arsenic result readable. Certifying is about the evidence, so the rows\n are checked, not the headline.\n \"\"\"\n assessment = state.get(\"wq_assessment\")\n if assessment is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No water quality results have been assessed.\"\n ungraded = assessment.indeterminate_rows + assessment.unknown_parameters\n if ungraded:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"Not graded against any limit: \"\n + \", \".join(dict.fromkeys(r.parameter for r in ungraded))\n + \".\"\n )\n if not assessment.evaluated_rows:\n return \"unmet\", \"No result in the sample could be graded.\"\n return \"met\", (\n f\"{len(assessment.evaluated_rows)} determinand(s) graded; verdict \"\n f\"{assessment.verdict_state}.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _water_quality_panel(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n assessment = state.get(\"wq_assessment\")\n if assessment is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No water quality results have been assessed.\"\n if assessment.missing_essential:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"No evaluable result for \"\n + \", \".join(assessment.missing_essential) + \".\"\n )\n return \"met\", \"The health panel was run and every result was evaluable.\"\n\n\ndef _design_derived(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n design = state.get(\"borehole_design\")\n if design is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No borehole design has been derived.\"\n errors = [f for f in (design.flags or []) if f.level == \"error\"]\n if errors:\n return \"unmet\", errors[0].message\n if not design.screens:\n return \"unmet\", \"The design places no screen.\"\n return \"met\", (\n f\"{design.total_screen_length_m:.1f} m of screen in \"\n f\"{len(design.screens)} run(s).\"\n )\n\n\ndef _no_errors(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Nothing anywhere raised an error-level flag.\n\n A catch-all, deliberately last: a module that learns to report a new\n fatal condition is covered by the gate the day it does, without this\n file having to be edited.\n \"\"\"\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n sources = [\n state.get(\"drilling_log\"), analysis, state.get(\"wq_assessment\"),\n state.get(\"borehole_design\"), state.get(\"cost_estimate\"),\n ]\n if analysis is not None:\n sources.append(analysis.test)\n errors = [f for f in _flags(*sources) if f.level == \"error\"]\n if errors:\n return \"unmet\", \"; \".join(dict.fromkeys(f.message for f in errors))\n return \"met\", \"No module reported a fatal problem with the data.\"\n\n\n#: Every requirement, in the order a reader should see them: the borehole\n#: first, then what was measured in it, then what it produced.\nREQUIREMENTS: dict[str, tuple[str, Any]] = {\n \"site_located\": (\"Site position\", _site_located),\n \"borehole_logged\": (\"Drilling log\", _borehole_logged),\n # Negative checks: vacuously met when there is nothing to have gone wrong\n # with, which is harmless because the positive requirements beside them\n # (a log, a test, a sample) already catch absence.\n \"readings_usable\": (\"Readable units\", _readings_usable),\n \"pumping_measured\": (\"Pumping test measured\", _pumping_measured),\n \"yield_established\": (\"Yield established\", _yield_established),\n \"water_quality_panel\": (\"Water quality panel\", _water_quality_panel),\n \"water_quality_evaluable\": (\"Water quality evaluable\", _water_quality_evaluable),\n \"design_derived\": (\"Borehole design\", _design_derived),\n \"no_errors\": (\"No fatal data problems\", _no_errors),\n}\n\n#: What each report has to be able to stand behind. A pumping report makes\n#: no claim about water quality, so an unassessed sample does not hold it\n#: back; a handover report tells a village the water is safe to drink, so it\n#: needs everything.\nREPORTS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n \"completion\": (\n \"site_located\", \"borehole_logged\", \"readings_usable\",\n \"pumping_measured\", \"yield_established\", \"water_quality_panel\",\n \"water_quality_evaluable\", \"design_derived\", \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"handover\": (\n \"site_located\", \"borehole_logged\", \"pumping_measured\",\n \"yield_established\", \"water_quality_panel\", \"water_quality_evaluable\",\n \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"quality\": (\n \"site_located\", \"water_quality_panel\", \"water_quality_evaluable\",\n \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"pumping\": (\n \"site_located\", \"readings_usable\", \"pumping_measured\",\n \"yield_established\", \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"geophysical\": (\"site_located\",),\n \"costing\": (\"site_located\", \"borehole_logged\", \"design_derived\"),\n \"supervision\": (\"site_located\",),\n}\n\n\ndef assess_readiness(\n state: dict,\n report: str = \"completion\",\n overrides: Optional[dict] = None,\n) -> Readiness:\n \"\"\"Judge one project against what one kind of report has to stand behind.\n\n ``state`` is keyed as the app's session is - ``site``, ``drilling_log``,\n ``pump_analysis``, ``wq_assessment``, ``borehole_design``,\n ``cost_estimate`` - so the app can pass its session straight in and a\n test can pass a dict.\n\n ``overrides`` maps a requirement key to ``{\"reason\": ..., \"by\": ...}``\n (a bare string is taken as the reason). An override is recorded on the\n requirement and reproduced on the report, and never makes the project\n certifiable - only issuable.\n \"\"\"\n overrides = overrides or {}\n keys = REPORTS.get(report, REPORTS[\"completion\"])\n requirements: list[Requirement] = []\n\n for key in keys:\n title, check = REQUIREMENTS[key]\n try:\n found, detail = check(state)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - a broken check is not a pass\n found, detail = \"unmet\", (\n f\"The {title.lower()} check could not run: \"\n f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"\n )\n override = overrides.get(key)\n if found == \"unmet\" and override:\n reason = override.get(\"reason\", \"\") if isinstance(override, dict) else str(override)\n by = override.get(\"by\", \"\") if isinstance(override, dict) else \"\"\n requirements.append(Requirement(\n key=key, title=title, state=\"overridden\", detail=detail,\n override_reason=reason, override_by=by,\n ))\n continue\n requirements.append(\n Requirement(key=key, title=title, state=found, detail=detail)\n )\n\n try:\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n sources = [\n state.get(\"drilling_log\"), analysis, state.get(\"wq_assessment\"),\n state.get(\"borehole_design\"),\n ]\n if analysis is not None:\n sources.append(analysis.test)\n assumptions = list(dict.fromkeys(\n f.message for f in _has(_flags(*sources), _UNIT_ASSUMPTIONS)\n ))\n except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a malformed object costs the list, not the gate\n assumptions = []\n return Readiness(report=report, requirements=requirements,\n assumptions=assumptions)\n"}, "groundwater/recompute.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Recompute analysis objects from the data sources saved in a project.\n\nThe web app stores the raw uploaded data files (or a reference to a bundled\nsample) in the project file, plus the few extra inputs an analysis needs\nthat are not in the file itself (pumping-test step discharges and the\nborehole-design static water level). On load, this module rebuilds the\nresult objects so the reports can be regenerated without re-uploading.\n\nA rebuild that fails is *reported*, not swallowed. It used to be: four bare\n``except Exception: pass`` blocks turned a failed rebuild into an absent\ndictionary key, and every consumer reads an absent key as \"the user never\nsupplied that data\". So a project whose water-quality workbook no longer\nparsed came back looking like a borehole nobody had ever sampled - the\noverview showed the stage as not started, the portfolio summary carried no\nverdict, and the handover report was written without a water-quality\nsection. Nothing anywhere said a file had failed to load.\n\nFailures are still contained - one bad source must not cost the other three\n- but each one now produces a :class:`RecomputeIssue` naming what failed,\nwhich file it was, and what to do about it.\n\nPure and Streamlit-free, so the round trip is unit-testable.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .config import Config\nfrom .design import design_borehole\nfrom .hydraulics import analyse_pumping_test\nfrom .ingestion import (\n read_drilling_workbook,\n read_pumping_docx,\n read_pumping_workbook,\n read_quality_workbook,\n read_ves_workbook,\n)\nfrom .quality import assess_sample\nfrom .ves import interpret_model, invert_sounding\nfrom .ves.interpret import rank_interpretations\n\n_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n#: The session key each upload key produces. An issue names it even when the\n#: file could not be opened at all: the key really is absent, and a banner\n#: that cannot say which result is missing can never be cleared when the\n#: analyst supplies it by hand.\nSOURCE_RESULTS = {\n \"ves\": \"ves_results\",\n \"wiz_ves\": \"ves_results\",\n \"pump\": \"pump_analysis\",\n \"wq\": \"wq_assessment\",\n \"log\": \"drilling_log\",\n}\n\n#: What each upload key is called in front of a user.\nSOURCE_LABELS = {\n \"ves\": \"Geophysics (VES)\",\n \"wiz_ves\": \"Geophysics (VES)\",\n \"pump\": \"Pumping test\",\n \"wq\": \"Water quality\",\n \"log\": \"Drilling log\",\n}\n\n#: Why a source did not produce its result.\nISSUE_CODES = {\n \"bad_payload\": \"the saved file content could not be read\",\n \"unreadable_file\": \"the saved file could not be written to disk\",\n \"missing_sample\": \"the bundled sample it refers to is no longer present\",\n \"outside_sample_root\": \"it refers to a file outside the sample directory\",\n \"parse_error\": \"the workbook could not be parsed\",\n \"analysis_error\": \"the data parsed but the analysis failed\",\n \"sounding_failed\": \"one sounding could not be inverted\",\n \"recompute_crashed\": \"the rebuild itself failed\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass RecomputeIssue:\n \"\"\"One saved source that did not produce its result.\"\"\"\n\n source: str # upload key: \"ves\" | \"wiz_ves\" | \"pump\" | \"wq\" | \"log\"\n result: str # the session key now absent, \"\" for a partial failure\n label: str # what the user calls it: \"Water quality\"\n level: str # \"error\" (no result at all) | \"warning\" (partial result)\n code: str # a key of ISSUE_CODES\n message: str # one plain, actionable sentence\n context: str = \"\" # the file name or sample path the user recognises\n detail: str = \"\" # \"ValueError: ...\", truncated\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:\n return asdict(self)\n\n\ndef _issue(source, result, code, message, context=\"\", exc=None, level=\"error\"):\n detail = \"\"\n if exc is not None:\n detail = f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"[:300]\n return RecomputeIssue(\n source=source,\n result=result,\n label=SOURCE_LABELS.get(source, source),\n level=level,\n code=code,\n message=message,\n context=context,\n detail=detail,\n )\n\n\ndef _source_name(source) -> str:\n if not isinstance(source, dict):\n return \"\"\n return str(source.get(\"name\") or source.get(\"sample\") or \"\")\n\n\ndef _materialize(source, sample_root, tmp_dir) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:\n \"\"\"Turn a saved source into a readable file path.\n\n Never raises. Returns ``(path, \"\")`` on success or ``(None, code)`` with\n a code from :data:`ISSUE_CODES`, so the caller can say which of several\n quite different failures happened rather than reporting them all as an\n absent file.\n \"\"\"\n if not isinstance(source, dict):\n return None, \"bad_payload\"\n if source.get(\"bytes\") is not None:\n try:\n # basename only, so a hand-edited project cannot write outside tmp_dir\n name = os.path.basename(str(source.get(\"name\") or \"data\")) or \"data\"\n path = Path(tmp_dir) / name\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n path.write_bytes(bytes(source[\"bytes\"]))\n return path, \"\"\n except OSError:\n return None, \"unreadable_file\"\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n # a str or out-of-range payload from a hand-edited project file;\n # this used to escape the function entirely and abort the whole load\n return None, \"bad_payload\"\n if source.get(\"sample\") and sample_root is not None:\n try:\n root = Path(sample_root).resolve()\n candidate = (root / str(source[\"sample\"])).resolve()\n except OSError:\n return None, \"unreadable_file\"\n if not candidate.is_relative_to(root):\n return None, \"outside_sample_root\"\n if not candidate.exists():\n return None, \"missing_sample\"\n return candidate, \"\"\n return None, \"bad_payload\"\n\n\ndef recompute_results(\n sources: dict,\n discharges: dict | None = None,\n design_swl: float | None = None,\n config: Config | None = None,\n sample_root=None,\n tmp_dir=\".\",\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Rebuild the analysis objects a saved project needs.\n\n ``sources`` maps an upload key (``ves``/``wiz_ves``/``pump``/``wq``/``log``)\n to a source dict. Returns session updates keyed like the app's session\n state (``ves_results``, ``pump_analysis``, ``wq_assessment``,\n ``borehole_design``, ``drilling_log``), plus ``recompute_diagnostics``\n - always present - carrying ``{\"ok\": [...], \"issues\": [...]}``. A source\n that fails is skipped and recorded; it never aborts the others.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or Config()\n discharges = discharges or {}\n out: dict = {}\n issues: list[RecomputeIssue] = []\n ok: list[str] = []\n\n def _path(key) -> Path | None:\n \"\"\"Resolve one source, recording why if it cannot be resolved.\"\"\"\n source = sources.get(key)\n if not source:\n return None\n path, code = _materialize(source, sample_root, tmp_dir)\n if path is None:\n issues.append(_issue(\n key, SOURCE_RESULTS.get(key, \"\"), code,\n f\"{SOURCE_LABELS.get(key, key)}: the saved file could not be \"\n f\"opened because {ISSUE_CODES[code]}. Upload it again.\",\n context=_source_name(source),\n ))\n return path\n\n # VES: the main tab wins over the guided-wizard upload\n ves_key = \"ves\" if sources.get(\"ves\") else \"wiz_ves\"\n ves_path = _path(\"ves\") or _path(\"wiz_ves\")\n if ves_path is not None:\n try:\n soundings = read_ves_workbook(ves_path)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - reported, not swallowed\n _log.exception(\"VES workbook could not be parsed\")\n soundings = None\n issues.append(_issue(\n ves_key, \"ves_results\", \"parse_error\",\n \"The geophysics workbook could not be read, so the soundings \"\n \"were not restored. Open it and check the layout, or upload it \"\n \"again.\",\n context=ves_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n if soundings:\n kept, results, interps = [], [], []\n # Per sounding, so one bad curve costs one curve rather than the\n # whole survey.\n for sounding in soundings:\n try:\n result = invert_sounding(sounding, config.ves)\n interps.append(interpret_model(sounding, result.model, config.ves))\n results.append(result)\n kept.append(sounding)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"sounding %s could not be inverted\", sounding.label)\n issues.append(_issue(\n ves_key, \"\", \"sounding_failed\",\n f\"Sounding {sounding.label} could not be inverted and \"\n \"was left out; the other soundings were restored.\",\n context=sounding.label, exc=exc, level=\"warning\",\n ))\n if kept:\n #
