MN/2.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef geometric_factor(\n array_type: str,\n ab2: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n mn: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n a: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n n: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Geometric factor K such that rho_a = K * (delta V / I).\n\n Parameters\n ----------\n array_type:\n \"schlumberger\", \"wenner\", \"dipole-dipole\" or \"pole-pole\".\n ab2:\n Half current electrode spacing AB/2 (Schlumberger).\n mn:\n Full potential electrode spacing MN (Schlumberger).\n a:\n Electrode spacing (Wenner) or dipole length (dipole-dipole,\n pole-pole).\n n:\n Dipole separation multiplier (dipole-dipole).\n\n For the Schlumberger array with finite MN the exact factor is\n ``K = pi (L^2 - b^2) / (2 b)`` with L = AB/2 and b = MN/2.\n \"\"\"\n kind = array_type.strip().lower()\n if kind.startswith(\"schlum\"):\n if ab2 is None or mn is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Schlumberger needs ab2 and mn\")\n L = np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float)\n b = np.asarray(mn, dtype=float) / 2.0\n if np.any(b <= 0) or np.any(L <= b):\n raise ValueError(\"Require 0 < MN/2 < AB/2 for Schlumberger\")\n return np.pi * (L**2 - b**2) / (2.0 * b)\n if kind.startswith(\"wenner\"):\n if a is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Wenner needs the spacing a\")\n return 2.0 * np.pi * np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n if kind.startswith(\"dipole\"):\n if a is None or n is None:\n raise ValueError(\"dipole-dipole needs a and n\")\n a_arr = np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n n_arr = np.asarray(n, dtype=float)\n return np.pi * n_arr * (n_arr + 1) * (n_arr + 2) * a_arr\n if kind.startswith(\"pole-pole\") or kind.startswith(\"pole pole\"):\n if a is None:\n raise ValueError(\"pole-pole needs the spacing a\")\n return 2.0 * np.pi * np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n raise ValueError(f\"Unknown array type: {array_type}\")\n\n\ndef apparent_resistivity(\n array_type: str,\n resistance_ohm: float | np.ndarray,\n **spacings,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Apparent resistivity from measured resistance (delta V / I).\"\"\"\n K = geometric_factor(array_type, **spacings)\n return K * np.asarray(resistance_ohm, dtype=float)\n"}, "groundwater/ves/classify.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Sounding curve type classification (H, K, A, Q and combinations).\n\nFor three layers the classical types are\n\n* H: rho1 > rho2 < rho3 (conductive middle layer)\n* K: rho1 < rho2 > rho3 (resistive middle layer)\n* A: rho1 < rho2 < rho3 (ascending)\n* Q: rho1 > rho2 > rho3 (descending)\n\nModels with more layers are classified by the sequence of overlapping\nthree layer triplets, giving the usual combined names such as HK, KH,\nHKH or QQ.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel\n\n__all__ = [\"classify_curve\", \"describe_curve_type\"]\n\n_TRIPLET = {\n (1, 0): \"K\", # up then down\n (0, 1): \"H\", # down then up\n (1, 1): \"A\", # up, up\n (0, 0): \"Q\", # down, down\n}\n\n\ndef classify_curve(model: LayeredModel) -> str:\n \"\"\"Curve type letters for a layered model.\n\n Two layer models return \"2-layer ascending\" or \"2-layer\n descending\"; models with three or more layers return letter codes.\n \"\"\"\n rho = np.asarray(model.resistivities, dtype=float)\n if len(rho) < 2:\n return \"uniform\"\n if len(rho) == 2:\n return \"2-layer ascending\" if rho[1] > rho[0] else \"2-layer descending\"\n letters = []\n for i in range(len(rho) - 2):\n up1 = 1 if rho[i + 1] > rho[i] else 0\n up2 = 1 if rho[i + 2] > rho[i + 1] else 0\n letters.append(_TRIPLET[(up1, up2)])\n return \"\".join(letters)\n\n\n_DESCRIPTIONS = {\n \"H\": \"a conductive layer between two more resistive layers, the classical \"\n \"signature of a saturated weathered zone above fresh basement\",\n \"K\": \"a resistive layer between two more conductive layers, often dry \"\n \"laterite or duricrust over a conductive saprolite\",\n \"A\": \"resistivity increasing with depth, typical of progressively less \"\n \"weathered rock towards fresh basement\",\n \"Q\": \"resistivity decreasing with depth, typical of deepening weathering \"\n \"or increasing saturation with depth\",\n}\n\n\ndef describe_curve_type(curve_type: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Short hydrogeological reading of a curve type for report text.\"\"\"\n if curve_type.startswith(\"2-layer\"):\n direction = \"ascending\" if \"ascending\" in curve_type else \"descending\"\n if direction == \"descending\":\n return (\n \"a two layer response with resistivity decreasing at depth, \"\n \"consistent with weathered or fractured, possibly water bearing \"\n \"rock beneath a resistive surface layer\"\n )\n return (\n \"a two layer response with resistivity increasing at depth, \"\n \"consistent with more competent rock beneath the surface layer\"\n )\n parts = [f\"type {curve_type}\"]\n seen = []\n for letter in curve_type:\n if letter in _DESCRIPTIONS and letter not in seen:\n seen.append(letter)\n parts.append(_DESCRIPTIONS[letter])\n return \"; \".join(parts)\n"}, "groundwater/ves/forward.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"1D layered earth forward modelling for resistivity soundings.\n\nThe apparent resistivity over a stack of horizontal layers is obtained\nfrom the resistivity transform ``T(lambda)`` (Koefoed recurrence) and\na Hankel transform:\n\n* ideal Schlumberger (gradient array, MN -> 0)::\n\n rho_a(L) = L^2 * Int_0^inf T(lam) J1(lam L) lam dlam\n\n* finite MN Schlumberger, from the surface potential\n ``F(r) = Int_0^inf T(lam) J0(lam r) dlam``::\n\n rho_a = (L^2 - b^2) / (2 b) * [F(L - b) - F(L + b)], b = MN/2\n\n* Wenner::\n\n rho_a(a) = 2 a * [F(a) - F(2a)]\n\nThe integrals are evaluated by direct quadrature on a hybrid\nlogarithmic + linear abscissa after subtracting the half space\nasymptote (``T -> rho_1`` for large lambda), which makes the integrand\ndecay exponentially. This avoids relying on tabulated digital filter\ncoefficients and is validated against the analytic two layer image\nseries in the test suite (agreement better than 0.2 percent).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom numpy.polynomial.legendre import leggauss\nfrom scipy.special import j0, j1, jn_zeros\n\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel, VESSounding\n\n__all__ = [\n \"resistivity_transform\",\n \"forward_schlumberger\",\n \"forward_schlumberger_finite_mn\",\n \"forward_wenner\",\n \"forward_for_sounding\",\n \"two_layer_schlumberger_series\",\n]\n\n\ndef resistivity_transform(\n lam: np.ndarray, resistivities: np.ndarray, thicknesses: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Koefoed/Pekeris recurrence for the resistivity transform T(lambda).\n\n Stable downward recurrence starting from the half space:\n ``T_n = rho_n``;\n ``T_i = (T_{i+1} + rho_i tanh(lam h_i)) / (1 + T_{i+1} tanh(lam h_i) / rho_i)``.\n \"\"\"\n lam = np.asarray(lam, dtype=float)\n rho = np.asarray(resistivities, dtype=float)\n h = np.asarray(thicknesses, dtype=float)\n T = np.full_like(lam, rho[-1])\n for i in range(len(h) - 1, -1, -1):\n th = np.tanh(lam * h[i])\n T = (T + rho[i] * th) / (1.0 + T * th / rho[i])\n return T\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Hankel integration machinery\n#\n# Integrals of the form Int_0^inf g(x) Jn(x) dx with g smooth and\n# exponentially decaying are computed in two sections:\n#\n# * x in (0, z1), z1 the first zero of Jn: composite Gauss-Legendre on\n# log-subdivided panels. The resistivity transform varies over about\n# a decade of lambda, so sub-decade panels resolve it for any layer\n# thickness / spacing ratio.\n# * x > z1: 10 point Gauss-Legendre panels between consecutive zeros\n# of Jn. Within a half period the integrand is smooth, so each panel\n# is near exact. The number of panels follows the exponential decay\n# scale of (T - rho1).\n#\n# Nodes and (weight x Bessel) products are precomputed once per order,\n# so each integral is two vectorised evaluations of g.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n_N_ZEROS = 1200\n\n# The quadrature runs out to the largest tabulated Bessel zero. A sounding\n# needs panels out to 9 * (AB/2) / h_min, so 1200 zeros (largest abscissa\n# 3770.7) covers spacings up to about 419 times the thinnest layer. Beyond\n# that the table is grown on demand: truncating the integral part-way\n# through an oscillation of J1 leaves a large spurious residue - at AB/2 =\n# 1000 m over a 0.5 m layer the model returned 574 ohm-m instead of 30.\n# The inversion explores thin layers, so it can walk into that regime.\n# Growth ceiling. 60000 zeros reach x = 188495, covering spacings up to about\n# 20900 times the thinnest layer - far past anything a real sounding sees, and\n# bounded so the browser build cannot be made to allocate without limit.\n_MAX_ZEROS = 60_000\n\n# Floor on the layer thickness used to size the decay scale. The inversion\n# bounds thicknesses at 0.2 m; this only guards a hand-built degenerate model.\n_MIN_DECAY_H = 0.02\n\n\ndef _build_tables(order: int, n_zeros: int = _N_ZEROS):\n zeros = jn_zeros(order, n_zeros)\n bessel = j0 if order == 0 else j1\n\n # section 1: 14 log-spaced panels from 1e-6 to the first zero, GL-8\n nodes8, weights8 = leggauss(8)\n edges = np.geomspace(1e-6, zeros[0], 15)\n s1_nodes, s1_wb = [], []\n for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):\n mid, half = 0.5 * (lo + hi), 0.5 * (hi - lo)\n x = mid + half * nodes8\n s1_nodes.append(x)\n s1_wb.append(half * weights8 * bessel(x))\n\n # section 2: GL-10 between consecutive zeros\n nodes10, weights10 = leggauss(10)\n s2_nodes, s2_wb = [], []\n lo = zeros[0]\n for hi in zeros[1:]:\n mid, half = 0.5 * (lo + hi), 0.5 * (hi - lo)\n x = mid + half * nodes10\n s2_nodes.append(x)\n s2_wb.append(half * weights10 * bessel(x))\n lo = hi\n return {\n \"s1_nodes\": np.concatenate(s1_nodes),\n \"s1_wb\": np.concatenate(s1_wb),\n \"s2_nodes\": np.concatenate(s2_nodes),\n \"s2_wb\": np.concatenate(s2_wb),\n \"panel_ends\": zeros[1:],\n }\n\n\n_TABLES = {0: _build_tables(0), 1: _build_tables(1)}\n\n\ndef _table_for(order: int, x_stop: float) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Quadrature table for ``order`` reaching at least ``x_stop``.\n\n Grows (and caches) the table rather than truncating the integral, which\n silently returned resistivities an order of magnitude wrong.\n \"\"\"\n table = _TABLES[order]\n if table[\"panel_ends\"][-1] >= x_stop or len(table[\"panel_ends\"]) + 1 >= _MAX_ZEROS:\n return table\n # zeros of J are spaced about pi apart, so this is the count that reaches\n # x_stop, with headroom so a sweep of spacings does not rebuild each time\n needed = min(int(x_stop / math.pi) + 32, _MAX_ZEROS)\n needed = min(max(needed, 2 * (len(table[\"panel_ends\"]) + 1)), _MAX_ZEROS)\n table = _build_tables(order, needed)\n _TABLES[order] = table\n return table\n\n\ndef _hankel_integral(g, order: int, x_decay: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Int_0^inf g(x) J_order(x) dx for smooth g decaying like\n exp(-x / x_decay) at large x.\"\"\"\n x_stop = 18.0 * max(x_decay, 1.0)\n t = _table_for(order, x_stop)\n acc = float(np.dot(g(t[\"s1_nodes\"]), t[\"s1_wb\"]))\n n_panels = int(np.searchsorted(t[\"panel_ends\"], x_stop)) + 1\n n_panels = min(max(n_panels, 8), len(t[\"panel_ends\"]))\n k = n_panels * 10\n acc += float(np.dot(g(t[\"s2_nodes\"][:k]), t[\"s2_wb\"][:k]))\n return acc\n\n\ndef forward_schlumberger(\n model: LayeredModel | tuple, ab2: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Ideal (gradient) Schlumberger apparent resistivity at AB/2 values.\"\"\"\n rho, h = _model_arrays(model)\n ab2 = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float))\n h_min = float(np.min(h)) if len(h) else 1.0\n out = np.empty_like(ab2)\n for i, L in enumerate(ab2):\n # substitute x = lambda L: rho_a = rho1 + Int (T(x/L) - rho1) J1(x) x dx\n # (the L^2 prefactor cancels against the 1/L^2 from the substitution)\n def g(x, L=L):\n return (resistivity_transform(x / L, rho, h) - rho[0]) * x\n\n # (T - rho1) decays like exp(-2 lambda h_min) = exp(-x / (L / (2 h_min)))\n out[i] = rho[0] + _hankel_integral(g, 1, L / (2.0 * max(h_min, _MIN_DECAY_H)))\n return out\n\n\ndef _potential_integral(rho, h, r: float, h_min: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"F(r) = Int T(lam) J0(lam r) dlam = (rho1 + Int (T - rho1) J0(x) dx) / r.\"\"\"\n\n def g(x, r=r):\n return resistivity_transform(x / r, rho, h) - rho[0]\n\n return (rho[0] + _hankel_integral(g, 0, r / (2.0 * max(h_min, _MIN_DECAY_H)))) / r\n\n\ndef forward_schlumberger_finite_mn(\n model: LayeredModel | tuple, ab2: np.ndarray, mn: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Schlumberger apparent resistivity with finite MN spacing.\n\n Reproduces what the instrument actually measures at each\n (AB/2, MN) pair, including the small jumps at segment changes.\n \"\"\"\n rho, h = _model_arrays(model)\n ab2 = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float))\n mn = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(mn, dtype=float))\n h_min = float(np.min(h)) if len(h) else 1.0\n out = np.empty_like(ab2)\n for i, (L, m) in enumerate(zip(ab2, mn)):\n b = m / 2.0\n if not np.isfinite(b) or b <= 0 or b >= L:\n # fall back to the ideal gradient value\n out[i] = forward_schlumberger((rho, h), np.array([L]))[0]\n continue\n f_in = _potential_integral(rho, h, L - b, h_min)\n f_out = _potential_integral(rho, h, L + b, h_min)\n out[i] = (L**2 - b**2) / (2.0 * b) * (f_in - f_out)\n return out\n\n\ndef forward_wenner(model: LayeredModel | tuple, a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Wenner apparent resistivity at spacings a.\"\"\"\n rho, h = _model_arrays(model)\n a = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(a, dtype=float))\n h_min = float(np.min(h)) if len(h) else 1.0\n out = np.empty_like(a)\n for i, s in enumerate(a):\n f1 = _potential_integral(rho, h, s, h_min)\n f2 = _potential_integral(rho, h, 2.0 * s, h_min)\n # rho_a = 2 pi a (V_M - V_N)/I; with A and B both contributing,\n # V_M - V_N = (I/pi) (F(a) - F(2a)), so rho_a = 2 a (F(a) - F(2a)).\n out[i] = 2.0 * s * (f1 - f2)\n return out\n\n\ndef forward_for_sounding(\n model: LayeredModel | tuple,\n sounding: VESSounding,\n finite_mn: bool = False,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Model response at a sounding's abscissas.\"\"\"\n if sounding.array_type.startswith(\"wenner\"):\n return forward_wenner(model, sounding.ab2)\n if finite_mn and np.all(np.isfinite(sounding.mn)):\n return forward_schlumberger_finite_mn(model, sounding.ab2, sounding.mn)\n return forward_schlumberger(model, sounding.ab2)\n\n\ndef two_layer_schlumberger_series(\n rho1: float, rho2: float, h: float, ab2: np.ndarray, n_terms: int = 4000\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Analytic two layer ideal Schlumberger curve from image theory.\n\n ``rho_a(L) = rho1 [1 + 2 sum_n k^n L^3 / (L^2 + (2 n h)^2)^(3/2)]``\n with reflection coefficient k = (rho2 - rho1) / (rho2 + rho1).\n Used to validate the numerical Hankel evaluation.\n \"\"\"\n ab2 = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float))\n k = (rho2 - rho1) / (rho2 + rho1)\n n = np.arange(1, n_terms + 1)[:, None]\n L = ab2[None, :]\n terms = (k**n) * L**3 / (L**2 + (2.0 * n * h) ** 2) ** 1.5\n return rho1 * (1.0 + 2.0 * np.sum(terms, axis=0))\n\n\ndef _model_arrays(model: LayeredModel | tuple) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n if isinstance(model, LayeredModel):\n return model.resistivities, model.thicknesses\n rho, h = model\n return np.asarray(rho, dtype=float), np.asarray(h, dtype=float)\n"}, "groundwater/ves/interpret.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Hydrogeological interpretation of layered models.\n\nThe rules target crystalline basement terrain typical of Sierra Leone:\na lateritic or clayey cover, saprolite, a weathered/fractured zone\nthat forms the main aquifer, and fresh basement at depth. Thresholds\nlive in :class:`~groundwater.config.VESConfig` so they can be tuned\nper area (coastal sedimentary sites use different ranges).\n\nOutputs:\n\n* per layer lithological/hydrogeological labels,\n* possible water zones as depth ranges,\n* estimated depth to (fresh) basement and aquifer thickness,\n* a recommended maximum drilling depth,\n* the ranked drilling preference table used in survey reports.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import VESConfig\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel, VESSounding\nfrom ..utils import fmt_num, ordinal\nfrom .classify import classify_curve, describe_curve_type\n\n__all__ = [\n \"LayerInterpretation\",\n \"SiteInterpretation\",\n \"interpret_model\",\n \"drilling_preference_table\",\n \"rank_interpretations\",\n]\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass LayerInterpretation:\n number: int\n rho: float\n thickness_m: float | None # None for the half space\n top_m: float\n bottom_m: float # inf for the half space\n unit: str\n water_bearing: bool\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SiteInterpretation:\n sounding_id: str\n model: LayeredModel\n curve_type: str\n layers: list[LayerInterpretation]\n water_zones: list[tuple[float, float]]\n depth_to_basement_m: float | None\n aquifer_thickness_m: float\n max_drilling_depth_m: float\n investigation_depth_m: float\n score: float # used for ranking between sites\n # Dar-Zarrouk parameters over the resolved overburden\n longitudinal_conductance_s: float = 0.0 # siemens, Sum(h/rho), full section\n transverse_resistance_t: float = 0.0 # ohm m2, Sum(h*rho), full section\n # conductance of the cover overlying the aquifer, used for protection\n protective_conductance_s: float = 0.0\n protective_capacity: str = \"\" # from the protective (cover) conductance\n narrative: str = \"\"\n rank: int | None = None\n site_easting: float | None = None\n site_northing: float | None = None\n site_elevation_m: float | None = None\n flags: list = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\ndef _unit_label(\n rho: float, is_top: bool, is_bottom: bool, config: VESConfig\n) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n \"\"\"Label a layer and judge whether it is potentially water bearing.\"\"\"\n lo, hi = config.fractured_zone_rho\n if is_top:\n if rho >= config.laterite_min_rho:\n return \"dry lateritic topsoil / duricrust\", False\n if rho >= hi:\n return \"compact laterite / dry overburden\", False\n if rho <= config.clay_max_rho:\n return \"clayey topsoil\", False\n return \"topsoil / laterite\", False\n if rho >= config.fresh_basement_min_rho:\n return \"fresh basement\", False\n if rho >= hi:\n if is_bottom:\n return \"slightly weathered or fractured bedrock (limited water potential)\", False\n return \"compact or dry weathered rock (regolith)\", False\n if rho <= config.clay_max_rho:\n return \"clay rich saprolite (low permeability)\", False\n if is_bottom:\n return \"fractured bedrock, low resistivity indicative of groundwater in fractures\", True\n return \"weathered / fractured zone, potentially water bearing when saturated\", True\n\n\ndef interpret_model(\n sounding: VESSounding | None,\n model: LayeredModel,\n config: VESConfig | None = None,\n) -> SiteInterpretation:\n \"\"\"Interpret one layered model hydrogeologically.\"\"\"\n config = config or VESConfig()\n rho = model.resistivities\n tops = model.depths_top\n bottoms = model.depths_bottom\n n = model.n_layers\n\n if sounding is not None:\n investigation = float(np.max(sounding.ab2))\n elif n > 1:\n investigation = float(bottoms[-2] * 2 + 20)\n else:\n # A bare half-space with no sounding carries no depth scale at all -\n # bottoms is just [inf], and bottoms[-2] used to raise IndexError.\n # Zero is the honest answer: nothing was resolved, so nothing is\n # recommended.\n investigation = 0.0\n\n layers: list[LayerInterpretation] = []\n for i in range(n):\n unit, water = _unit_label(\n float(rho[i]), is_top=(i == 0), is_bottom=(i == n - 1), config=config\n )\n layers.append(\n LayerInterpretation(\n number=i + 1,\n rho=float(rho[i]),\n thickness_m=float(model.thicknesses[i]) if i < n - 1 else None,\n top_m=float(tops[i]),\n bottom_m=float(bottoms[i]),\n unit=unit,\n water_bearing=water,\n )\n )\n\n # ---- water zones ------------------------------------------------------\n zones: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n for layer in layers:\n if not layer.water_bearing:\n continue\n top = max(layer.top_m, 3.0) # the top few metres are vadose\n bottom = layer.bottom_m if math.isfinite(layer.bottom_m) else investigation\n if bottom - top >= 1.0:\n zones.append((round(top), round(bottom)))\n # merge touching zones\n merged: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n for zone in sorted(zones):\n if merged and zone[0] <= merged[-1][1] + 1:\n merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], zone[1]))\n else:\n merged.append(zone)\n zones = merged\n\n # ---- depth to basement -------------------------------------------------\n depth_to_basement = None\n for layer in layers:\n if layer.rho >= config.fresh_basement_min_rho and layer.top_m > 0:\n depth_to_basement = layer.top_m\n break\n if depth_to_basement is None and layers[-1].rho >= config.fractured_zone_rho[1]:\n depth_to_basement = layers[-1].top_m\n\n aquifer_thickness = sum(b - t for t, b in zones)\n\n # ---- recommended maximum drilling depth ---------------------------------\n # deepest target zone plus a margin, but never past the depth the\n # sounding actually investigated (taken as the maximum AB/2)\n if zones:\n deepest = zones[-1][1] + config.max_drilling_margin_m\n else:\n deepest = investigation\n step = config.round_drilling_depth_to_m\n # Round up to the nearest step, then re-apply the investigated-depth cap:\n # rounding after the min() could push the recommendation past the depth the\n # sounding actually resolved, defeating the cap.\n max_depth = math.ceil(min(deepest, investigation) / step) * step\n max_depth = min(max_depth, investigation)\n\n # ---- suitability score for ranking --------------------------------------\n score = 0.0\n for top, bottom in zones:\n thickness = bottom - top\n mid_rho = _zone_rho(layers, top, bottom)\n # favour thick zones with resistivities in the productive window\n lo, hi = config.fractured_zone_rho\n centre = math.sqrt(lo * hi)\n rho_term = 1.0 / (1.0 + abs(math.log(max(mid_rho, 1e-3) / centre)))\n score += thickness * rho_term\n if depth_to_basement is not None and depth_to_basement < 5 and not zones:\n score *= 0.5 # thin regolith and nothing water bearing\n\n curve_type = classify_curve(model)\n interp = SiteInterpretation(\n sounding_id=model.sounding_id or (sounding.sounding_id if sounding else \"\"),\n model=model,\n curve_type=curve_type,\n layers=layers,\n water_zones=zones,\n depth_to_basement_m=depth_to_basement,\n aquifer_thickness_m=aquifer_thickness,\n max_drilling_depth_m=max_depth,\n investigation_depth_m=investigation,\n score=score,\n )\n # ---- Dar-Zarrouk parameters and protective capacity ---------------------\n s_cond, t_res = _dar_zarrouk(layers)\n interp.longitudinal_conductance_s = s_cond\n interp.transverse_resistance_t = t_res\n # protective capacity uses only the cover above the aquifer, so a\n # conductive water-bearing zone is not counted as its own protection\n s_cover = _cover_conductance(layers)\n interp.protective_conductance_s = s_cover\n interp.protective_capacity = _protective_capacity(s_cover)\n\n if sounding is not None and sounding.site is not None:\n interp.site_easting = sounding.site.easting\n interp.site_northing = sounding.site.northing\n interp.site_elevation_m = sounding.site.elevation_m\n interp.narrative = _narrative(interp)\n return interp\n\n\ndef _dar_zarrouk(layers: list[LayerInterpretation]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n \"\"\"Longitudinal conductance S = Sum(h/rho) and transverse resistance\n T = Sum(h*rho) over the finite (non-basement) layers.\"\"\"\n s_cond = 0.0\n t_res = 0.0\n for layer in layers:\n if layer.thickness_m is None or layer.rho <= 0:\n continue\n s_cond += layer.thickness_m / layer.rho\n t_res += layer.thickness_m * layer.rho\n return s_cond, t_res\n\n\ndef _cover_conductance(layers: list[LayerInterpretation]) -> float:\n \"\"\"Longitudinal conductance of the cover overlying the aquifer.\n\n Only the material above the shallowest water-bearing layer counts as\n protective cover, so a thick or conductive aquifer is not credited as\n its own contamination barrier. With no water-bearing layer the whole\n overburden is the cover.\n\n The top is taken from the layers, not from the reported water zones:\n those are floored at 3 m by the vadose rule and rounded for display, so\n a weathered aquifer reaching close to the surface had its own top 3 m -\n conductive, and therefore a large contribution - credited as its\n barrier, rating a poorly protected aquifer as moderately protected.\n \"\"\"\n aquifer_top = min(\n (layer.top_m for layer in layers if layer.water_bearing),\n default=float(\"inf\"),\n )\n s_cover = 0.0\n for layer in layers:\n if layer.thickness_m is None or layer.rho <= 0:\n continue\n cover_thickness = max(0.0, min(layer.bottom_m, aquifer_top) - layer.top_m)\n if cover_thickness > 0:\n s_cover += cover_thickness / layer.rho\n return s_cover\n\n\ndef _protective_capacity(s_cond: float) -> str:\n \"\"\"Aquifer protective-capacity rating from the longitudinal conductance\n (standard crystalline-basement classification, siemens).\"\"\"\n if s_cond < 0.1:\n return \"poor\"\n if s_cond < 0.2:\n return \"weak\"\n if s_cond < 0.7:\n return \"moderate\"\n if s_cond < 5.0:\n return \"good\"\n return \"very good\"\n\n\ndef _zone_rho(layers: list[LayerInterpretation], top: float, bottom: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Thickness weighted geometric mean resistivity across a depth range.\"\"\"\n total = 0.0\n acc = 0.0\n for layer in layers:\n lo = max(layer.top_m, top)\n hi = min(layer.bottom_m if math.isfinite(layer.bottom_m) else bottom, bottom)\n if hi > lo:\n acc += math.log(layer.rho) * (hi - lo)\n total += hi - lo\n return math.exp(acc / total) if total > 0 else 100.0\n\n\ndef _narrative(interp: SiteInterpretation) -> str:\n \"\"\"Interpretation paragraph for the report, one block per sounding.\"\"\"\n n = interp.model.n_layers\n parts = [\n f\"The data at {interp.sounding_id} resolves a {n} layer subsurface \"\n f\"({describe_curve_type(interp.curve_type)}).\"\n ]\n for layer in interp.layers:\n if layer.thickness_m is not None:\n span = (\n f\"from {fmt_num(layer.top_m)} m to {fmt_num(layer.bottom_m)} m \"\n f\"({fmt_num(layer.thickness_m)} m thick)\"\n )\n else:\n span = f\"below {fmt_num(layer.top_m)} m\"\n parts.append(\n f\"Layer {layer.number} {span} has a resistivity of about \"\n f\"{fmt_num(layer.rho, 4)} ohm-m and is interpreted as {layer.unit}.\"\n )\n if interp.water_zones:\n zones_text = \", \".join(f\"{int(t)} m to {int(b)} m\" for t, b in interp.water_zones)\n parts.append(\n \"The unusually low resistivity within the interpreted fractured or \"\n \"weathered intervals is indicative of pore electrolyte, possibly \"\n f\"groundwater. The possible water zones are {zones_text}.\"\n )\n else:\n parts.append(\n \"No clearly water bearing low resistivity zone is resolved at this \"\n \"point within the investigated depth.\"\n )\n if interp.depth_to_basement_m is not None:\n parts.append(\n f\"The depth to bedrock is estimated at about \"\n f\"{fmt_num(interp.depth_to_basement_m)} m.\"\n )\n if interp.longitudinal_conductance_s > 0:\n base = (\n \"The Dar-Zarrouk longitudinal conductance of the section is \"\n f\"{fmt_num(interp.longitudinal_conductance_s, 3)} siemens and the \"\n \"transverse resistance is \"\n f\"{fmt_num(interp.transverse_resistance_t)} ohm m2.\"\n )\n if interp.water_zones:\n base += (\n \" The cover overlying the water bearing zone has a longitudinal \"\n f\"conductance of {fmt_num(interp.protective_conductance_s, 3)} \"\n f\"siemens, indicating a {interp.protective_capacity} protective \"\n \"capacity against surface contamination.\"\n )\n else:\n base += (\n f\" This gives a {interp.protective_capacity} protective capacity \"\n \"against surface contamination.\"\n )\n parts.append(base)\n return \" \".join(parts)\n\n\n\ndef rank_interpretations(\n interpretations: list[SiteInterpretation],\n preferred_order: list[str] | None = None,\n) -> list[SiteInterpretation]:\n \"\"\"Assign ``rank`` (1 = most preferred) in place; return them ranked.\n\n Kept separate from the preference table so callers that only need the\n ranking - the dashboard, a reloaded project - get it without building the\n table. Every caller reading ``rank`` must have ranked first: an unranked\n set leaves every rank None, and \"best\" then falls back to whichever\n sounding happened to be parsed first.\n \"\"\"\n if preferred_order:\n position = {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(preferred_order)}\n ranked = sorted(\n interpretations,\n key=lambda i: (position.get(i.sounding_id, len(position)), -i.score),\n )\n else:\n ranked = sorted(interpretations, key=lambda i: (-i.score, i.sounding_id))\n for rank, interp in enumerate(ranked, start=1):\n interp.rank = rank\n return ranked\n\n\ndef drilling_preference_table(\n interpretations: list[SiteInterpretation],\n preferred_order: list[str] | None = None,\n) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Ranked drilling preference table (one row per VES point).\n\n Matches the survey report layout: layers with thickness, depth and\n resistivity, possible water zones, maximum drilling depth and the\n ranking. Ranks are assigned from the suitability score (1st = most\n preferred). When sites score close together the choice is a\n professional judgment call, so ``preferred_order`` (a list of\n sounding ids, most preferred first) lets the analyst set the\n ranking explicitly; unlisted sites follow after, by score.\n \"\"\"\n rank_interpretations(interpretations, preferred_order)\n rows = []\n for i, interp in enumerate(interpretations, start=1):\n layer_numbers = \"\\n\".join(str(l.number) for l in interp.layers)\n thicknesses = \"\\n\".join(\n fmt_num(l.thickness_m) if l.thickness_m is not None else \"\"\n for l in interp.layers\n )\n depths = \"\\n\".join(\n fmt_num(l.bottom_m) if math.isfinite(l.bottom_m) else \"\"\n for l in interp.layers\n )\n rhos = \"\\n\".join(fmt_num(l.rho, 4) for l in interp.layers)\n zones = \"\\n\".join(f\"{int(t)}-{int(b)}\" for t, b in interp.water_zones) or \"none resolved\"\n rows.append(\n {\n \"No.\": i,\n \"VES Point\": interp.sounding_id,\n \"Layer\": layer_numbers,\n \"Thickness (m)\": thicknesses,\n \"Depth (m)\": depths,\n \"Apparent Resistivity (Ohm-m)\": rhos,\n \"Possible Water Zones (m)\": zones,\n \"Max Drilling Depth (m)\": f\"{interp.max_drilling_depth_m:.0f} m\",\n \"Ranking\": ordinal(interp.rank),\n }\n )\n return rows\n"}, "groundwater/ves/inversion.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Damped least squares (Levenberg-Marquardt) 1D inversion of VES data.\n\nParameters are the logarithms of layer resistivities and thicknesses,\nthe misfit is measured on the logarithm of apparent resistivity, and a\nMarquardt damping term stabilises the ill posed steps, which is the\nclassical ridge regression approach used by IPI2Win and similar tools.\nThe reported fit error matches the IPI2Win ERR quantity::\n\n ERR % = sqrt( mean( ((rho_calc - rho_obs) / rho_obs)^2 ) ) * 100\n\n``invert_sounding`` searches over the number of layers (2 to\n``max_layers``) from several deterministic starting models and returns\nthe simplest model that reaches the target fit, with all trial results\nattached for review.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import VESConfig\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel, VESSounding\nfrom .forward import forward_schlumberger, forward_wenner\nfrom .splice import splice_segments\n\n__all__ = [\"InversionResult\", \"invert_model\", \"invert_sounding\"]\n\n_RHO_BOUNDS = (0.5, 200000.0)\n_H_BOUNDS = (0.2, 300.0)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass InversionResult:\n model: LayeredModel\n ab2: np.ndarray\n rho_obs: np.ndarray\n rho_calc: np.ndarray\n fit_error_percent: float\n n_iterations: int\n converged: bool\n trials: list = field(default_factory=list) # (n_layers, err) for auto search\n shifts: list = field(default_factory=list) # splice diagnostics\n # linearised 1-sigma multiplicative uncertainty per parameter, so a\n # resistivity rho is constrained to rho x/ factor. Larger factors mark\n # the equivalence/suppression that makes resistivity models non-unique.\n rho_uncertainty_factor: np.ndarray | None = None\n h_uncertainty_factor: np.ndarray | None = None\n\n\ndef _forward(rho, h, ab2, array_type: str):\n if array_type.startswith(\"wenner\"):\n return forward_wenner((rho, h), ab2)\n return forward_schlumberger((rho, h), ab2)\n\n\ndef fit_error_percent(rho_obs: np.ndarray, rho_calc: np.ndarray) -> float:\n rel = (rho_calc - rho_obs) / rho_obs\n return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(rel**2)) * 100.0)\n\n\ndef _pack(rho, h):\n return np.concatenate([np.log(rho), np.log(h)]) if len(h) else np.log(rho)\n\n\ndef _unpack(theta, n_layers):\n rho = np.exp(theta[:n_layers])\n h = np.exp(theta[n_layers:])\n return rho, h\n\n\ndef _clip(theta, n_layers):\n lo = np.concatenate(\n [np.full(n_layers, np.log(_RHO_BOUNDS[0])), np.full(len(theta) - n_layers, np.log(_H_BOUNDS[0]))]\n )\n hi = np.concatenate(\n [np.full(n_layers, np.log(_RHO_BOUNDS[1])), np.full(len(theta) - n_layers, np.log(_H_BOUNDS[1]))]\n )\n return np.clip(theta, lo, hi)\n\n\ndef invert_model(\n ab2: np.ndarray,\n rho_app: np.ndarray,\n rho0: np.ndarray,\n h0: np.ndarray,\n array_type: str = \"schlumberger\",\n damping: float = 0.02,\n max_iterations: int = 60,\n) -> tuple[LayeredModel, np.ndarray, float, int, bool]:\n \"\"\"Levenberg-Marquardt refinement from one starting model.\"\"\"\n n_layers = len(rho0)\n theta = _clip(_pack(np.asarray(rho0, float), np.asarray(h0, float)), n_layers)\n log_obs = np.log(rho_app)\n\n def residuals(t):\n rho, h = _unpack(t, n_layers)\n calc = _forward(rho, h, ab2, array_type)\n calc = np.maximum(calc, 1e-9)\n return np.log(calc) - log_obs, calc\n\n res, calc = residuals(theta)\n cost = float(res @ res)\n lam = damping\n iterations = 0\n converged = False\n for iterations in range(1, max_iterations + 1):\n # numerical Jacobian in log space\n J = np.empty((len(ab2), len(theta)))\n step = 1e-4\n for j in range(len(theta)):\n tp = theta.copy()\n tp[j] += step\n rp, _ = residuals(tp)\n J[:, j] = (rp - res) / step\n\n JtJ = J.T @ J\n g = J.T @ res\n improved = False\n for _ in range(12):\n try:\n delta = np.linalg.solve(\n JtJ + lam * np.diag(np.maximum(np.diag(JtJ), 1e-8)), -g\n )\n except np.linalg.LinAlgError:\n lam *= 10\n continue\n trial = _clip(theta + delta, n_layers)\n r_trial, c_trial = residuals(trial)\n cost_trial = float(r_trial @ r_trial)\n if cost_trial < cost:\n theta, res, calc, cost = trial, r_trial, c_trial, cost_trial\n lam = max(lam / 3.0, 1e-7)\n improved = True\n break\n lam *= 10\n if lam > 1e8:\n break\n if not improved:\n converged = True\n break\n if cost < 1e-10:\n converged = True\n break\n\n rho, h = _unpack(theta, n_layers)\n err = fit_error_percent(rho_app, calc)\n model = LayeredModel(rho, h, fit_error_percent=err, method=\"damped-lsq\")\n return model, calc, err, iterations, converged\n\n\ndef _starting_models(ab2: np.ndarray, rho: np.ndarray, n_layers: int) -> list:\n \"\"\"Deterministic starting models from the smoothed field curve.\n\n Thicknesses grow logarithmically over the depth range covered by\n the spacings (depth of investigation taken as AB/2 / 2); starting\n resistivities are read off the smoothed curve at the corresponding\n spacings. Two depth-scale variants bracket the depth of investigation.\n \"\"\"\n log_rho = np.log(rho)\n starts = []\n for depth_factor in (0.35, 0.7):\n z_top = max(ab2[0] * depth_factor, 0.5)\n z_bot = max(ab2[-1] * depth_factor, z_top * 4)\n # An n-layer model has n-1 interfaces, and they must span the whole\n # investigated range. Spacing n points and then dropping the last\n # put the deepest starting interface at the second geomspace point:\n # 6 m for a sounding that reaches 56 m, so the search began with\n # basement far too shallow and had to climb out of it.\n interfaces = np.geomspace(z_top, z_bot, max(n_layers - 1, 1))\n h0 = np.maximum(np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.0], interfaces])), 0.3)\n # one starting resistivity per layer, read off the smoothed curve at\n # the spacing that senses each layer's mid-depth\n tops = np.concatenate([[0.0], interfaces])\n mids = np.concatenate([\n 0.5 * (tops[:-1] + tops[1:]), # the finite layers\n [interfaces[-1] * 1.5], # the half space below\n ])\n rho0 = []\n for z in mids[:n_layers]:\n L = np.clip(2.0 * z, ab2[0], ab2[-1])\n rho0.append(np.exp(np.interp(np.log(L), np.log(ab2), log_rho)))\n starts.append((np.array(rho0), h0))\n return starts\n\n\ndef invert_sounding(\n sounding: VESSounding,\n config: VESConfig | None = None,\n n_layers: int | None = None,\n initial_model: LayeredModel | None = None,\n splice: bool = True,\n) -> InversionResult:\n \"\"\"Invert a sounding to a layered model.\n\n With ``n_layers=None`` the layer count is searched from\n ``config.min_layers`` to ``config.max_layers`` and the simplest\n model whose fit reaches ``config.target_fit_percent`` is kept (or\n the best fitting model if none reaches it). Passing\n ``initial_model`` (for example an imported IPI2Win model) refines\n that model instead.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or VESConfig()\n if splice and not sounding.array_type.startswith(\"wenner\"):\n ab2, rho_app, shifts = splice_segments(sounding)\n else:\n order = np.argsort(sounding.ab2, kind=\"stable\")\n ab2, rho_app, shifts = sounding.ab2[order], sounding.rho_app[order], [1.0]\n\n keep = np.isfinite(rho_app) & (rho_app > 0)\n ab2, rho_app = ab2[keep], rho_app[keep]\n if len(ab2) < 4:\n raise ValueError(\"Not enough readings to invert\")\n\n candidates: list[tuple[LayeredModel, np.ndarray, float, int, bool]] = []\n trials: list[tuple[int, float]] = []\n\n if initial_model is not None:\n result = invert_model(\n ab2,\n rho_app,\n initial_model.resistivities,\n initial_model.thicknesses,\n sounding.array_type,\n config.damping,\n config.max_iterations,\n )\n candidates.append(result)\n trials.append((result[0].n_layers, result[2]))\n else:\n layer_range = (\n [n_layers]\n if n_layers is not None\n else list(range(config.min_layers, config.max_layers + 1))\n )\n for n in layer_range:\n best_for_n = None\n for rho0, h0 in _starting_models(ab2, rho_app, n):\n result = invert_model(\n ab2, rho_app, rho0, h0,\n sounding.array_type, config.damping, config.max_iterations,\n )\n if best_for_n is None or result[2] < best_for_n[2]:\n best_for_n = result\n candidates.append(best_for_n)\n trials.append((n, best_for_n[2]))\n if n_layers is None:\n # stop adding layers once the target is comfortably reached\n # or when the extra layer no longer helps materially - but the\n # diminishing-returns test only applies once an adequate fit is\n # already in hand, so a small n-1 -> n gain (equivalence /\n # suppression) cannot abandon the search while the fit is still\n # far above target.\n if best_for_n[2] <= config.target_fit_percent / 2:\n break\n if (\n len(trials) >= 2\n and trials[-1][1] > 0.9 * trials[-2][1]\n and best_for_n[2] <= config.target_fit_percent\n ):\n break\n\n # Parsimony: the simplest model reaching the target; otherwise the\n # simplest model whose fit is within 15 percent of the best fit\n # (extra layers must earn their keep), otherwise the overall best.\n #\n # \"Reaching the target\" is not enough on its own. A two-layer model can\n # sit just under the target while a three-layer one fits the same curve\n # an order of magnitude better and puts basement at 65 m instead of 4 m -\n # the difference between drilling into the aquifer and stopping in the\n # regolith. So a simple model is only accepted while no available model\n # more than halves its misfit.\n best_err = min(c[2] for c in candidates)\n chosen = None\n for cand in candidates:\n if cand[2] <= config.target_fit_percent and (\n cand[2] <= config.parsimony_max_error_ratio * max(best_err, 1e-9)\n or cand[2] <= config.target_fit_percent / 10.0\n ):\n chosen = cand\n break\n if chosen is None:\n for cand in candidates:\n if cand[2] <= 1.15 * best_err:\n chosen = cand\n break\n if chosen is None:\n chosen = min(candidates, key=lambda c: c[2])\n\n model, calc, err, iterations, converged = chosen\n model.sounding_id = sounding.sounding_id\n rho_factor, h_factor = _parameter_uncertainty(\n ab2, rho_app, model, sounding.array_type\n )\n return InversionResult(\n model=model,\n ab2=ab2,\n rho_obs=rho_app,\n rho_calc=calc,\n fit_error_percent=err,\n n_iterations=iterations,\n converged=converged,\n trials=trials,\n shifts=shifts,\n rho_uncertainty_factor=rho_factor,\n h_uncertainty_factor=h_factor,\n )\n\n\ndef _parameter_uncertainty(ab2, rho_app, model, array_type):\n \"\"\"Linearised 1-sigma multiplicative uncertainty per model parameter.\n\n Reuses the log-space Jacobian the inversion is built on: the model\n covariance is sigma^2 (J'J)^-1 with sigma^2 the variance of the log\n residuals, and because the parameters are logarithms, exp(sigma_i)\n gives the multiplicative factor on each resistivity and thickness.\n Returns ``(rho_factor, h_factor)``; factors near 1 are well resolved,\n large factors mark equivalence.\n \"\"\"\n rho = np.asarray(model.resistivities, float)\n h = np.asarray(model.thicknesses, float)\n n_layers = len(rho)\n theta = _pack(rho, h)\n log_obs = np.log(rho_app)\n\n def residuals(t):\n r, hh = _unpack(t, n_layers)\n calc = np.maximum(_forward(r, hh, ab2, array_type), 1e-9)\n return np.log(calc) - log_obs\n\n res = residuals(theta)\n m, p = len(ab2), len(theta)\n J = np.empty((m, p))\n step = 1e-4\n for j in range(p):\n tp = theta.copy()\n tp[j] += step\n J[:, j] = (residuals(tp) - res) / step\n\n dof = max(m - p, 1)\n sigma2 = float(res @ res) / dof\n JtJ = J.T @ J\n try:\n cov = sigma2 * np.linalg.inv(JtJ)\n except np.linalg.LinAlgError:\n cov = sigma2 * np.linalg.pinv(JtJ)\n std = np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(cov), 0.0, None))\n # cap the reported factor so a wildly unconstrained parameter does not\n # print an absurd number; anything above ~10x is \"not resolved\"\n factors = np.minimum(np.exp(std), 10.0)\n return factors[:n_layers], factors[n_layers:]\n"}, "groundwater/ves/ipi2win.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Import layered models from IPI2Win output tables.\n\nIPI2Win reports models as a table with columns N, rho, h and z, where\nz is the depth to the top of the layer, the first z prints as ``0/0``\nand the half space row has no thickness. The overall fit is reported\nas ``ERR = ``. Interpretations already made in IPI2Win can be\ntranscribed into a small Excel/CSV table and reused directly.\n\nExpected layout (one worksheet per sounding, or one CSV per sounding):\n\n Sounding Number: 1 (optional header row(s))\n ERR (%): 21.5 (optional)\n N | rho | h | z\n 1 | 832.14 | 1 | 0/0\n 2 | 2102.8 | 7.37 | 1\n 3 | 36.71 | | 8.37\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\n\n# \"ERR\" / \"Error\" as a whole word, so it does not fire on unrelated words that\n# merely contain the letters e-r-r (Terrain, Errol, ...).\n_ERR_RE = re.compile(r\"\\berr(?:or)?\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\n__all__ = [\"read_ipi2win_models\", \"model_from_rows\"]\n\n\ndef _find_table(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = [clean_text(c).lower().rstrip(\".\") for c in row]\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n base = t.replace(\"(m)\", \"\").replace(\"(ohm-m)\", \"\").strip()\n if base in (\"n\", \"no\", \"layer\"):\n cols[\"n\"] = c\n elif base in (\"rho\", \"p\", \"resistivity\") or \"rho\" in base or \"resist\" in base:\n cols.setdefault(\"rho\", c)\n elif base in (\"h\", \"thickness\") or base.startswith(\"h \"):\n cols.setdefault(\"h\", c)\n elif base in (\"z\", \"depth\") or base.startswith(\"z \"):\n cols.setdefault(\"z\", c)\n if \"rho\" in cols and (\"h\" in cols or \"z\" in cols):\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\ndef _find_err(grid: list[list]) -> float | None:\n for row in grid:\n for cell in row:\n text = clean_text(cell)\n if not text or not _ERR_RE.search(text):\n continue\n # Prefer the value after a '=' or ':' delimiter (\"ERR = 3.5%\"); a\n # label cell that merely mentions error but has no number is\n # skipped rather than yielding a bogus fit error.\n tail = re.split(r\"[=:]\", text)[-1] if re.search(r\"[=:]\", text) else text\n value = parse_number(tail)\n if value is not None:\n return value\n return None\n\n\ndef model_from_rows(\n rows: list[dict], err: float | None = None, sounding_id: str = \"\"\n) -> LayeredModel:\n \"\"\"Build a LayeredModel from row dicts with rho / h / z entries.\"\"\"\n rho = [r[\"rho\"] for r in rows]\n h = [r.get(\"h\") for r in rows]\n z = [r.get(\"z\") for r in rows]\n thicknesses: list[float] = []\n for i in range(len(rho) - 1):\n if h[i] is not None:\n thicknesses.append(float(h[i]))\n elif z[i + 1] is not None and z[i] is not None:\n thicknesses.append(float(z[i + 1]) - float(z[i]))\n elif z[i + 1] is not None and i == 0:\n thicknesses.append(float(z[i + 1]))\n else:\n raise ValueError(\"Cannot determine layer thicknesses from the table\")\n return LayeredModel(\n np.asarray(rho, float),\n np.asarray(thicknesses, float),\n fit_error_percent=err,\n method=\"ipi2win-import\",\n sounding_id=sounding_id,\n )\n\n\ndef _model_from_grid(grid: list[list], sounding_id: str) -> LayeredModel | None:\n located = _find_table(grid)\n if located is None:\n return None\n header_row, cols = located\n rows = []\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n def cell(key):\n c = cols.get(key)\n return row[c] if c is not None and c < len(row) else None\n\n rho = parse_number(cell(\"rho\"))\n if rho is None:\n if rows:\n break\n continue\n z_raw = clean_text(cell(\"z\"))\n z = 0.0 if z_raw.startswith(\"0/0\") else parse_number(cell(\"z\"))\n rows.append({\"rho\": rho, \"h\": parse_number(cell(\"h\")), \"z\": z})\n if not rows:\n return None\n err = _find_err(grid)\n return model_from_rows(rows, err=err, sounding_id=sounding_id)\n\n\ndef read_ipi2win_models(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, LayeredModel]:\n \"\"\"Read IPI2Win model tables from an Excel workbook or CSV file.\n\n Returns a mapping of sounding id (worksheet title or a \"Sounding\n Number\" header value, else the file stem) to the layered model.\n \"\"\"\n from ..ingestion import common\n\n path = Path(path)\n models: dict[str, LayeredModel] = {}\n if path.suffix.lower() == \".csv\":\n with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8-sig\") as fh:\n grid = [[c if c != \"\" else None for c in row] for row in csv.reader(fh)]\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid)\n sounding_id = str(fields.get(\"sounding_id\", \"\") or path.stem)\n model = _model_from_grid(grid, sounding_id)\n if model is not None:\n models[sounding_id] = model\n return models\n\n for name in common.sheet_names(path):\n grid, title = common.load_grid(path, sheet=name)\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid)\n sounding_id = str(fields.get(\"sounding_id\", \"\") or title)\n model = _model_from_grid(grid, sounding_id)\n if model is not None:\n models[sounding_id] = model\n return models\n"}, "groundwater/ves/plots.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"VES figures: sounding curves with models, layer pseudo-sections and\nmulti-sounding geoelectric cross-sections.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nfrom matplotlib import colors as mcolors\nfrom matplotlib import cm\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel, VESSounding\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom ..utils import fmt_num\nfrom .forward import forward_schlumberger, forward_wenner\nfrom .splice import splice_segments\n\n__all__ = [\n \"plot_sounding_curve\",\n \"plot_model_pseudosection\",\n \"plot_geoelectric_section\",\n]\n\n_RHO_NORM = mcolors.LogNorm(vmin=10, vmax=5000)\n\n\ndef _model_step(model: LayeredModel, depth_max: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n \"\"\"Stepwise rho(z) profile for plotting.\"\"\"\n tops = model.depths_top\n rho = model.resistivities\n z = [0.0]\n r = [rho[0]]\n for i in range(1, len(rho)):\n z.extend([tops[i], tops[i]])\n r.extend([rho[i - 1], rho[i]])\n z.append(depth_max)\n r.append(rho[-1])\n return np.array(z), np.array(r)\n\n\ndef plot_sounding_curve(\n sounding: VESSounding,\n model: LayeredModel | None = None,\n rho_calc: np.ndarray | None = None,\n ab2_calc: np.ndarray | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n show_splice: bool = True,\n):\n \"\"\"Log-log sounding curve with optional fitted model panel.\n\n Left: apparent resistivity against AB/2 with the field segments,\n the spliced curve and the model response. Right: the layered model\n as a resistivity-depth step plot, annotated with the fit error.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n with figure_context(style):\n if model is not None:\n fig, (ax, axm) = plt.subplots(\n 1, 2, figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 3.4), width_ratios=[1.6, 1]\n )\n else:\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.75, 3.4))\n axm = None\n\n # field segments\n markers = [\"o\", \"s\", \"^\", \"D\", \"v\", \"P\"]\n for k, idx in enumerate(sounding.segments()):\n mn = sounding.mn[idx][0] if len(idx) else float(\"nan\")\n label = f\"MN = {fmt_num(mn)} m\" if np.isfinite(mn) else \"field data\"\n ax.loglog(\n sounding.ab2[idx],\n sounding.rho_app[idx],\n markers[k % len(markers)],\n ms=4.5,\n mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color,\n mew=1.2,\n ls=\"none\",\n label=label,\n )\n if show_splice and len(sounding.segments()) > 1:\n ab2_s, rho_s, _ = splice_segments(sounding)\n ax.loglog(\n ab2_s, rho_s, \"-\", color=style.accent_color, lw=1.0, alpha=0.8,\n label=\"spliced curve\",\n )\n if model is not None:\n if rho_calc is None or ab2_calc is None:\n ab2_calc = np.geomspace(sounding.ab2.min(), sounding.ab2.max(), 60)\n # the array decides the kernel: drawing a Schlumberger\n # response over Wenner readings shows a model that misses\n # its own data by tens of percent\n rho_calc = (\n forward_wenner(model, ab2_calc)\n if sounding.array_type.startswith(\"wenner\")\n else forward_schlumberger(model, ab2_calc)\n )\n ax.loglog(\n ab2_calc, rho_calc, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=\"model response\",\n )\n ax.set_xlabel(\"AB/2 (m)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Apparent resistivity (ohm-m)\")\n ax.set_title(f\"{sounding.label} sounding curve\")\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n ax.grid(True, which=\"both\")\n\n if axm is not None and model is not None:\n depth_max = max(float(np.max(sounding.ab2)), model.depths_top[-1] * 1.5 + 5)\n z, r = _model_step(model, depth_max)\n axm.plot(r, z, color=style.secondary_color, lw=2.0)\n axm.set_xscale(\"log\")\n axm.set_ylim(depth_max, 0)\n axm.set_xlabel(\"Layer resistivity (ohm-m)\")\n axm.set_ylabel(\"Depth (m)\")\n err = model.fit_error_percent\n title = \"Layered model\"\n if err is not None:\n title += f\" (ERR = {err:.1f}%)\"\n axm.set_title(title)\n tops = model.depths_top\n for i, row in enumerate(model.as_table()):\n top = tops[i]\n bottom = tops[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(tops) else depth_max\n z_label = 0.5 * (top + min(bottom, depth_max))\n axm.annotate(\n f\"{fmt_num(row['rho_ohm_m'], 4)}\",\n xy=(row[\"rho_ohm_m\"], z_label),\n xytext=(3, 0), textcoords=\"offset points\",\n fontsize=7.5, va=\"center\", color=\"#333333\",\n )\n axm.grid(True, which=\"both\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_model_pseudosection(\n model: LayeredModel,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n depth_max: float | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Single sounding layer column coloured by resistivity.\n\n The 'pseudo-section showing apparent resistivity and layer\n thicknesses' figure of the survey reports: horizontal bands to\n scale with a logarithmic resistivity colour bar.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.72, 3.6))\n tops = model.depths_top\n if depth_max is None:\n depth_max = (tops[-1] if len(tops) > 1 else 10) * 1.35 + 3\n cmap = plt.get_cmap(\"viridis\")\n for i, rho in enumerate(model.resistivities):\n top = tops[i]\n bottom = tops[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(tops) else depth_max\n ax.axhspan(top, bottom, color=cmap(_RHO_NORM(max(rho, _RHO_NORM.vmin))))\n z_text = (top + min(bottom, depth_max)) / 2\n ax.text(\n 0.5, z_text, f\"{fmt_num(rho, 4)} ohm-m\",\n ha=\"center\", va=\"center\", fontsize=9,\n color=\"white\", transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(),\n path_effects=None,\n bbox=dict(boxstyle=\"round,pad=0.25\", fc=\"#00000055\", ec=\"none\"),\n )\n for z in tops[1:]:\n ax.axhline(z, color=\"white\", lw=1.0)\n ax.set_ylim(depth_max, 0)\n ax.set_xlim(0, 1)\n ax.set_xticks([])\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Depth (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title or f\"{model.sounding_id or 'VES'} layer section\")\n sm = cm.ScalarMappable(norm=_RHO_NORM, cmap=cmap)\n cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, pad=0.04)\n cbar.set_label(\"Resistivity (ohm-m)\")\n ax.grid(False)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_geoelectric_section(\n models: list[LayeredModel],\n positions: list[float] | None = None,\n labels: list[str] | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n depth_max: float | None = None,\n title: str = \"Interpreted geoelectric cross-section\",\n):\n \"\"\"Cross-section through several soundings along a profile.\n\n Each sounding is drawn as a column at its chainage; layer\n boundaries are connected between adjacent soundings.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n if positions is None:\n positions = list(np.arange(len(models), dtype=float) * 100.0)\n if labels is None:\n labels = [m.sounding_id or f\"VES {i + 1}\" for i, m in enumerate(models)]\n if depth_max is None:\n depth_max = max(\n (m.depths_top[-1] if m.n_layers > 1 else 10) * 1.35 + 5 for m in models\n )\n span = max(positions) - min(positions) or 100.0\n half_w = span / (len(models) * 2.6)\n cmap = plt.get_cmap(\"viridis\")\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 3.6))\n for x, model in zip(positions, models):\n tops = model.depths_top\n for i, rho in enumerate(model.resistivities):\n top = tops[i]\n bottom = tops[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(tops) else depth_max\n ax.fill_between(\n [x - half_w, x + half_w], top, bottom,\n color=cmap(_RHO_NORM(max(rho, _RHO_NORM.vmin))), lw=0,\n )\n for z in tops[1:]:\n ax.plot([x - half_w, x + half_w], [z, z], color=\"white\", lw=1.0)\n # connect boundaries between neighbouring soundings\n for a in range(len(models) - 1):\n m1, m2 = models[a], models[a + 1]\n n_shared = min(m1.n_layers, m2.n_layers) - 1\n for k in range(1, n_shared + 1):\n z1 = m1.depths_top[k] if k < m1.n_layers else None\n z2 = m2.depths_top[k] if k < m2.n_layers else None\n if z1 is None or z2 is None:\n continue\n ax.plot(\n [positions[a] + half_w, positions[a + 1] - half_w],\n [z1, z2],\n color=\"#777777\", lw=1.0, ls=\"--\",\n )\n for x, label in zip(positions, labels):\n ax.text(\n x, depth_max * 0.035, label, ha=\"center\", va=\"top\", fontsize=9,\n fontweight=\"bold\", color=style.accent_color,\n bbox=dict(boxstyle=\"round,pad=0.25\", fc=\"white\", ec=\"none\", alpha=0.85),\n )\n ax.set_ylim(depth_max, 0)\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Distance along profile (m)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Depth (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title)\n sm = cm.ScalarMappable(norm=_RHO_NORM, cmap=cmap)\n cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, pad=0.03)\n cbar.set_label(\"Resistivity (ohm-m)\")\n ax.grid(False)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/ves/splice.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Schlumberger segment handling and optional curve splicing.\n\nAt MN segment changes the same AB/2 is read with the old and new MN,\nand the two readings differ slightly (electrode geometry and lateral\nheterogeneity). Both readings are kept in the raw data. For plotting\nand for inversion with the ideal gradient forward model the segments\ncan be spliced into one smooth curve: each segment after the first is\nscaled by the ratio of overlapping readings (multiplicative shift,\nstandard practice), then overlapping points are merged by geometric\nmean.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import VESSounding\n\n__all__ = [\"splice_segments\"]\n\n\ndef splice_segments(\n sounding: VESSounding, mode: str = \"merge\"\n) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list[float]]:\n \"\"\"Combine a segmented Schlumberger sounding into a single curve.\n\n Parameters\n ----------\n sounding:\n The sounding with possible duplicate AB/2 readings at segment\n changes.\n mode:\n \"merge\" (default) keeps every segment at its measured level and\n merges duplicate AB/2 readings by geometric mean. This honours\n the absolute values of the deep branch that drive the aquifer\n interpretation and matches how IPI2Win treats the data.\n \"first\" applies multiplicative shifts so overlaps coincide,\n anchored to the first (smallest MN) segment; \"last\" anchors to\n the deepest segment. Shifted modes give a visually smooth\n curve but redistribute any overlap jump onto the other\n segments, so they are offered for plotting rather than as the\n inversion default.\n\n Returns\n -------\n ab2, rho:\n Strictly increasing AB/2 and the combined apparent resistivity.\n shifts:\n The multiplicative shift applied to each segment (all 1.0 for\n \"merge\"; values far from 1 in the shifted modes indicate noisy\n overlaps).\n \"\"\"\n segments = sounding.segments()\n if len(segments) <= 1:\n order = np.argsort(sounding.ab2, kind=\"stable\")\n return sounding.ab2[order], sounding.rho_app[order], [1.0]\n\n if mode == \"merge\":\n shifts = [1.0] * len(segments)\n else:\n shifts = [1.0]\n # cumulative shift so each segment matches the (already shifted) previous\n for i in range(1, len(segments)):\n prev_idx = segments[i - 1]\n cur_idx = segments[i]\n prev_ab2 = sounding.ab2[prev_idx]\n cur_ab2 = sounding.ab2[cur_idx]\n common = np.intersect1d(prev_ab2, cur_ab2)\n if len(common) == 0:\n shifts.append(shifts[-1])\n continue\n ratios = []\n for value in common:\n r_prev = sounding.rho_app[prev_idx][prev_ab2 == value]\n r_cur = sounding.rho_app[cur_idx][cur_ab2 == value]\n ratios.append(np.mean(r_prev) / np.mean(r_cur))\n # geometric mean of overlap ratios\n shifts.append(shifts[i - 1] * float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(ratios)))))\n if mode == \"last\":\n shifts = [s / shifts[-1] for s in shifts]\n\n ab2_all, rho_all = [], []\n for shift, idx in zip(shifts, segments):\n ab2_all.extend(sounding.ab2[idx])\n rho_all.extend(sounding.rho_app[idx] * shift)\n ab2_all = np.asarray(ab2_all)\n rho_all = np.asarray(rho_all)\n\n # merge duplicates by geometric mean\n unique = np.unique(ab2_all)\n rho_merged = np.array(\n [np.exp(np.mean(np.log(rho_all[ab2_all == u]))) for u in unique]\n )\n return unique, rho_merged, shifts\n"}, "groundwater/waterpoints.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Existing water points near a site: the rehabilitate-or-drill decision.\n\nBefore a programme spends money drilling a new borehole it is worth\nasking what is already on the ground. A broken but *improved* handpump\n200 m away is usually far cheaper to rehabilitate than a fresh borehole,\nand a working improved source inside the service radius may mean the\ncommunity is already served. This module answers, for a proposed site,\n\"what water points already exist nearby, are they working, and does that\nchange the drill-new decision?\" using the Water Point Data Exchange\n(WPDx+), the global open dataset of rural water points.\n\nDesign\n------\nThe network call is deliberately thin and *optional*. ``fetch_water_points``\nis the only function that touches the internet; it fails soft with a typed\n``WaterPointFetchError`` and takes an injectable opener so it is testable\noffline. Every unit of analysis below it is a pure function over\nalready-fetched records, so the rehab-or-drill logic is fully unit-tested\nwithout connectivity and the app degrades gracefully where there is none\n(the common field situation in rural Sierra Leone).\n\nData source\n-----------\nWater Point Data Exchange - Plus (WPdx+), https://www.waterpointdata.org,\npublished under CC BY 4.0. Field names follow the WPDx data standard; the\nparser accepts the documented ``lat_deg`` / ``status_clean`` style keys and\ntolerant fallbacks so a schema tweak does not silently drop every point.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport re\nimport urllib.error\nimport urllib.parse\nimport urllib.request\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, replace\nfrom typing import Callable, Iterable\n\nWPDX_CREDIT = (\n \"Water points: Water Point Data Exchange (WPdx+), CC BY 4.0, \"\n \"https://www.waterpointdata.org\"\n)\n\n# WPdx+ is served from a Socrata endpoint; the resource id is documented but\n# kept overridable so a future dataset id needs no code change.\nWPDX_DOMAIN = \"data.waterpointdata.org\"\nWPDX_RESOURCE = \"eqje-vguj\"\n\n# how far around a site to look, and the radius inside which an existing\n# working source is treated as already serving the site. 500 m is a common\n# rural handpump service distance (RWSN / Sphere order of magnitude).\nDEFAULT_SEARCH_RADIUS_M = 1000.0\nSERVICE_RADIUS_M = 500.0\n\n_EARTH_RADIUS_M = 6371000.0\n\n# recommendation codes returned by ``rehab_vs_drill``\nDRILL_NEW = \"drill_new\"\nASSESS_REHAB = \"assess_rehab\"\nVERIFY_NEED = \"verify_need\"\n\n\nclass WaterPointFetchError(RuntimeError):\n \"\"\"Raised when water points cannot be fetched (offline, timeout, HTTP).\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterPoint:\n \"\"\"One water point from WPDx, reduced to the fields siting cares about.\"\"\"\n\n row_id: str\n lat: float\n lon: float\n functional: bool | None # True, False, or None when unknown/unreported\n status: str # raw status text, e.g. \"Functional, needs repair\"\n source: str # water source, e.g. \"Borehole\"\n technology: str # water technology, e.g. \"Hand Pump - India Mark II\"\n install_year: int | None\n adm2: str # district / second admin level, as recorded upstream\n distance_m: float | None = None # filled in by ``points_within``\n #: Year the point was last surveyed. A point reported functional in 2016\n #: is evidence about 2016; whether it still works is a separate question,\n #: which is why this is carried rather than folded into ``functional``.\n report_year: int | None = None\n #: Months of the year the point yields water, where the survey asked.\n #: ``None`` means nobody recorded it - which is not the same as twelve.\n months_per_year: int | None = None\n\n @property\n def year_round(self) -> bool | None:\n \"\"\"Whether it works all year: True, False, or None when unrecorded.\"\"\"\n if self.months_per_year is None:\n return None\n return self.months_per_year >= 12\n\n @property\n def improved(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether the source is an improved type worth rehabilitating.\n\n A borehole, tubewell, protected well or spring, or a piped supply is\n an improved source; an unprotected well/spring or surface water is\n not, so it is not a rehabilitation alternative to a new borehole.\n\n The unimproved check runs first because \"unprotected\" contains\n \"protected\": a \"Protected Spring\" is improved, an \"Unprotected\n Spring\" is not, and both must resolve correctly.\n \"\"\"\n text = f\"{self.source} {self.technology}\".lower()\n unimproved = (\"unprotected\", \"unimproved\", \"open well\", \"open dug\",\n \"surface\", \"river\", \"stream\", \"pond\", \"rainwater\")\n if any(word in text for word in unimproved):\n return False\n improved = (\"borehole\", \"tubewell\", \"tube well\", \"protected\",\n \"piped\", \"hand pump\", \"handpump\", \"mechani\")\n return any(word in text for word in improved)\n\n def as_row(self) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Compact dict for a results table.\"\"\"\n state = (\"Functional\" if self.functional else \"Non-functional\"\n if self.functional is False else \"Unknown\")\n return {\n \"Distance (m)\": round(self.distance_m) if self.distance_m is not None\n else None,\n \"Status\": state,\n \"Source\": self.source or \"\",\n \"Technology\": self.technology or \"\",\n \"Installed\": self.install_year,\n }\n\n\ndef _haversine_m(lat1: float, lon1: float, lat2: float, lon2: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Great-circle distance in metres between two lat/lon points.\"\"\"\n p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n dphi = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)\n dlam = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n a = (math.sin(dphi / 2) ** 2\n + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dlam / 2) ** 2)\n return 2 * _EARTH_RADIUS_M * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))\n\n\ndef _first(record: dict, *keys: str):\n \"\"\"First present, non-empty value among ``keys`` (with '#'-prefixed twins).\"\"\"\n for key in keys:\n for variant in (key, \"#\" + key):\n if variant in record:\n value = record[variant]\n if value not in (None, \"\"):\n return value\n return None\n\n\ndef _to_float(value) -> float | None:\n try:\n return float(value)\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return None\n\n\ndef _to_int(value) -> int | None:\n try:\n return int(float(value))\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return None\n\n\ndef _year_of(value) -> int | None:\n \"\"\"The year out of a date as WPDx writes it, or ``None``.\n\n Exports carry ISO timestamps, ``dd/mm/yyyy`` and bare years depending on\n who assembled them, so the year is taken as the first four-digit number\n in a plausible range rather than by parsing a format that varies.\n \"\"\"\n text = str(value or \"\").strip()\n if not text:\n return None\n for match in re.findall(r\"\\d{4}\", text):\n year = int(match)\n if 1960 <= year <= 2100:\n return year\n return None\n\n\ndef _months_per_year(value) -> int | None:\n \"\"\"Months of the year a point yields water, or ``None`` when unrecorded.\n\n ``None`` is deliberately not twelve. Most surveys never asked, and\n reading silence as a year-round supply is how a dry-season coverage\n figure ends up matching the wet-season one.\n \"\"\"\n text = str(value or \"\").strip().lower()\n if not text:\n return None\n if text in (\"yes\", \"year round\", \"year-round\", \"all year\", \"permanent\"):\n return 12\n if text in (\"no\", \"seasonal\"):\n return None # says it is seasonal but not for how long\n match = re.search(r\"\\d+\", text)\n if not match:\n return None\n months = int(match.group(0))\n return months if 0 <= months <= 12 else None\n\n\ndef _functional_from(status_text: str, status_id) -> bool | None:\n \"\"\"Map WPDx status to functional True / False / None.\n\n ``status_clean`` text is authoritative when present (\"Functional\",\n \"Non-Functional\", \"Functional, needs repair\"); ``status_id`` (\"Yes\"/\"No\")\n is the fallback. A source that is functional but needs repair still\n delivers water, so it counts as functional.\n \"\"\"\n text = (status_text or \"\").strip().lower()\n if text:\n if \"non\" in text or \"not functional\" in text or \"abandoned\" in text:\n return False\n # match \"functional\" as a whole word, so \"functionality\" (used in\n # \"unknown functionality\") does not read as functional.\n if \"functional\" in re.findall(r\"[a-z]+\", text):\n return True\n sid = str(status_id or \"\").strip().lower()\n if sid in (\"yes\", \"y\", \"true\", \"1\"):\n return True\n if sid in (\"no\", \"n\", \"false\", \"0\"):\n return False\n return None\n\n\ndef parse_wpdx_records(records: Iterable[dict]) -> list[WaterPoint]:\n \"\"\"Parse raw WPDx JSON rows into :class:`WaterPoint` objects.\n\n Rows without a usable latitude/longitude are skipped rather than raising,\n so one malformed record does not lose the whole response.\n \"\"\"\n points: list[WaterPoint] = []\n for record in records:\n if not isinstance(record, dict):\n continue\n lat = _to_float(_first(record, \"lat_deg\", \"latitude\", \"lat\"))\n lon = _to_float(_first(record, \"lon_deg\", \"longitude\", \"lon\"))\n if lat is None or lon is None:\n continue\n status_text = str(_first(record, \"status_clean\", \"status\") or \"\")\n points.append(\n WaterPoint(\n row_id=str(_first(record, \"row_id\", \"wpdx_id\", \"objectid\") or \"\"),\n lat=lat,\n lon=lon,\n functional=_functional_from(\n status_text, _first(record, \"status_id\", \"status\")\n ),\n status=status_text,\n source=str(_first(record, \"water_source_clean\",\n \"water_source\", \"source\") or \"\"),\n technology=str(_first(record, \"water_tech_clean\",\n \"water_tech\", \"technology\") or \"\"),\n install_year=_to_int(_first(record, \"install_year\")),\n adm2=str(_first(record, \"clean_adm2\", \"adm2\") or \"\"),\n report_year=_year_of(_first(record, \"report_date\", \"date_of_record\",\n \"survey_date\", \"created_timestamp\")),\n months_per_year=_months_per_year(\n _first(record, \"months_year\", \"#months_year\",\n \"months_of_year\", \"water_point_seasonality\")),\n )\n )\n return points\n\n\ndef points_within(\n points: Iterable[WaterPoint], lat: float, lon: float, radius_m: float\n) -> list[WaterPoint]:\n \"\"\"Points within ``radius_m`` of (lat, lon), each stamped with its distance,\n sorted nearest first.\"\"\"\n out: list[WaterPoint] = []\n for point in points:\n distance = _haversine_m(lat, lon, point.lat, point.lon)\n if distance <= radius_m:\n out.append(replace(point, distance_m=distance))\n out.sort(key=lambda p: p.distance_m)\n return out\n\n\ndef functionality_summary(points: Iterable[WaterPoint]) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Counts and the functional rate for a set of water points.\"\"\"\n points = list(points)\n functional = sum(1 for p in points if p.functional is True)\n non_functional = sum(1 for p in points if p.functional is False)\n unknown = sum(1 for p in points if p.functional is None)\n reported = functional + non_functional\n return {\n \"total\": len(points),\n \"functional\": functional,\n \"non_functional\": non_functional,\n \"unknown\": unknown,\n \"functional_rate\": (functional / reported * 100.0) if reported else None,\n }\n\n\ndef rehab_vs_drill(\n points: Iterable[WaterPoint],\n lat: float,\n lon: float,\n *,\n search_radius_m: float = DEFAULT_SEARCH_RADIUS_M,\n service_radius_m: float = SERVICE_RADIUS_M,\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Turn nearby water points into a rehabilitate-or-drill recommendation.\n\n Logic, in priority order:\n\n * a *working improved* source inside the service radius -> the community\n may already be served; verify the need before drilling;\n * otherwise a *non-functional improved* source nearby -> a rehabilitation\n candidate, usually cheaper than a new borehole;\n * otherwise -> new construction is the reasonable option, noting the\n nearest working source if one exists beyond the service radius.\n \"\"\"\n nearby = points_within(points, lat, lon, search_radius_m)\n functional = [p for p in nearby if p.functional is True]\n non_functional_improved = [\n p for p in nearby if p.functional is False and p.improved\n ]\n served = [p for p in functional if p.improved\n and p.distance_m <= service_radius_m]\n\n summary = functionality_summary(nearby)\n common = {\n \"n_nearby\": len(nearby),\n \"search_radius_m\": search_radius_m,\n \"service_radius_m\": service_radius_m,\n \"summary\": summary,\n \"rehab_candidates\": [p.as_row() | {\"_distance\": p.distance_m}\n for p in non_functional_improved],\n }\n\n if served:\n nearest = served[0]\n return {\n **common,\n \"recommendation\": VERIFY_NEED,\n \"headline\": (\n f\"A working {nearest.source or 'improved source'} is already \"\n f\"{round(nearest.distance_m)} m away.\"\n ),\n \"rationale\": (\n \"An improved, functional source sits inside the \"\n f\"{round(service_radius_m)} m service radius, so the site may \"\n \"already be served. Confirm demand (population, queue times, \"\n \"dry-season reliability) before committing to a new borehole.\"\n ),\n }\n\n if non_functional_improved:\n nearest = non_functional_improved[0]\n return {\n **common,\n \"recommendation\": ASSESS_REHAB,\n \"headline\": (\n f\"A broken {nearest.source or 'improved source'} is \"\n f\"{round(nearest.distance_m)} m away - a rehabilitation \"\n \"candidate.\"\n ),\n \"rationale\": (\n \"A non-functional improved source is nearby. Rehabilitating an \"\n \"existing point is usually far cheaper than a new borehole; \"\n \"assess it (yield, cause of failure, spare parts) before \"\n \"drilling.\"\n ),\n }\n\n if not nearby:\n return {\n **common,\n \"recommendation\": DRILL_NEW,\n \"headline\": (\n f\"No mapped water point within {round(search_radius_m)} m.\"\n ),\n \"rationale\": (\n \"No existing water point is mapped near the site, so new \"\n \"construction is likely justified. Field-verify, since WPDx \"\n \"coverage is not exhaustive.\"\n ),\n }\n\n note = \"\"\n if functional:\n distance = functional[0].distance_m\n if distance > service_radius_m:\n note = (\n f\" The nearest working source is {round(distance)} m away, \"\n f\"beyond the {round(service_radius_m)} m service radius.\"\n )\n else:\n # inside the service radius but not an improved source, so it is\n # not a rehabilitation alternative to a borehole.\n note = (\n f\" The nearest working source is {round(distance)} m away but \"\n \"is not an improved source suitable for rehabilitation.\"\n )\n return {\n **common,\n \"recommendation\": DRILL_NEW,\n \"headline\": \"No rehabilitation candidate nearby.\" + note,\n \"rationale\": (\n \"Nearby points are either working but beyond the service radius or \"\n \"not improved sources, so there is no cheaper rehabilitation \"\n \"alternative. New construction is reasonable.\" + note\n ),\n }\n\n\ndef fetch_water_points(\n lat: float,\n lon: float,\n radius_m: float = DEFAULT_SEARCH_RADIUS_M,\n *,\n timeout: float = 20.0,\n limit: int = 5000,\n domain: str = WPDX_DOMAIN,\n resource: str = WPDX_RESOURCE,\n urlopen: Callable | None = None,\n) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Fetch raw WPDx rows in a bounding box around (lat, lon).\n\n A bounding-box query on the standard ``lat_deg``/``lon_deg`` columns is\n used (rather than a Socrata ``within_circle`` on a geo column) so the\n request does not depend on a particular geometry field name. Distance\n filtering to a true radius is done client-side by :func:`points_within`.\n\n Raises :class:`WaterPointFetchError` on any network, HTTP or decode\n failure; the caller (and the app) treats that as \"offline / unavailable\".\n \"\"\"\n opener = urlopen or urllib.request.urlopen\n # metres -> degrees; guard the cosine near the poles (irrelevant for\n # Sierra Leone but keeps the maths well-defined everywhere).\n dlat = radius_m / 111320.0\n dlon = radius_m / (111320.0 * max(math.cos(math.radians(lat)), 1e-6))\n where = (\n f\"lat_deg between {lat - dlat} and {lat + dlat} \"\n f\"AND lon_deg between {lon - dlon} and {lon + dlon}\"\n )\n # $order by the Socrata row id makes a capped result deterministic across\n # runs (a truncated slice is at least the same slice every time).\n query = urllib.parse.urlencode(\n {\"$where\": where, \"$limit\": int(limit), \"$order\": \":id\"}\n )\n url = f\"https://{domain}/resource/{resource}.json?{query}\"\n request = urllib.request.Request(\n url, headers={\"User-Agent\": \"groundwater-toolkit/waterpoints\"}\n )\n try:\n with opener(request, timeout=timeout) as response:\n payload = response.read()\n data = json.loads(payload)\n except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:\n raise WaterPointFetchError(\n f\"Could not reach the Water Point Data Exchange: {exc}\"\n ) from exc\n if not isinstance(data, list):\n raise WaterPointFetchError(\n \"Unexpected response from the Water Point Data Exchange \"\n \"(expected a list of records).\"\n )\n return data\n\n\ndef parse_wpdx_csv(text: str) -> list[WaterPoint]:\n \"\"\"Parse a WPDx CSV export into :class:`WaterPoint` records.\n\n A WPDx/Socrata CSV export uses the same column names as the JSON API\n (``lat_deg``, ``lon_deg``, ``status_clean``, ``water_source_clean`` ...),\n so the rows feed straight into :func:`parse_wpdx_records`. This is the\n fully offline input path - a user downloads their country's export and\n uploads it, no network required.\n \"\"\"\n # Excel's \"CSV UTF-8\" writes a byte order mark, which csv.DictReader keeps\n # on the first field name. When that field is lat_deg every row loses its\n # coordinates and the file parses to zero points - reported to the user as\n # \"no water points near this site\", the opposite of what the export says.\n return parse_wpdx_records(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text.lstrip(\"\ufeff\"))))\n\n\ndef water_points_near(\n lat: float,\n lon: float,\n radius_m: float = DEFAULT_SEARCH_RADIUS_M,\n **fetch_kwargs,\n) -> list[WaterPoint]:\n \"\"\"Fetch, parse and distance-filter water points near a site (one call).\n\n Convenience wrapper for the app; raises :class:`WaterPointFetchError` when\n the data cannot be fetched.\n \"\"\"\n raw = fetch_water_points(lat, lon, radius_m, **fetch_kwargs)\n return points_within(parse_wpdx_records(raw), lat, lon, radius_m)\n"},
